(p-٤٤٢٣) Sūrat al-Nūr

It is called by this name because it contains what is possible of the explanation of the Divine Light through illustration, which yields the perfection of knowledge attainable by mankind, together with its preliminaries; and this is among the greatest aims of the Qur'an. So said al-Mahāyimī. It is Medinan. Al-Qurṭubī said: the verse "O you who have believed, let your slaves ask permission of you..." [al-Nūr: 58] and so on is Meccan, and the surah has sixty-four verses.

(p-٤٤٢٤) In the name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful

Commentary on the words of the Exalted:

[1] ﴿A surah which We have sent down and made obligatory, and in which We have sent down clear verses, that you may remember.﴾

﴿A surah which We have sent down﴾: the predicate of an omitted subject, i.e., this is the surah. The indefiniteness is for magnification. ﴿And made obligatory﴾: i.e., We made obligatory the rulings it contains as a definitive obligation. ﴿And in which We have sent down clear verses, that you may remember﴾: i.e., that you may remember them and act according to what they require.

Imam Ibn Taymiyya, may God have mercy on him, said in explaining these verses: God made this surah obligatory with clear proofs, measures and limits; whoever transgresses its lawful into the unlawful has wronged himself, and whoever approaches its unlawful has exceeded and overstepped the limits. In it He made clear the obligation of the punishment, the verse of flogging, the obligation of testimony for adultery, and the obligation of the testimony of the two who engage in mutual cursing (li'ān), each of whom testifies four times by God. In it He forbade overstepping God's limits concerning private parts, honour and nakedness, and obeying the ruler, whether in his house or in his jurisdiction; one should not go out or come in except with his permission. For rights are of two kinds: a kind belonging to God, so one does not overstep His limits; and a kind belonging to the servants, in which there is a command, so one does not act except with the permission of the owner. Thus no one may do anything in the right of another except by God's permission. And if the owner does not grant permission, God's permission is the origin, and the owner's permission is valid where God has permitted it and given him authority over it. For this reason He included in it the seeking of permission for houses, for food, and in comprehensive matters such as prayer, jihad and the like. He placed in its midst the mention of light, which is the substance of every good and the soundness of everything; it arises from complying with God's command and avoiding His prohibition, and from patience in that. For it is illumination: guarding the limits through God-fearing piety gives its bearer light, as the Exalted said: ﴿Fear God and believe in His Messenger; He will give you a double portion of His mercy and make for you a light by which you walk﴾ [al-Ḥadīd: 28], and so on. The opposite of light is darkness; for this reason He followed the mention of light and the deeds of the believers with the deeds of the disbelievers and the people of innovation and misguidance. (p-٤٤٢٥) He said: ﴿And those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage﴾ [al-Nūr: 39], up to His saying: ﴿or like darkness in a deep sea, covered by a wave﴾ [al-Nūr: 40], and so likewise injustice is darkness on the Day of Resurrection. The wronging of a servant of himself is also a form of injustice; for a sin has darkness in the heart, blackness in the face, weakness in the body, deficiency in provision, and hatred in the hearts of creatures. This has been related from Ibn ʿAbbās. It is clarified by the fact that God struck the parable of the faith of the believers as light, and the deeds of the disbelievers as darkness. Faith is a comprehensive name for everything God loves, and disbelief is a comprehensive name for everything He hates; yet a servant does not become a disbeliever if the root of faith remains with him along with some branches of disbelief in the form of sins, just as he does not become a believer merely because some branches of faith are with him.

Lowering the gaze has a particular connection with light, as in the hadith of Abū Hurayra, which al-Tirmidhī declared authentic: "Indeed, when the servant commits a sin..." — the hadith — and in it: "That is the rān (rust) which God mentioned." And in the Ṣaḥīḥ: "Indeed, there is a veil (ghayn) over my heart, and indeed I seek God's forgiveness a hundred times a day." The ghayn is a thin veil, finer than cloud; so he informed that he seeks forgiveness to remove the ghayn, so that it does not become a black spot; and when it is removed it does not become rān. Ḥudhayfa said: Faith appears in the heart as a white spot; so whenever the servant's faith increases, his heart grows whiter. And in the sermon of Imam Aḥmad, in refutation of the heretics: "Praise be to God who in every age has placed a remnant of scholars from among the messengers' heirs, who call those who have gone astray to guidance and who bear harm from them with patience; by the Book of God they give life to the dead, and by the light of God they give sight to the people of blindness..." etc. God, glory be to Him, has coupled guidance and error with things similar to this, such as His saying: ﴿Nor are the blind and the seeing alike﴾ [Fāṭir: 19], ﴿nor the darknesses and the light﴾ [Fāṭir: 20]; and He said: ﴿The likeness of the two groups is like the blind and the deaf, and the seeing and the hearing﴾ [Hūd: 24]; and He said: ﴿Their likeness is like that of one who kindled a fire﴾ [al-Baqara: 17], and the verses. (p-٤٤٢٦) This light which the believer has in this world through his good deeds and sound belief appears in the Hereafter, as He said: ﴿Their light runs before them and on their right hands﴾ [al-Ḥadīd: 12], and so on. He mentioned the light here after His command to repentance, as in Sūrat al-Nūr after His command to lower the gaze and to repent; and He mentioned that after commanding the rights of the family and the spouses and what relates to women. In Sūrat al-Ḥadīd He said: ﴿The day you see the believing men and believing women...﴾ [al-Ḥadīd: 12] up to His saying: ﴿and wretched is the destination﴾ [al-Ḥadīd: 15]. Thus God, glory be to Him, informed that the hypocrites lose the light by which the believers walked and seek to borrow from their light, but they are kept from that by a veil set up between them, just as in this world, when they lost the light: ﴿like one who kindled a fire﴾ [al-Baqara: 17], and so on. And His saying, may He be exalted:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 24, verse 2 (part 1 of 2):

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:
[2] ﴿The adulterous woman and the adulterous man, flog each one of them with a hundred lashes. Let not pity for them overtake you in the religion of Allah, if you believe in Allah and the Last Day. And let a group of the believers witness their punishment.﴾

﴿The adulterous woman and the adulterous man, flog each one of them with a hundred lashes﴾ begins the detailing of what was mentioned of the clear verses and the explanation of their rulings. That is: every man and woman who commits adulture, apply this prescribed punishment (hadd) to him. It is that he be flogged, meaning he is struck on his skin a hundred lashes, as a punishment for what he did. ﴿Let not pity for them overtake you in the religion of Allah﴾, meaning: tenderness and mercy in obeying Him regarding what He has commanded you concerning applying the punishment to them, which He has obligated upon you. ﴿If you believe in Allah and the Last Day﴾, meaning: you affirm that Allah is your Lord and the Last Day, and that you will be resurrected for the gathering of the Resurrection and for reward and punishment. For whoever affirms this, he does not oppose Allah in His command and prohibition, out of fear of His punishment for His disobedience. ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾ (p. 4427), meaning: let a group of the people of faith in Allah and His Messenger attend their flogging. Ibn Jarir said: The Arabs call one or more a group (ta'ifa).

Ibn Taymiyya, may Allah have mercy on him, said: So Allah, exalted is He, commanded that their punishment be carried out in the presence of a group of the believers. This is either by his own confession against himself, or by the testimony of the believers against him. Because when a sin becomes apparent, its punishment is to be apparent, as in the report: "Whoever commits a sin in secret, let him repent in secret, and whoever commits a sin openly, let him repent openly." And this is not from the concealment that Allah loves, as in the hadith: "Indeed, when a sin is concealed, it harms only its doer. But when it is announced and not denounced, it harms the public." So when it is announced, its punishment is announced according to possible justice. For this reason, there is no backbiting (ghiba) for one who openly displays innovations (bid'a) and immorality, as was narrated from al-Hasan and others, because when he announced it, he deserved punishment. The least of it is that he be censured for it so that he may be restrained and people may keep away from him and from associating with him. And if he were mentioned only by what is in him, people would be deceived by him. But when he is mentioned, he refrains and others refrain from that and from his company. Al-Hasan said: Do you shrink from mentioning the sinner? Mention him by what is in him so that people may beware of him. And "al-fujur" (immorality) is a comprehensive term for every person who openly displays a sin or foul speech, which indicates to the listener the corruption of the heart of the one who speaks it. For this reason he deserves to be shunned (hijra) when he openly displays innovation or sin, or immorality, or shamelessness, or association with one of such a state. By this, he does not care about people's criticism of him, for shunning him is a form of discipline (ta'zir) for him. So when he openly displays evil deeds, his shunning is openly announced, and when he conceals them, his shunning is kept secret, since shunning (al-hijra) is shunning over evil deeds and shunning the evil deeds, as in His saying: ﴿And the abomination, abandon﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 5], and His saying: ﴿And forsake them with a gracious forsaking﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 10], and His saying: ﴿So do not sit with them until they engage in a conversation other than this. Indeed, you would then be like them﴾ [an-Nisa: 140]. It was narrated from Umar that when his son Abd al-Rahman drank wine in Egypt, and his brother took him to its governor Amr ibn al-As so that he might apply the prescribed punishment to him, he flogged him in secret. Umar sent to him, rebuking him for it. He did not consider that sufficient until he sent for his son, brought him to Madina, and flogged him openly. His son lived for a period, then fell ill and died, and he did not die from the flogging, nor was he struck after death, as the liars claim.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Let not pity for them overtake you in the religion of Allah﴾ forbids what Satan commands regarding punishments in general and regarding immoral acts in particular. For this matter is founded upon love and desire, and the pity that Satan adorns through the inclination of hearts toward the people of immorality, so that many people, because of this affliction, fall into being a cuckold (dayyuth) when he sees one whom he loves among those attached to him, or one who associates with him in a reprehensible way even if it is his own son, he feels tender toward him and thinks this is from the mercy of creation. But that is only cuckoldry, abasement, lack of religion, and helping one another in sin and transgression. And it is abandoned for the sake of forbidding evil. And the soul enters through it into pimping (qiyada), which is greater than cuckoldry, just as the wicked old woman entered among her people, in approving of what they were engaged in of approaching males and assisting them in that. She was outwardly a Muslim on the religion of her husband Lut, but inwardly a hypocrite on the religion of her people, not disliking their deed as Lut disliked it.

And as the women did with Yusuf. For they helped the wife of the ruler (al-Aziz) in what she invited him to, the commission of immorality with her. For this reason he said: ﴿My Lord, the prison is dearer to me than that to which they invite me﴾ [Yusuf: 33], after their saying: ﴿Indeed, we see her in clear error﴾ [Yusuf: 30]. There is no doubt that love of immoral acts is a sickness of the heart. For desire necessitates intoxication, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, they are in their intoxication, wandering blindly﴾ [al-Hijr: 72]. And in the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Abu Hurayra: "The two eyes commit adultery," etc. So many people's aim is some of these types, such as looking, enjoyment, and conversation. And among them is one who advances to touching and physical contact. And among them is one who kisses and looks. And all of that is forbidden.

Allah, glorified is He, has forbidden us to be overtaken by pity for adulterers, rather we apply the punishment upon them. So how about what is less than it, such as shunning, forbidding, (p. 4429) rebuke, and other things? Rather, one should feel hatred and aversion toward the transgressors, regarding the kinds of adultery mentioned in the hadith through which a person enjoys [sin]. As for the lover, although he loves to look at and enjoy the image and speech of the beloved, his cure is not in that, for he is sick. And the sick person, if he desires what harms him, or recoils from taking the bitter medicine, and pity overtakes us regarding him, then we have helped him in what destroys and harms him. And Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, prayer forbids immorality and wrongdoing﴾ [al-Ankabut: 45], meaning: in it is the healing and cure from that. Rather, true pity for him is that he be helped to drink the medicine even if it is bitter, such as prayer and what it contains of remembrances and supplications, and that he be protected from what increases his illness. And it should not be thought that when he enjoys what is forbidden, his affliction is calmed. Rather, that necessitates for him an increase in the affliction. For although what is in him calms after his enjoyment, that results in a grave sickness from which he cannot be freed. Rather, what is obligatory is to repel the greater of the two harms by bearing the lesser of them before the disease becomes entrenched.

It is well known that the pain of beneficial treatment is less than the pain of a lasting sickness. By this it becomes clear that the legal punishments are beneficial medicines, and they are part of Allah's mercy to His servants, which is included in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds﴾ [al-Anbiya: 107]. So whoever abandons this beneficial mercy out of pity for the patient, it is he who has helped in his punishment, even if he intends only good, for he is ignorant and foolish in that, as some women do with their sick ones and with the children they raise, by abandoning their discipline for what they do of evil and abandon of good.

Among people there is one whom pity overtakes concerning them because he shares with them in that sickness, coldness of heart, and cuckoldry. And he, in that, is among the most unjust of people and the most wicked toward his own soul and its like. He is like a group of sick people for whom a physician has prescribed what benefits them, but their elder found it bitter, so he left drinking it. He also prohibited giving it to the rest. And among them is one whom pity overtakes because one of the two adulterers is beloved to him, either due to kinship, affection, or kindness, or because of what he hopes from him, or because of the pain in the punishment which necessitates tenderness of heart. He interprets the hadith: "Allah has mercy only upon those of His servants (p. 4430) who are merciful," and it is not as he said. Rather, that is placing a thing in other than its proper place. Indeed, it has been reported: "A cuckold will not enter Paradise." So whoever is not hateful toward immoral acts, averse to them and to their people, and does not become angry upon seeing or hearing them, he does not desire punishment for them. Thus the punishment for them causes pain in his heart. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Let not pity for them overtake you in the religion of Allah﴾, the verse. "In the religion of Allah" is obedience to Him and to His Messenger, which is founded upon love for Him and love for His Messenger, and that Allah and His Messenger be dearer to him than all else. For pity and mercy, he loves them for the sake of Allah as long as they are not a waste of the religion of Allah.

So mercy is commanded, unlike pity in the religion of Allah. And Satan wants from the human being excess in all his affairs. For if he sees him inclined toward mercy, he adorns mercy for him until he no longer hates what Allah hates, nor is zealous. And if he sees him inclined toward severity, he adorns severity for him in what is not for the sake of Allah, so he increases in blame, hatred, and punishment beyond what Allah loves. And he abandons the gentleness, kinship, kindness, and righteousness which Allah commands. So the first is a sinner and the second is an extravagant one. Let them both say together: ﴿Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our excess in our affair﴾ [Al 'Imran: 147], the verse.

And His saying: ﴿If you believe in Allah and the Last Day﴾: the believer in that does what Allah loves and forbids what Allah hates. But whoever does not believe in Allah and the Last Day follows his desire, so at times severity overcomes him, and at times looking and physical contact, even if some of it is minor sin (lamam). The persistence in that and what is connected with it, of association and physical contact, may be far greater than the corruption of an adultery without persistence. Indeed, looking and physical contact may lead a man to shirk. As Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And among the people are those who take other than Allah as equals, loving them as they love Allah﴾ [al-Baqara: 165], the verse. For this reason, the love of images arises only from weakness of love for Allah and weakness of faith. And Allah, exalted is He, mentioned it only regarding the wife of the ruler (p. 4431), who was a polytheist, and regarding the people of Lut. And the Prophet ﷺ gathered the prescribed punishments in what Abu Dawud narrated from the hadith of Ibn Umar: "Whoever intercession prevents a punishment from among the punishments of Allah, has opposed Allah in His command. Whoever disputes in falsehood, knowing it, will remain in the wrath of Allah until he desists. And whoever says about a Muslim what is not in him, will be detained in Radghat al-Khabal until he comes out of what he said." So the intercessor in the prescribed punishments opposes Allah in His command. Therefore it is not permissible that pity overtake the believer regarding the people of innovation, immorality, and sins. And the summary of all this is His saying: ﴿Humble toward the believers, mighty against the disbelievers﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 54], and His saying: ﴿Severe against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves﴾ [al-Fath: 29]. For all these major sins are branches of disbelief, as in the authentic collections: "An adulterer does not commit adultery while he is a believer," etc. So among them there is a deficiency of faith that necessitates the removal of pity for them. And there is no contradiction between one person being loved from one aspect and hated from another, rewarded from one aspect and punished from another. This is contrary to the Kharijites and the Mu'tazila. For this reason it came in the Sunna that the one upon whom the prescribed punishment is applied is shown mercy from another aspect, so he is treated kindly and prayed for.

And this aspect predominates in the Shari'a, as in the attributes of the Lord, glorified is He and exalted.

For in the Sahih: "Indeed My mercy overcomes My wrath." And He said: ﴿Inform My servants that I am the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ [al-Hijr: 49], ﴿and that My punishment is the painful punishment﴾ [al-Hijr: 50]. And He said: ﴿Know that Allah is severe in punishment (p. 4432) and that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 98]. So He made mercy an attribute mentioned among His names. As for punishment and retribution, He made them among His acts. And from this is what Allah, exalted is He, commanded regarding harshness toward the disbelievers and the hypocrites.

And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those of your women who commit immorality, bring against them four witnesses from among you﴾ [an-Nisa': 15], and so on. In the hadith is an explanation of the way (sabil) that Allah made for them: for a virgin (bikr), one hundred lashes and a year's exile (taghrib); for a married person (thayyib), stoning (rajm). However, what is in the hadith is lashing and exile for the virgin among men, whereas the verse mentions confinement of women in their houses until death, and the way (sabil) is specific to women. Among the jurists (fuqaha') are those who do not require exile along with the prescribed punishment (hadd), and among them are those who distinguish between man and woman. Likewise, most of them do not require lashing along with stoning. And among them are those who require both together, as was done to Sharrahah al-Hamdaniyyah, when he lashed her and then stoned her, and he said: "I lashed her by the Book of Allah and I stoned her by the Sunnah of His Prophet." Related by al-Bukhari.

Allah, glorified is He, mentioned in Surat an-Nisa' the punishment specific to them. Then He mentioned what applies to both categories, saying: ﴿And the two of you who commit it, harm them; but if they repent and amend, leave them alone. Indeed, Allah is ever Accepting of repentance, Merciful﴾ [an-Nisa': 16]. The harm (adha) encompasses both categories. As for confinement (imsak), it is specific to women, because a woman must be protected by what is not required of men in the same measure, and for this reason she was singled out for veiling (ihtijab), abandoning adornment, and abandoning display (tabarruj), because her exposure causes temptation (fitnah), and "men are the protectors (qawwamun) over women."

His saying: ﴿Then call four witnesses against them from among you﴾ [an-Nisa': 15] indicates two things: the quorum of testimony (nisab al-shahadah), and that the witnesses against our women are from among us. There is no dispute about this.

As for the testimony of disbelievers against one another, there are two reports from Ahmad. The second is that it is accepted. Abu al-Khattab chose this, and it is the view of Abu Hanifah. It is more consistent with the Book and the Sunnah.

As for his saying (ﷺ): "The testimony of people of one religion is not valid against people of another religion, except my community," its implication is the validity of the testimony of people of one religion against one another. But in it there is: that the believers' testimony is accepted against others, due to His saying: ﴿that you may be witnesses over mankind﴾ [al-Baqarah: 143]. In the end of al-Hajj there is a similar verse. In al-Bukhari, from the hadith of Abu Sa'id: "Nuh will be called..." (the hadith). Likewise in both of them, from the hadith of Anas, regarding their testimony over the two funerals, good and bad, he said: "You are the witnesses of Allah on His earth" (the hadith). For this reason, when the people of the Sunnah and the Jama'ah (Ahl al-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah) did not mix Islam with anything else, their testimony was accepted over all the sects of the Ummah, unlike the people of innovation (ahl al-bid'ah) and desires, such as the Khawarij and the Rafidah, for among them is enmity and injustice that removes them from this reality which Allah made for the people of the Sunnah. He said about them: "From every generation, its upright ones will carry this knowledge; they will remove from it the distortion of the extremists, the false claims of the falsifiers, and the misinterpretation of the ignorant."

Those who permitted the testimony of the protected people (ahl al-dhimmah) against one another used this verse: ﴿O you who have believed, testimony among you﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 106], to the end of the verse. They said: it indicates the acceptance of their testimony against Muslims. Therefore, it contains an alert to the acceptance of the testimony of some of them against others by way of priority (bi-tariq al-awla). Then, abrogation (naskh) of the apparent ruling does not necessitate abrogation of the implication (fahwa), and the alert to the stronger (al-aqwa). As Ahmad and other imams of hadith who agreed with the early predecessors (al-salaf) explicitly stated. For this reason, in testimony, what is not permitted in other matters is permitted out of necessity (li-l-darurah). Just as the testimony of women is accepted regarding what men do not witness. Ahmad even explicitly stated the acceptance of the testimony of two women in the hudud that occur in their private gatherings. (p-4434) So the disbelievers with whom Muslims do not mix are more deserving of this, and Allah commanded us to judge between them, and the Prophet (ﷺ) stoned the two Jewish adulterers, without hearing a confession from them and without the testimony of a Muslim. Had the testimony of some of them against others not been accepted, that would not have been permissible.

Regarding the guardianship (tawalli) of some of them over the property of others, there is a dispute: does a disbelieving upright person in his religion inherit the property of his disbelieving child? There are two opinions. The definitively correct view is that some of them have priority over others, and the Sunnah has passed on this, and the Sunnah of his caliphs.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[24:3] ﴿The adulterer does not marry except an adulterous woman or a polytheist, and the adulteress is not married except by an adulterer or a polytheist, and that has been forbidden to the believers.﴾

[p. 4443] ﴿The adulterer does not marry except an adulterous woman or a polytheist, and the adulteress is not married except by an adulterer or a polytheist, and that has been forbidden to the believers.﴾ When Allah commanded the punishment of the two adulterers, He forbade the believers from marrying them, as a way of shunning them and what they carry of sins. This is like His saying: ﴿And the abomination, shun it﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 5]. The one who keeps company with the doer of that evil is treated like him, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, you would then be like them﴾ [an-Nisa': 140]. The spouse is a companion to him, as Exalted Allah said: ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their spouses﴾ [as-Saffat: 22], meaning their companions and their like. For this reason it is said: "The listener is a partner of the one who backbites." 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz was informed of a group who drank wine, and among them was a companion of theirs who was fasting. He said: "Begin with him in the flogging. Has he not heard the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿So do not sit with them﴾ [an-Nisa': 140]?" If this applies to sitting together and to the passing association at the time they commit the evil, then their companion is like them. How much more so, then, is the lasting companionship? The husband is called al-'ashir (the close companion), as in the hadith: "and they disbelieve in the companion (al-'ashir)." He was informed that he does not do this except an adulterer or a polytheist. As for the polytheist, he has no faith that restrains him from indecency and from intercourse with its people. As for the adulterer, his immorality calls him to that, even if he is not a polytheist. In this there is evidence that the adulterer is not a believer in an absolute sense, even if he is not a polytheist, as in the Sahih: "An adulterer does not commit adultery while he is a believer." This is because He informed that he does not marry an adulteress except an adulterer or a polytheist. Then He said: ﴿and that has been forbidden to the believers﴾, so it is known that faith prevents this, and that its doer is either a polytheist or an adulterer, not among the believers whose faith restrains them from that. This is because fornication involves corrupting a man's marital bed, and marrying her involves lasting association with a wicked woman. Allah has commanded the shunning of evil and its people as long as they persist in it, and this is found in the adulterer. If he does not corrupt the bed of his wife, he is still a bad companion to her, as al-Sha'bi said: "Whoever marries his noble daughter to a corrupt man has severed her kinship." This is among what brings harm to the woman in her religion and her worldly life. So marrying an adulteress is worse in respect of the bed, and marrying an adulterer is worse in that he is the master, the owner, the ruler. Thus the free, chaste woman remains in the captivity of the wicked adulterer, who falls short in her rights and transgresses against her. For this reason, the scholars agreed on considering kafa'ah (equality of standing) in religion, and on (p. 4444) the validity of faskh (annulment) when this equality is lost. They differed over the validity of the marriage without it. Whoever marries an adulteress has consented for himself to pimping and cuckoldry. Whoever is married by an adulterer, he does not preserve his semen; rather he places it in her and in other prostitutes. She is in the position of one who takes a lover. The purpose of marriage is the preservation of semen in the woman, and this man does not preserve his semen. Allah, glorified is He, stipulated for men that they be muhsinin (chaste, protected), not musafihin (fornicators), saying: ﴿And lawful for you is what lies beyond that, that you seek with your wealth, being chaste, not fornicating﴾ [an-Nisa': 24]. This is something that must not be neglected, for the Qur'an has detailed it and clarified it with an obligatory clarity, as He said: ﴿A surah which We have sent down and made obligatory﴾ [an-Nur: 1]. As for the prohibition of marrying an adulteress, the jurists have discussed it, and there are reports from the early generations concerning it. Whoever permitted it has nothing reliable to rely on. Some have claimed that it was abrogated by His saying: ﴿And chaste women from among the women, except those whom your right hands possess﴾ [an-Nisa': 24], and they claimed that the prostitute is among the muhsanat (chaste women). That is a proof against them, for the least of what ihsan (chastity) entails is 'iffah (abstinence). When freedom is stipulated for it, that is a completion of 'iffah and ihsan. As for the one who forbids marrying a slave woman lest his child become a slave, how then does he permit a prostitute, to whom is attached one who is not his child? Where is the corruption of his bed in comparison with the enslavement of his child? Likewise, whoever claims that marriage here means intercourse, this is also a proof against them. Whoever has intercourse with an adulteress or a polytheist by marriage is an adulterer, and likewise whoever has intercourse with her is an adulterer. The adulterer is blamed for his act, which is zina. Even if she is forced, or if she draws his penis into herself while he is asleep, the punishment falls upon the adulterer and not his partner. The point is that the verse indicates that the adulterer does not marry except an adulteress or a polytheist, and that this is forbidden to the believers. This is not merely because he is a wicked person, but because of the specific nature of him being an adulterer. The same applies to the woman: it is not merely because of her immorality, but because of the specific nature of her fornication. The evidence is that He made the woman an adulteress if she marries an adulterer, just as He made him an adulterer if he marries an adulteress. This applies when both are Muslims who believe in the prohibition of fornication. But if they are polytheists, then it should be known. Its meaning is that an adulterer may not be married off until he repents. This accords with the stipulation of ihsan, and an adulterous woman does not protect her private part. For this reason it is obligatory for him to disown a child that is not his. Whoever marries an adulteress (p. 4445) is himself an adulterer, that is, he married her. Whoever marries an adulterer is an adulteress, that is, she married him. Many adulterers restrict themselves to adulteresses, so she becomes his lover who does not come to anyone else. When a man is an adulterer, he does not keep his wife chaste, so she longs for another and commits adultery, as is the usual case with the wives of adulterers and of those who commit sodomy with boys. Their wives commit adultery to satisfy their desires and to spite their husbands. For this reason it is said: "Be chaste, and your women will be chaste. Be dutiful to your fathers, and your sons will be dutiful to you." As you judge, so you will be judged; the recompense is of the same kind as the deed, and the punishment for an evil deed is an evil deed after it. When a man agrees to marry an adulteress, he agrees to let his wife commit adultery. Allah, glorified is He, has placed between the spouses affection and mercy, so each loves for the other what he loves for himself. When the woman agrees to marry an adulterer, she has agreed to his act, and likewise the man. Whoever is pleased with fornication is in the position of the adulterer, for the root of the act is the will. For this reason there is a report: "Whoever is absent from a sin and is pleased with it is like one who witnessed it." And in the hadith: "A person is upon the religion of his close friend." The greatest closeness is the closeness of the spouses. Furthermore, Allah, exalted is He, placed in the souls of the children of Adam a jealousy which is well known. A man regards it as far more grave that another man should have intercourse with his wife than that he himself should commit adultery. So if he does not dislike that his wife be a prostitute while he is a dayyuth (cuckold), how can he dislike being an adulterer himself? For this reason, no one has been found who is a dayyuth or a qawwad (pimp) and yet is abstinent from fornication, for fornication has a desire in his own self, while the dayyuth has a desire in the fornication of another. If he has no faith that makes him dislike this from his wife, how could he have faith that prevents him from fornication? Whoever considers it permissible to leave his wife to commit adultery has permitted the greatest adultery. Whoever helps in that is like the adulterer. Whoever approves of it, while it is possible to change it, has consented to it. Whoever marries an unrepentant woman has consented to her committing adultery, since he cannot prevent her, for indeed their guile is great. For this reason, if she comes with a manifest indecency, it is permissible for him to restrain her (ya'dulaha) so that she ransoms herself. This is because by her adultery she has sought khul' (divorce by compensation) from him and has exposed his marriage to corruption. It is not possible for him to remain with her until she repents. And the dower does not fall away merely by her adultery, as is shown by the saying of the Prophet ﷺ to the one engaged in li'an, when he said: "My wealth," he said: "You have no wealth with her (p. 4446) if you are truthful, for it is in return for what you made lawful from her private part. And if you are lying about her, then that is further and further away from you, because if she commits adultery she may repent." However, her adultery permits restraining her until she ransoms herself if she chooses separation from him, or until she repents. In most cases, a man does not commit adultery with other than his wife unless that other woman pleases him. He keeps pursuing what pleases him, so his wife remains in the position of one left hanging, neither a widow nor a married woman. This leads her to commit adultery, and her motive is to match her husband as a form of retaliation. If he is among those who transgress, he has not guarded himself chastely. Furthermore, the call of the adulterer occupies itself with whatever prostitutes he chooses, so his call to lawful relations does not remain complete, nor is his jealousy sufficient to keep the woman chaste. Thus she becomes to him like the adulteress who takes a lover. These are noble meanings that must not be neglected. On this basis, a woman who engages in lesbianism is an adulteress, as in the hadith: "The fornication of women is their sihaq (lesbianism)." And the one who does the deed of the people of Lut is an adulterer, so he marries none but an adulteress or a polytheist. For this reason, many of the wives of the sodomite commit adultery, and perhaps she commits adultery with one who sodomizes him, to spite him and satisfy her desire. Likewise, the woman married to a mukhannath (effeminate man) who is married as a woman is married, is married to an adulterer, indeed he is the worse of the two in condition. For along with his fornication he has become cursed upon himself by effeminacy, apart from the curse that falls upon him for the deed of the people of Lut. The Prophet ﷺ cursed whoever does the deed of the people of Lut. In the Sahih it is reported that he cursed effeminate men among men and masculine women among women. How is it permissible for her to marry an effeminate man whose desire has shifted to his rear? He is penetrated as a woman is penetrated, and his desire for what is in front of him weakens, just as the desire of the adulterer for other than his wife weakens toward it. If he has no jealousy for himself, his jealousy for his wife and others is weakened. For this reason, one who is effeminate is found to have little jealousy for his child, his slave, or the one he is responsible for. If a woman is content with an effeminate man or a sodomite, she follows his religion, so she is an adulteress, and more so. For a woman's yielding of herself is easier than a man's yielding of himself. So if she is content with that from her husband, she is content with it from herself.

(p. 4447) The wording of the verse: ﴿The adulterer does not marry except an adulteress or a polytheist, and the adulteress is not married except by an adulterer or a polytheist﴾ encompasses all of this either by the generality of the wording or by way of alerting (tanbih), and by the implication of the address (fahwa al-khitab), which is stronger than the explicit meaning of the wording. And less than that is by way of analogy (qiyas), as we have explained in the hadd (prescribed punishment) for the sodomite and others. The words of Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, end here. All of this supports what Imam Ahmad held: that a contract by a chaste man with a prostitute woman is not valid as long as she remains so; if she repents, the contract with her is valid, otherwise it is not. Likewise, marrying a free, chaste woman to a wicked fornicator who persists in it is not valid until he repents a sincere repentance, because of His saying: ﴿and that has been forbidden to the believers﴾, as Taqi al-Din preferred.

Al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir has narrated here reports, both attributed to the Prophet and recorded as sayings of the Companions, all of which reinforce this. Then he said after them: As for the hadith that al-Nasa'i narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: 'I have a wife who is among the dearest of people to me, but she does not turn away the hand of one who touches her.' He said: 'Divorce her.' He said: 'I cannot bear to be parted from her.' He said: 'Then enjoy her.'" Al-Nasa'i said: this hadith is not authentic (ghayr thabit). 'Abd al-Karim, one of its narrators, is weak in hadith and not strong. Imam Ahmad said: it is a munkar hadith (a hadith rejected for its weakness). Ibn Qutaybah said: he only meant that she is generous and does not refuse a beggar. Al-Nasa'i related this in his Sunan from some of them, saying: "It was also said: she is generous and gives." This was refuted on the ground that if this were the meaning he would have said: "She does not refuse the hand of one who seeks." It was also said: the meaning is that her disposition (sajiyyah) does not turn away the hand of one who touches, not that this actually happens from her and that she commits lewdness. For the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would not permit companionship with one who has this description, since her husband in such a state would be a dayyuth (a man who tolerates indecency in his household), and the threat against that has already been mentioned. But since her disposition is such that there is no resistance or opposition in her to whoever desires her if someone were alone with her, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered her separation. Then, when he mentioned that he loves her, he permitted him to remain with her, because his love for her is certain, while the commission of lewdness by her is merely presumed; so one does not resort to a present, certain harm on account of a future, presumed one. And Allah knows best. End.

(p-4448) A subtle point: The reason for placing "the adulterous woman" (al-zaniyah) first in the first verse and "the adulterer" (al-zani) in the second is that the first concerns the ruling on fornication, and its origin lies with the woman because of the enticement and allurement that appear from her. The second concerns marriage to fornicators when that occurs in valid form. The origin in marriage is the men, who initiate the proposal, so it was attributed only to them. For this reason, although the purpose of the verse is to deter chaste men and women from marrying fornicators, male and female, as a deterrence from indecency, it joined fornication with polytheism. Accordingly Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, disliked marrying those known for indecency. His companions transmitted a consensus within the school that the woman, or whichever of her guardians stands in for her, has the right to annul the marriage of a wicked person (fasiq). Malik was the furthest of people from considering equality (kafa'ah) except in religion. As for lineage, it reached him that they distinguished between an Arab and a mawla (non-Arab client), so he considered this grave and recited: "O mankind, indeed We created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you" [al-Hujurat: 13]. End of the words of al-Nasir in al-Insif. What the early scholars meant by "disliked" is what is known as disliked in the sense of prohibition (karahah tahrimiyyah). Thus the position of the Malikis comes close to this.

Then He, Exalted is He, explained the ruling for flogging the slanderer of the chaste woman (muhsanah), who is the free, adult, chaste woman, with His saying, glory be to Him and exalted is He:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 24, verses 4–5 (part 1 of 2):

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:
[4–5] ﴿And those who accuse chaste women and then do not produce four witnesses, lash them eighty lashes, and never accept their testimony, and those are the defiantly disobedient (al-fasiqun)﴾ ﴿Except those who repent after that and reform. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Nur: 5].

﴿Those who accuse﴾ meaning: those who slander with fornication (zina). ﴿Chaste women﴾ meaning: Muslim, free, sane, adult women who are chaste, (p-4449) guarding themselves against fornication. ﴿Then do not produce four witnesses﴾ meaning: who testify to what they accused them of. ﴿Lash them eighty lashes﴾ meaning: each one of the accusers. The specification of women is due to the particular occurrence (of the incident), and because slander against them is more common and more heinous; otherwise, there is no difference in this between males and females. ﴿And never accept their testimony﴾ meaning: in any matter whatsoever, because their lying is evident. ﴿And those are the defiantly disobedient﴾ meaning: because they have departed from what was obligatory upon them, namely safeguarding the rights of chaste women. ﴿Except those who repent after that﴾ [al-Nur: 5] meaning: after the slander. ﴿And reform﴾ [al-Nur: 5] meaning: their deeds. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Nur: 5] meaning: by accepting their repentance and pardoning them.

Remarks:

First: Ibn Taymiyya said: He, exalted is He, mentioned the number of witnesses and left their description unrestricted; He did not qualify them as "from among us," nor "whom we approve of," nor "of those possessing justice." Therefore, scholars have disputed: Does the testimony of four who are not (themselves) of upright character, such as the testimony of people of wickedness, avert the hadd (prescribed punishment) from the slanderer? There are two opinions. One holds that it averts it, like the testimony of a husband against his wife four times: it averts the hadd of slander, but does not impose the hadd on the woman. If the woman does not testify, is she then subjected to the hadd, or is she detained until she confesses or performs li'an (mutual imprecation), or is her path left free? On this there is dispute. Therefore, it does not follow from averting the hadd from the slanderer that the hadd of zina is obligatory, for both are hudud. And the hudud are averted by doubts (shubuhat). The four testimonies for the slanderer constitute a strong doubt. Even if the one slandered confessed once, twice, or three times, the hadd is averted from the slanderer, and it is not obligatory upon him according to most scholars. Even if the one slandered was not muhsan, such as one who is well known for indecency, his slanderer is not punished with the hadd of slander, and he himself is not subjected to the hadd of zina merely by public reputation (istifada), though each of them is punished with a discretionary penalty short of the hadd. The hadd of zina is not established against a Muslim except by the testimony of Muslim witnesses. However, it is said: He did not restrict them with justice ('adala), yet Allah has commanded us to bear testimony that is needed from people of justice and approval, and they are those who comply with what Allah has commanded in His words: ﴿Be steadfast in upholding justice﴾ [al-Nisa': 135], His words: ﴿And when you speak, be just, even if it concerns a near relative﴾ [al-An'am: 152], His words: ﴿And do not conceal testimony﴾ [al-Baqara: 283], His words: ﴿And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called﴾ [al-Baqara: 282], and His words: ﴿And those who are upright in their testimonies﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 33]. So they establish it with justice for Allah, and thus the purpose of the one who sought their testimony is achieved.

The second aspect: their testimony is accepted because they are people of justice and approval. This indicates that it is obligatory to accept it and to give it. Allah, glorified is He, has forbidden accepting the testimony of a defiantly disobedient person in His words: ﴿If a defiantly disobedient person brings you a report, verify it﴾ [al-Hujurat: 6]. However, this is explicit that the report of a single defiant person must be verified. As for two or more defiant persons, the evidence for it requires another premise. What he mentioned regarding the number of witnesses is not fixed in judgment by the consensus of scholars in several cases. According to the majority, judgment is made without witnesses in several cases, such as when the party refuses (nukul) or makes a return of oath (radd), and the like.

We judge by one witness and an oath, as the Sunnah has established. What indicates this is that Allah did not stipulate this condition at the time of giving testimony, neither in the verse on zina nor in the verse on slander. Rather, He said: ﴿Call upon four of your men to testify against them﴾ [al-Nisa': 15]. He only commanded verification regarding the report of a single defiant person, and did not command it regarding the report of two defiant persons. The report of two persons produces a belief that the report of one person does not produce. Therefore, the scholars have said: If the judge doubts the witnesses, he separates them and questions them about what reveals their agreement and disagreement. End of quote.

Second: The Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in al-Fath: The majority hold that the testimony of one who slandered is accepted after repentance, and the designation of defiance (fisq) is removed from him, whether this occurs after the hadd is applied or before it, based on His words: ﴿except those who repent﴾ [al-Nur: 5]. Al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding this verse: Whoever repents, his testimony is accepted in the Book of Allah. They interpreted His words ﴿never﴾ to mean as long as he persists in his slander, because the "never" of anything is according to what befits it, just as if it were said: The testimony of a disbeliever is never accepted, meaning as long as he persists in disbelief. Al-Sha'bi went further, saying: If the slanderer repents before the hadd is applied to him, it is dropped from him. The Hanafis held (p-4451) that the exception relates only to defiance; when he repents, the designation of defiance is dropped from him, but his testimony is never accepted. Some of the Successors (tabi'un) said this as well. End of quote.

Al-Zamakhshari said: What the apparent meaning and arrangement of the verse require is that the three clauses together constitute the response of the condition, as if it were said: Whoever slanders chaste women, lash them, reject their testimony, and label them defiant. That is, combine for them the lashing, the rejection, and the labeling as defiant, except those who repent of the slander and reform, for Allah will forgive them, so they become neither lashed, nor rejected, nor labeled defiant. End of quote.

Al-Bukhari recorded in his Sahih, in the Book of Testimonies, in the chapter on the testimony of the slanderer, the thief, and the fornicator, from 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, that he lashed Abu Bakra, Shibl ibn Ma'bad, and Nafi', for slandering al-Mughira with zina, when they testified that they saw him between the legs of the woman (mutabattin al-mar'a). Ziyad did not give a definitive testimony. Then he asked them to repent and said: Whoever repents, I will accept his testimony. In another narration he said to them: Whoever retracts his statement, I will accept his testimony concerning what is to come; and whoever does not do so, I will not permit his testimony. Shibl and Nafi' retracted their statements, but Abu Bakra refused to retract.

Al-Muhallab said: It is inferred from this that retracting one's accusation is not a condition for the acceptance of his repentance, because Abu Bakra did not deny his statement, and yet the Muslims accepted his narration and acted upon it.

Third: Al-Razi said: They differed over how repentance from slander is to be done.

Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Repentance from it is retracting one's own statement. His companions differed over its meaning. Al-Istakhri said: He says, "I lied in what I said, and I will not return to the like of it." Abu Ishaq said: He should not say "I lied," because he may in fact be truthful, and then his saying "I lied" would be a lie, and lying is a sin, and committing a sin is not repentance from another sin. Rather, he says: "The accusation is false. I regret what I said, I have retracted it, and I will not return to it."

Fourth: Al-Razi said regarding His words ﴿and reform﴾ [al-Nur: 5]: Our companions said that after repentance, a period must pass in which good conduct is shown, before his testimony is accepted and his guardianship (wilaya) is restored. They then fixed that period at one year (p-4452), so that the four seasons pass over him, during which conditions and temperaments change, just as a year's term is given to the impotent man (al-'innin). The Law has attached rulings to the year, such as zakat, jizya, and others. End of quote.

Al-Ghazali said in al-Wajiz: It suffices for him to say: "I have repented and will not return." Except when he confesses to having lied about himself, in which case he is a defiant person who must be tested, like every defiant person who says "I have repented." He is not believed until he is tested for a period, so that the soundness of his inner state is known through indications of his circumstances. End of quote.

From this it is known that fixing a year has no evidence, rather the criterion is knowledge of his righteousness and the manifestation of his uprightness, even if it occurs after the hadd.

Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said: Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated through the chain of Husayn ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, who said: I saw a man lashed with the hadd for slander with zina. When the flogging was finished, he showed repentance. I met Abu al-Zinad, who said to me: The ruling among us in Medina is that when the slanderer retracts his statement and seeks forgiveness from his Lord, his testimony is accepted. Al-Bukhari also cited it in suspended form (mu'allaq).

Fifth: We transmit here what al-Suyuti summarized in al-Iklil regarding the rulings of the verse. He said, may Allah have mercy on him: In this verse is the prohibition of slander, that it is defiance (fisq), that the slanderer's testimony is not accepted, and that he is lashed eighty lashes if he slanders a muhsana, that is, a chaste woman. Its implication is that if he slanders one known for zina, he is not punished with the hadd for slander. This is made explicit by His words: ﴿then do not produce four witnesses﴾. And in it: zina is not established by fewer than four men, nor by women. This applies whether they testify together or separately. Some who argued from the generality of the verse held that a slave is also lashed eighty lashes; others held that the slanderer of a disbeliever, a slave, a minor, or an insane person, and his offspring, is also punished. It is also used as evidence by those who say that one who slanders himself and then retracts is not punished with the hadd for himself, because he has not harmed anyone. And those who say that the hadd of slander is one of the rights of Allah, so pardoning it is not permitted, also cite it as evidence. End of quote.

Then I came across the Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyya, may Allah have mercy on him, in his investigation into the acceptance of testimony after repentance, a verification worthy of attention. He said, may Allah have mercy on him: His words, exalted is He, ﴿and never accept their testimony﴾ are explicit that these slanderers' testimony is never accepted, whether they are one or many. Indeed, the wording of the verse encompasses the plural both collectively and distributively, because it was revealed concerning the people of the slander (ahl al-ifk), by the agreement of the people of knowledge, hadith, jurisprudence, and exegesis. Those who slandered 'A'isha were a number, not one, when they saw her return in the company of Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal after the army had withdrawn; she had gone looking for a necklace of hers that had been lost. They lifted her howdah, believing she was inside it because of her lightness, but she was not in it. When she returned, she found no one, so she remained in her place. Safwan had lagged behind the army. When he saw her, he turned his face away from her and made his mount kneel until she mounted it. Then he went to the army, and his being alone with her was out of necessity, just as it is permissible for a woman to travel without a mahram out of necessity, such as in a journey of migration (hijra), just as Umm Kulthum bint 'Uqba came as a migrant, and the story of 'A'isha.

The verse indicates that the slanderers' testimony is not accepted, either when they act together or when they act separately. The verse also indicates that their testimony after repentance is accepted, as is the position of the majority of scholars (jumhur). Among them were Misṭaḥ, Ḥassān and Ḥamnah. It is known that the Prophet (ﷺ) did not reject the testimony of any one of them, nor did the Muslims after him, because all of them repented when the Qur'an was revealed clearing her (ʿĀʾishah). Whoever did not repent at that time would be a disbeliever who denies the Qur'an. These people remained Muslims, and God forbade severing ties with them. Had their testimony been rejected after repentance, this would have become widely known, just as ʿUmar's rejection of the testimony of Abū Bakrah became widely known. The story of ʿĀʾishah is greater than the story of al-Mughīrah.

However, whoever rejects the testimony of a slanderer after repentance says: "I reject the testimony of one who has been subjected to the prescribed punishment (ḥadd) for slander." These people were not subjected to it. The earlier scholars answer with several responses. The first: it has been related in the Sunan that they were subjected to the punishment. The second: this condition is not considered in the apparent meaning of the Qur'an, and they (the opponents) do not hold it. The third: those who took the punishment into account and made it a condition said: a slanderer may be truthful and may be lying. The victim's refraining from demanding the punishment may be due to the slanderer's truthfulness. So if the victim demands it and the slanderer does not produce four witnesses, his lie becomes apparent. It is known that the lie of those who slandered ʿĀʾishah became apparent to a greater degree than the lie of anyone else, for God, mighty and majestic, is the One who cleared her by His speech which He sent down from above the seven heavens and which is recited. If their testimony is accepted in that case, then the testimony of others is more deserving of acceptance. The story of ʿUmar, in which he judged between the Muhājirūn and the Anṣār concerning al-Mughīrah, is evidence for both divisions together. When the fourth (witness) hesitated, he (ʿUmar) flogged the three others, excluding him, and rejected their testimony, because two of the three repented, so he accepted their testimony. The third, Abū Bakrah, despite being among the best of them, did not repent [p. 4454], so the Muslims did not accept his testimony. ʿUmar had said: "Repent, and I will accept your testimony." However, if the Qur'an has made clear that if they do not produce four witnesses their testimony will never be accepted, and then said after that: ﴿And those are the defiantly disobedient (al-fāsiqūn)﴾ ﴿except those who repent﴾ [al-Nūr: 5], then it is known that His saying: { they are the defiantly disobedient } is a description of blame directed at them, beyond the rejection of testimony.

As for the interpretation of justice ('adālah), it is uprightness in religion and manliness (murwah). When this is found in a person, he is just in his testimony and is among the righteous. As for the claim that no one may be called as a witness in a bequest, nor in a revocation (of divorce), in all places and times until he possesses this attribute, there is nothing in the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Messenger that indicates this. Rather, this is the attribute of the believer who has perfected his faith by performing the obligations, even if he has not perfected the recommended acts. Whoever is like this is among the God-fearing friends of God.

Furthermore, those who hold this view may interpret the obligations as the five daily prayers and the like. Indeed, a person may have obligations toward God and toward His servants that no one can count except God, and neglecting some of them may be a greater sin than drinking wine or fornication. Nevertheless, they do not consider this a defect in his justice, either because they do not sense the abundance of obligations, or because they focus on abstaining from misdeeds without performing the obligations. The matter is not so in the Sharia. In sum, this (performance of obligations) is taken into account in the matters of reward and punishment, praise and blame, loyalty and enmity, and this is a great matter. The matter of testimony depends on the witness being acceptable (marḍiyyan), or being one of ʿadl, by diligently seeking equity and justice in his words and actions, and truthfulness in his testimony and report. Often this is found together with a neglect of many of those attributes. Likewise, the attributes that they took into account are often found without this, as we have seen, each of the two categories frequently. But it is said: this is a presumption (maẓinnah) of truthfulness and justice, and the purpose of testimony, its evidence and its sign. For the Prophet (ﷺ) said in the hadith agreed upon for its authenticity: ««Adhere to truthfulness, for truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise.»» The hadith... Truthfulness necessitates righteousness, just as lying necessitates wickedness. When the necessitating thing, which is diligence in truthfulness, is found, the necessitated thing, which is righteousness, is found. When the necessitated thing, which is righteousness, is absent, the necessitating thing, which is truthfulness, is absent. When lying, the necessitating thing, is found, wickedness, the necessitated thing, is found. When wickedness, the necessitated thing, is absent, lying, the necessitating thing, is absent. For this reason, a man's lack of righteousness is used as evidence of his lying, and his lack of wickedness as evidence of his truthfulness. So the justice they mention: whoever is free of wickedness, which is committing a major sin and persisting in a minor sin. When this is absent from him, his lying, which calls him to wickedness, is absent. The defiantly disobedient (al-fāsiq) is the one whose righteousness is lacking, and when his righteousness is lacking, his truthfulness is lacking. The indication of this hadith is based on the fact that the one who calls to righteousness necessitates righteousness, and the one who calls to wickedness necessitates wickedness. Error is like forgetfulness, and deliberate action is like lying. End. Then God, exalted is He, explained the ruling concerning those who accuse their wives specifically, after explaining the ruling concerning those who accuse others, by His saying, glorified is He:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 24, verses 4–5 (part 1 of 2):

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:
[4–5] ﴿And those who accuse chaste women and then do not produce four witnesses, lash them eighty lashes, and never accept their testimony, and those are the defiantly disobedient (al-fasiqun)﴾ ﴿Except those who repent after that and reform. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Nur: 5].

﴿Those who accuse﴾ meaning: those who slander with fornication (zina). ﴿Chaste women﴾ meaning: Muslim, free, sane, adult women who are chaste, (p-4449) guarding themselves against fornication. ﴿Then do not produce four witnesses﴾ meaning: who testify to what they accused them of. ﴿Lash them eighty lashes﴾ meaning: each one of the accusers. The specification of women is due to the particular occurrence (of the incident), and because slander against them is more common and more heinous; otherwise, there is no difference in this between males and females. ﴿And never accept their testimony﴾ meaning: in any matter whatsoever, because their lying is evident. ﴿And those are the defiantly disobedient﴾ meaning: because they have departed from what was obligatory upon them, namely safeguarding the rights of chaste women. ﴿Except those who repent after that﴾ [al-Nur: 5] meaning: after the slander. ﴿And reform﴾ [al-Nur: 5] meaning: their deeds. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Nur: 5] meaning: by accepting their repentance and pardoning them.

Remarks:

First: Ibn Taymiyya said: He, exalted is He, mentioned the number of witnesses and left their description unrestricted; He did not qualify them as "from among us," nor "whom we approve of," nor "of those possessing justice." Therefore, scholars have disputed: Does the testimony of four who are not (themselves) of upright character, such as the testimony of people of wickedness, avert the hadd (prescribed punishment) from the slanderer? There are two opinions. One holds that it averts it, like the testimony of a husband against his wife four times: it averts the hadd of slander, but does not impose the hadd on the woman. If the woman does not testify, is she then subjected to the hadd, or is she detained until she confesses or performs li'an (mutual imprecation), or is her path left free? On this there is dispute. Therefore, it does not follow from averting the hadd from the slanderer that the hadd of zina is obligatory, for both are hudud. And the hudud are averted by doubts (shubuhat). The four testimonies for the slanderer constitute a strong doubt. Even if the one slandered confessed once, twice, or three times, the hadd is averted from the slanderer, and it is not obligatory upon him according to most scholars. Even if the one slandered was not muhsan, such as one who is well known for indecency, his slanderer is not punished with the hadd of slander, and he himself is not subjected to the hadd of zina merely by public reputation (istifada), though each of them is punished with a discretionary penalty short of the hadd. The hadd of zina is not established against a Muslim except by the testimony of Muslim witnesses. However, it is said: He did not restrict them with justice ('adala), yet Allah has commanded us to bear testimony that is needed from people of justice and approval, and they are those who comply with what Allah has commanded in His words: ﴿Be steadfast in upholding justice﴾ [al-Nisa': 135], His words: ﴿And when you speak, be just, even if it concerns a near relative﴾ [al-An'am: 152], His words: ﴿And do not conceal testimony﴾ [al-Baqara: 283], His words: ﴿And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called﴾ [al-Baqara: 282], and His words: ﴿And those who are upright in their testimonies﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 33]. So they establish it with justice for Allah, and thus the purpose of the one who sought their testimony is achieved.

The second aspect: their testimony is accepted because they are people of justice and approval. This indicates that it is obligatory to accept it and to give it. Allah, glorified is He, has forbidden accepting the testimony of a defiantly disobedient person in His words: ﴿If a defiantly disobedient person brings you a report, verify it﴾ [al-Hujurat: 6]. However, this is explicit that the report of a single defiant person must be verified. As for two or more defiant persons, the evidence for it requires another premise. What he mentioned regarding the number of witnesses is not fixed in judgment by the consensus of scholars in several cases. According to the majority, judgment is made without witnesses in several cases, such as when the party refuses (nukul) or makes a return of oath (radd), and the like.

We judge by one witness and an oath, as the Sunnah has established. What indicates this is that Allah did not stipulate this condition at the time of giving testimony, neither in the verse on zina nor in the verse on slander. Rather, He said: ﴿Call upon four of your men to testify against them﴾ [al-Nisa': 15]. He only commanded verification regarding the report of a single defiant person, and did not command it regarding the report of two defiant persons. The report of two persons produces a belief that the report of one person does not produce. Therefore, the scholars have said: If the judge doubts the witnesses, he separates them and questions them about what reveals their agreement and disagreement. End of quote.

Second: The Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in al-Fath: The majority hold that the testimony of one who slandered is accepted after repentance, and the designation of defiance (fisq) is removed from him, whether this occurs after the hadd is applied or before it, based on His words: ﴿except those who repent﴾ [al-Nur: 5]. Al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding this verse: Whoever repents, his testimony is accepted in the Book of Allah. They interpreted His words ﴿never﴾ to mean as long as he persists in his slander, because the "never" of anything is according to what befits it, just as if it were said: The testimony of a disbeliever is never accepted, meaning as long as he persists in disbelief. Al-Sha'bi went further, saying: If the slanderer repents before the hadd is applied to him, it is dropped from him. The Hanafis held (p-4451) that the exception relates only to defiance; when he repents, the designation of defiance is dropped from him, but his testimony is never accepted. Some of the Successors (tabi'un) said this as well. End of quote.

Al-Zamakhshari said: What the apparent meaning and arrangement of the verse require is that the three clauses together constitute the response of the condition, as if it were said: Whoever slanders chaste women, lash them, reject their testimony, and label them defiant. That is, combine for them the lashing, the rejection, and the labeling as defiant, except those who repent of the slander and reform, for Allah will forgive them, so they become neither lashed, nor rejected, nor labeled defiant. End of quote.

Al-Bukhari recorded in his Sahih, in the Book of Testimonies, in the chapter on the testimony of the slanderer, the thief, and the fornicator, from 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, that he lashed Abu Bakra, Shibl ibn Ma'bad, and Nafi', for slandering al-Mughira with zina, when they testified that they saw him between the legs of the woman (mutabattin al-mar'a). Ziyad did not give a definitive testimony. Then he asked them to repent and said: Whoever repents, I will accept his testimony. In another narration he said to them: Whoever retracts his statement, I will accept his testimony concerning what is to come; and whoever does not do so, I will not permit his testimony. Shibl and Nafi' retracted their statements, but Abu Bakra refused to retract.

Al-Muhallab said: It is inferred from this that retracting one's accusation is not a condition for the acceptance of his repentance, because Abu Bakra did not deny his statement, and yet the Muslims accepted his narration and acted upon it.

Third: Al-Razi said: They differed over how repentance from slander is to be done.

Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Repentance from it is retracting one's own statement. His companions differed over its meaning. Al-Istakhri said: He says, "I lied in what I said, and I will not return to the like of it." Abu Ishaq said: He should not say "I lied," because he may in fact be truthful, and then his saying "I lied" would be a lie, and lying is a sin, and committing a sin is not repentance from another sin. Rather, he says: "The accusation is false. I regret what I said, I have retracted it, and I will not return to it."

Fourth: Al-Razi said regarding His words ﴿and reform﴾ [al-Nur: 5]: Our companions said that after repentance, a period must pass in which good conduct is shown, before his testimony is accepted and his guardianship (wilaya) is restored. They then fixed that period at one year (p-4452), so that the four seasons pass over him, during which conditions and temperaments change, just as a year's term is given to the impotent man (al-'innin). The Law has attached rulings to the year, such as zakat, jizya, and others. End of quote.

Al-Ghazali said in al-Wajiz: It suffices for him to say: "I have repented and will not return." Except when he confesses to having lied about himself, in which case he is a defiant person who must be tested, like every defiant person who says "I have repented." He is not believed until he is tested for a period, so that the soundness of his inner state is known through indications of his circumstances. End of quote.

From this it is known that fixing a year has no evidence, rather the criterion is knowledge of his righteousness and the manifestation of his uprightness, even if it occurs after the hadd.

Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said: Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated through the chain of Husayn ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, who said: I saw a man lashed with the hadd for slander with zina. When the flogging was finished, he showed repentance. I met Abu al-Zinad, who said to me: The ruling among us in Medina is that when the slanderer retracts his statement and seeks forgiveness from his Lord, his testimony is accepted. Al-Bukhari also cited it in suspended form (mu'allaq).

Fifth: We transmit here what al-Suyuti summarized in al-Iklil regarding the rulings of the verse. He said, may Allah have mercy on him: In this verse is the prohibition of slander, that it is defiance (fisq), that the slanderer's testimony is not accepted, and that he is lashed eighty lashes if he slanders a muhsana, that is, a chaste woman. Its implication is that if he slanders one known for zina, he is not punished with the hadd for slander. This is made explicit by His words: ﴿then do not produce four witnesses﴾. And in it: zina is not established by fewer than four men, nor by women. This applies whether they testify together or separately. Some who argued from the generality of the verse held that a slave is also lashed eighty lashes; others held that the slanderer of a disbeliever, a slave, a minor, or an insane person, and his offspring, is also punished. It is also used as evidence by those who say that one who slanders himself and then retracts is not punished with the hadd for himself, because he has not harmed anyone. And those who say that the hadd of slander is one of the rights of Allah, so pardoning it is not permitted, also cite it as evidence. End of quote.

Then I came across the Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyya, may Allah have mercy on him, in his investigation into the acceptance of testimony after repentance, a verification worthy of attention. He said, may Allah have mercy on him: His words, exalted is He, ﴿and never accept their testimony﴾ are explicit that these slanderers' testimony is never accepted, whether they are one or many. Indeed, the wording of the verse encompasses the plural both collectively and distributively, because it was revealed concerning the people of the slander (ahl al-ifk), by the agreement of the people of knowledge, hadith, jurisprudence, and exegesis. Those who slandered 'A'isha were a number, not one, when they saw her return in the company of Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal after the army had withdrawn; she had gone looking for a necklace of hers that had been lost. They lifted her howdah, believing she was inside it because of her lightness, but she was not in it. When she returned, she found no one, so she remained in her place. Safwan had lagged behind the army. When he saw her, he turned his face away from her and made his mount kneel until she mounted it. Then he went to the army, and his being alone with her was out of necessity, just as it is permissible for a woman to travel without a mahram out of necessity, such as in a journey of migration (hijra), just as Umm Kulthum bint 'Uqba came as a migrant, and the story of 'A'isha.

The verse indicates that the slanderers' testimony is not accepted, either when they act together or when they act separately. The verse also indicates that their testimony after repentance is accepted, as is the position of the majority of scholars (jumhur). Among them were Misṭaḥ, Ḥassān and Ḥamnah. It is known that the Prophet (ﷺ) did not reject the testimony of any one of them, nor did the Muslims after him, because all of them repented when the Qur'an was revealed clearing her (ʿĀʾishah). Whoever did not repent at that time would be a disbeliever who denies the Qur'an. These people remained Muslims, and God forbade severing ties with them. Had their testimony been rejected after repentance, this would have become widely known, just as ʿUmar's rejection of the testimony of Abū Bakrah became widely known. The story of ʿĀʾishah is greater than the story of al-Mughīrah.

However, whoever rejects the testimony of a slanderer after repentance says: "I reject the testimony of one who has been subjected to the prescribed punishment (ḥadd) for slander." These people were not subjected to it. The earlier scholars answer with several responses. The first: it has been related in the Sunan that they were subjected to the punishment. The second: this condition is not considered in the apparent meaning of the Qur'an, and they (the opponents) do not hold it. The third: those who took the punishment into account and made it a condition said: a slanderer may be truthful and may be lying. The victim's refraining from demanding the punishment may be due to the slanderer's truthfulness. So if the victim demands it and the slanderer does not produce four witnesses, his lie becomes apparent. It is known that the lie of those who slandered ʿĀʾishah became apparent to a greater degree than the lie of anyone else, for God, mighty and majestic, is the One who cleared her by His speech which He sent down from above the seven heavens and which is recited. If their testimony is accepted in that case, then the testimony of others is more deserving of acceptance. The story of ʿUmar, in which he judged between the Muhājirūn and the Anṣār concerning al-Mughīrah, is evidence for both divisions together. When the fourth (witness) hesitated, he (ʿUmar) flogged the three others, excluding him, and rejected their testimony, because two of the three repented, so he accepted their testimony. The third, Abū Bakrah, despite being among the best of them, did not repent [p. 4454], so the Muslims did not accept his testimony. ʿUmar had said: "Repent, and I will accept your testimony." However, if the Qur'an has made clear that if they do not produce four witnesses their testimony will never be accepted, and then said after that: ﴿And those are the defiantly disobedient (al-fāsiqūn)﴾ ﴿except those who repent﴾ [al-Nūr: 5], then it is known that His saying: { they are the defiantly disobedient } is a description of blame directed at them, beyond the rejection of testimony.

As for the interpretation of justice ('adālah), it is uprightness in religion and manliness (murwah). When this is found in a person, he is just in his testimony and is among the righteous. As for the claim that no one may be called as a witness in a bequest, nor in a revocation (of divorce), in all places and times until he possesses this attribute, there is nothing in the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Messenger that indicates this. Rather, this is the attribute of the believer who has perfected his faith by performing the obligations, even if he has not perfected the recommended acts. Whoever is like this is among the God-fearing friends of God.

Furthermore, those who hold this view may interpret the obligations as the five daily prayers and the like. Indeed, a person may have obligations toward God and toward His servants that no one can count except God, and neglecting some of them may be a greater sin than drinking wine or fornication. Nevertheless, they do not consider this a defect in his justice, either because they do not sense the abundance of obligations, or because they focus on abstaining from misdeeds without performing the obligations. The matter is not so in the Sharia.
