In sum, this (performance of obligations) is taken into account in the matters of reward and punishment, praise and blame, loyalty and enmity, and this is a great matter. The matter of testimony depends on the witness being acceptable (marḍiyyan), or being one of ʿadl, by diligently seeking equity and justice in his words and actions, and truthfulness in his testimony and report. Often this is found together with a neglect of many of those attributes. Likewise, the attributes that they took into account are often found without this, as we have seen, each of the two categories frequently. But it is said: this is a presumption (maẓinnah) of truthfulness and justice, and the purpose of testimony, its evidence and its sign. For the Prophet (ﷺ) said in the hadith agreed upon for its authenticity: ««Adhere to truthfulness, for truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise.»» The hadith... Truthfulness necessitates righteousness, just as lying necessitates wickedness. When the necessitating thing, which is diligence in truthfulness, is found, the necessitated thing, which is righteousness, is found. When the necessitated thing, which is righteousness, is absent, the necessitating thing, which is truthfulness, is absent. When lying, the necessitating thing, is found, wickedness, the necessitated thing, is found. When wickedness, the necessitated thing, is absent, lying, the necessitating thing, is absent. For this reason, a man's lack of righteousness is used as evidence of his lying, and his lack of wickedness as evidence of his truthfulness. So the justice they mention: whoever is free of wickedness, which is committing a major sin and persisting in a minor sin. When this is absent from him, his lying, which calls him to wickedness, is absent. The defiantly disobedient (al-fāsiq) is the one whose righteousness is lacking, and when his righteousness is lacking, his truthfulness is lacking. The indication of this hadith is based on the fact that the one who calls to righteousness necessitates righteousness, and the one who calls to wickedness necessitates wickedness. Error is like forgetfulness, and deliberate action is like lying. End. Then God, exalted is He, explained the ruling concerning those who accuse their wives specifically, after explaining the ruling concerning those who accuse others, by His saying, glorified is He:

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[6–7] ﴿And those who accuse their wives, and have no witnesses except themselves, then the testimony of one of them is four testimonies by Allah, that indeed he is of the truthful. And the fifth [testimony is] that the curse of Allah be upon him if he is of the liars.﴾ [An-Nur: 7]

﴿And those who accuse their wives﴾ i.e., of adultery. ﴿And have no witnesses except themselves, then the testimony of one of them is four testimonies by Allah, that indeed he is of the truthful﴾ i.e., in what he has accused her of of adultery. ﴿And the fifth﴾ [An-Nur: 7] i.e., and the fifth testimony in addition to the four preceding ones: ﴿that the curse of Allah be upon him if he is of the liars﴾ [An-Nur: 7] i.e., in what he has accused her of of adultery. Thereby the hadd (prescribed punishment) of qadhf (false accusation) falls from him, and the hadd falls upon her, which is stoning (al-rajm), unless she also performs li'an (mutual imprecation). As He, glorified is He, said:

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[6–7] ﴿And those who accuse their wives, and have no witnesses except themselves, then the testimony of one of them is four testimonies by Allah, that indeed he is of the truthful. And the fifth [testimony is] that the curse of Allah be upon him if he is of the liars.﴾ [An-Nur: 7]

﴿And those who accuse their wives﴾ i.e., of adultery. ﴿And have no witnesses except themselves, then the testimony of one of them is four testimonies by Allah, that indeed he is of the truthful﴾ i.e., in what he has accused her of of adultery. ﴿And the fifth﴾ [An-Nur: 7] i.e., and the fifth testimony in addition to the four preceding ones: ﴿that the curse of Allah be upon him if he is of the liars﴾ [An-Nur: 7] i.e., in what he has accused her of of adultery. Thereby the hadd (prescribed punishment) of qadhf (false accusation) falls from him, and the hadd falls upon her, which is stoning (al-rajm), unless she also performs li'an (mutual imprecation). As He, glorified is He, said:

[p. 4456]

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[8-10] ﴿And it averts the punishment from her that she testify four testimonies by Allah that he is surely of the liars. And the fifth [testimony] that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he is of the truthful.﴾ [al-Nur: 9] ﴿And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, and that Allah is Oft-Returning, All-Wise.﴾ [al-Nur: 10]

﴿And it averts the punishment from her﴾, i.e., the worldly punishment, which is stoning. ﴿That she testify four testimonies by Allah that he is surely of the liars﴾, i.e., regarding what he accused her of, namely adultery. ﴿And the fifth [testimony] that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he﴾ [al-Nur: 9], i.e., the husband, ﴿is of the truthful﴾ [al-Nur: 9]. ﴿And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, and that Allah is Oft-Returning, All-Wise﴾ [al-Nur: 10], i.e., you would have been in distress, and many of your affairs would have become difficult for you. But out of His mercy and kindness, He legislated for you the relief and the way out, which He revealed and made firm.

Notes:

First: Ibn Kathir said: This noble verse contains relief for spouses and an additional way out. When one of them accuses his wife [of adultery] and it is difficult for him to produce evidence, he may perform li'an (mutual imprecation) with her, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has commanded. This means that he brings her before the imam (leader) and makes a claim against her regarding what he accused her of. The judge then makes him swear four oaths by Allah in place of four witnesses, [saying] that he is surely of the truthful, i.e., regarding what he accused her of, namely adultery. [He swears] the fifth [oath] that the curse of Allah be upon him if he is of the liars. When he says this, she is separated from him by this very li'an according to al-Shafi'i and a large group of scholars, and she is forbidden to him forever. He gives her her dowry (mahr). The hadd (prescribed punishment) for adultery becomes obligatory upon her. The punishment is averted from her only if she performs li'an by testifying four testimonies by Allah that he is surely of the liars, i.e., regarding what he accused her of, and [swears] the fifth [oath] that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he is of the truthful.

Second: It is narrated in the Sahih (authentic collection) that this occurred during the time of the Prophet (ﷺ), and that "a man said to the Prophet (ﷺ): (Tell me, if a man sees a man with his wife, would he kill him and you kill him, or how should he act?) The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: 'Allah has decided concerning you and your wife.' And he recited to him what had been revealed of this verse. So they performed li'an in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

It is also established that it occurred for two men who were named. The commentators on the Sahih have differed about the meaning of what is narrated, that the verse was revealed concerning both of them together.

If you review what we wrote in (al-Muqaddimah) (the Introduction) regarding the meaning of the occasion of revelation (sabab al-nuzul), the difficulty will be removed, so refer to it.

Third: al-Suyuti said in (al-Iklil): This verse is the foundation of li'an (mutual imprecation). It contains the condition that it requires a prior qadhf (false accusation of unchastity). It is only between spouses, not between a man and a non-related woman, nor between a master and his female slave. Those who argue from its general wording have deduced li'an for disbelievers, slaves, the eunuch, the impotent man, one who has been punished for qadhf, the blind, the mute, and [in the case of] a young girl who cannot conceive and a woman past childbearing age. Those who take the saying ﴿And they have no witnesses except themselves﴾ [al-Nur: 6] as evidence said there is no li'an if he produces evidence of her adultery. Those who take the saying ﴿So the testimony of one of them﴾ [al-Nur: 6] as evidence said that li'an is a testimony, not an oath. His saying ﴿four testimonies by Allah﴾ [al-Nur: 6], etc., indicates that its formula is that he says: "I testify by Allah that I am surely of the truthful," four times, and the fifth [time]: "The curse of Allah be upon him if he is of the liars." Those who do not permit replacing "I testify" (ashhadu) with "I swear" (uqsimu) or the like, or with "by Allah" replaced by "by the Most Merciful" or the like, or who add "by the knowledge of Allah" or the like, have used this as evidence. Likewise those who do not require adding "Other than whom there is no god" [and those who do not permit omitting "I am surely of the truthful"], nor replacing it with "I have lied against her" or the like, nor being satisfied with fewer than four [testimonies]. This is contrary to Abu Hanifa, who was satisfied with three testimonies. [They also deny] placing the curse before the testimony, or in the middle, or replacing it with the wrath. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It averts the punishment from her﴾ etc., indicates that his li'an makes the hadd for adultery obligatory upon the woman, and that she may avert it by saying four times: "I testify by Allah that he is surely of the liars," and the fifth [time]: "The wrath of Allah be upon her if...," etc. It also indicates that she may not replace "I testify" with "I swear," or the wrath with the curse, and so on, as mentioned above. It has also been used as evidence that her li'an may not precede his li'an. End.

Fourth: Know that the prescribed punishment for adultery is of two kinds: flogging (jald) and stoning (rajm). Flogging is the punishment for two free, unmarried persons who commit adultery. Each of them is flogged one hundred lashes. As for exiling them for one year, and exiling the adulterer alone in the same way, there is disagreement. However, if the imam sees it as beneficial, there is no disagreement about implementing it. Stoning is the punishment for two adulterers who are muhsan (married and eligible). Ihsan is an expression for being adult, sane, free, and having entered into a valid marriage. He is not to be killed by the sword; rather, he is to be stoned, not with a crushing boulder, nor with pebbles that prolong the torment, but with moderate stones, as in (al-Wajiz) (The Concise).

A group of the Kharijites (an early sectarian group) objected to the legislation of stoning in Islam and said: "Allah did not command it in His Mighty Book." What appears in the Qur'an as the punishment for adultery consists of two rulings. One of them is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those of your women who commit lewdness, bring four [witnesses] from among you against them. And if they testify, then confine them to the houses until death takes them or Allah ordains for them a way﴾ [al-Nisa': 15]; ﴿And the two of you who commit it, harm them both. And if they repent and reform, then leave them alone﴾ [al-Nisa': 16]. This ruling has been abrogated (naskh), i.e., clarified, by the second ruling, which is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The adulterous woman and the adulterous man, flog each one of them with a hundred lashes. And let not pity for them detain you in the religion of Allah, if you should believe in Allah and the Last Day. And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾ [al-Nur: 2]. This is the argument of the Kharijites.

As for the argument of consensus (ijma'), it is the transmission of authentic reports indicating that "the Prophet (ﷺ) commanded the stoning of the muhsan, and carried it out." A number of hadiths and rulings from the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them all, have been transmitted regarding this. So it is stated in the book (al-Muqabalat). Al-Razi preceded him in (his Tafsir), but he lengthened the discussion in presenting the doubt of the Kharijites, and answered it with what can be summarized as follows: The aforementioned verse is specific to the unmarried person. He specified it by the mutawatir (widely transmitted) report about stoning. Specifying the Qur'an by a solitary report (khabar al-wahid) is permissible, so specifying it by a mutawatir report is even more appropriate. Second, he said: It is not unlikely that the legal rulings change according to the changing of benefits. Then Allah, exalted is He, alluded to the account of the slander (ifk) and the exoneration of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, in His saying, glorified is He:

[p. 4456]

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[8-10] ﴿And it averts the punishment from her that she testify four testimonies by Allah that he is surely of the liars. And the fifth [testimony] that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he is of the truthful.﴾ [al-Nur: 9] ﴿And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, and that Allah is Oft-Returning, All-Wise.﴾ [al-Nur: 10]

﴿And it averts the punishment from her﴾, i.e., the worldly punishment, which is stoning. ﴿That she testify four testimonies by Allah that he is surely of the liars﴾, i.e., regarding what he accused her of, namely adultery. ﴿And the fifth [testimony] that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he﴾ [al-Nur: 9], i.e., the husband, ﴿is of the truthful﴾ [al-Nur: 9]. ﴿And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, and that Allah is Oft-Returning, All-Wise﴾ [al-Nur: 10], i.e., you would have been in distress, and many of your affairs would have become difficult for you. Notes:

First: Ibn Kathir said: This noble verse contains relief for spouses and an additional way out. This means that he brings her before the imam (leader) and makes a claim against her regarding what he accused her of. The judge then makes him swear four oaths by Allah in place of four witnesses, [saying] that he is surely of the truthful, i.e., regarding what he accused her of, namely adultery. [He swears] the fifth [oath] that the curse of Allah be upon him if he is of the liars. When he says this, she is separated from him by this very li'an according to al-Shafi'i and a large group of scholars, and she is forbidden to him forever. He gives her her dowry (mahr). The hadd (prescribed punishment) for adultery becomes obligatory upon her. The punishment is averted from her only if she performs li'an by testifying four testimonies by Allah that he is surely of the liars, i.e., regarding what he accused her of, and [swears] the fifth [oath] that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he is of the truthful.

Second: It is narrated in the Sahih (authentic collection) that this occurred during the time of the Prophet (ﷺ), and that "a man said to the Prophet (ﷺ): (Tell me, if a man sees a man with his wife, would he kill him and you kill him, or how should he act?) The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: 'Allah has decided concerning you and your wife.' And he recited to him what had been revealed of this verse. So they performed li'an in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

It is also established that it occurred for two men who were named. The commentators on the Sahih have differed about the meaning of what is narrated, that the verse was revealed concerning both of them together.

If you review what we wrote in (al-Muqaddimah) (the Introduction) regarding the meaning of the occasion of revelation (sabab al-nuzul), the difficulty will be removed, so refer to it.

It is only between spouses, not between a man and a non-related woman, nor between a master and his female slave. Those who argue from its general wording have deduced li'an for disbelievers, slaves, the eunuch, the impotent man, one who has been punished for qadhf, the blind, the mute, and [in the case of] a young girl who cannot conceive and a woman past childbearing age. Those who take the saying ﴿And they have no witnesses except themselves﴾ [al-Nur: 6] as evidence said there is no li'an if he produces evidence of her adultery. Those who take the saying ﴿So the testimony of one of them﴾ [al-Nur: 6] as evidence said that li'an is a testimony, not an oath. His saying ﴿four testimonies by Allah﴾ [al-Nur: 6], etc., indicates that its formula is that he says: "I testify by Allah that I am surely of the truthful," four times, and the fifth [time]: "The curse of Allah be upon him if he is of the liars." This is contrary to Abu Hanifa, who was satisfied with three testimonies. [They also deny] placing the curse before the testimony, or in the middle, or replacing it with the wrath. It has also been used as evidence that her li'an may not precede his li'an. End.

Fourth: Know that the prescribed punishment for adultery is of two kinds: flogging (jald) and stoning (rajm). Flogging is the punishment for two free, unmarried persons who commit adultery. Each of them is flogged one hundred lashes. As for exiling them for one year, and exiling the adulterer alone in the same way, there is disagreement. However, if the imam sees it as beneficial, there is no disagreement about implementing it. Stoning is the punishment for two adulterers who are muhsan (married and eligible). Ihsan is an expression for being adult, sane, free, and having entered into a valid marriage. He is not to be killed by the sword; rather, he is to be stoned, not with a crushing boulder, nor with pebbles that prolong the torment, but with moderate stones, as in (al-Wajiz) (The Concise).

This is the argument of the Kharijites.

A number of hadiths and rulings from the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them all, have been transmitted regarding this. So it is stated in the book (al-Muqabalat). He specified it by the mutawatir (widely transmitted) report about stoning. Then Allah, exalted is He, alluded to the account of the slander (ifk) and the exoneration of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, in His saying, glorified is He:

The discussion of the words of His, exalted is He:

[11] ﴿Indeed, those who came with the slander are a faction among you. Do not consider it bad for you; rather, it is good for you. For every person among them is what he earned of the sin, and he who took upon himself its greater part among them will have a great punishment.﴾

﴿Indeed, those who came with the slander﴾: that is, with the most eloquent form of lying. It was said that it is slander (buhtan) which suddenly strikes you without warning. What is meant by it is that with which they slandered the Truthful One (al-Siddiqah), the Mother of the Believers, may Allah be pleased with her. The alif-lam here is for specific reference (al-'ahd), and it is permissible to take it as generic (al-jins). It was said: it then conveys restriction (qasr), as if there is no slander except this. In the wording "came" (al-maji') there is an indication that they fabricated it from their own selves, without it having any basis: ﴿a faction among you﴾, that is, a group from among you. It is the predicate of "indeed" (inna), and "among you" is a qualifier of it. And by this the information is conveyed. His, exalted is He, statement ﴿Do not consider it bad for you﴾ (p-4460) is a resumptive sentence (musta'nafah), and the pronoun "it" refers to the slander or the accusation. The address is to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, to the family of the Truthful One, may Allah be pleased with them, and to those among the believers whom that distressed, as consolation for them from the very beginning. His, exalted is He, statement ﴿rather, it is good for you﴾ is an addition to the consolation and the honouring. That is: do not think that it brings an accusation upon you or causes a defect in you; rather, it has brought you a great good.

Al-Zamakhshari said: The meaning of it being good for them is that they earned great reward through it, because it was a manifest trial and an apparent ordeal. And that eighteen verses were revealed concerning it, each one independent, containing that which glorifies the station of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and consoles him, and exonerates the Mother of the Believers, may Allah's good pleasure be upon her, and purifies the People of the House, and terrifies those who spoke about it or heard of it and whose ears did not reject it. And it contains a number of subtle kindnesses for the listeners and reciters until the Day of Resurrection, and religious benefits, rulings and etiquettes which are not hidden from those who reflect upon them. ﴿For every person among them is what he earned of the sin﴾: that is, its recompense, and that is blame in this world until the Day of Resurrection, and the lashing of eighty. And the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe. ﴿And he who took upon himself its greater part among them will have a great punishment﴾: that is, he undertook its magnitude and its spreading, after having begun by plunging into it, and he was the head of the hypocrites, 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy, due to his excessive enmity towards the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, his seizing of opportunities, and his seeking a path to defamation.

Al-Tabari narrated from Ibn Zayd who said: As for the one who took upon himself its greater part, it was 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, the wicked. He is the one who initiated this speech and said: "The wife of your Prophet spent the night with a man until morning, then he came leading her by the hand." And the great punishment encompasses the punishment of both abodes, as we have said.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted be He:

[12] ﴿Why, when you heard it, did the believing men and believing women not think well of their own people and say, "This is a clear lie"?﴾

﴿Why, when you heard it, did the believing men and believing women not think well of their own people﴾ means: of those among them who are believers, men and women. This is like His saying: ﴿and do not defame yourselves﴾ [al-Hujurat: 11]. Al-Shihab said: "This is from the artful speech (badi' al-kalam), and it occurs often in the Qur'an. Outwardly it implies that each person thinks well of himself, which is not what is meant. Rather, it means that he should think this of others. Its justification is that it is a figurative usage (majaz), since it treats the unity of kind as the unity of the self. This is why His saying ﴿nor kill yourselves﴾ [al-Nisa': 29] was explained as: nor kill those who are of your kind, or as: He makes them like a single self. So whoever defames a believer has defamed himself." It is also permissible to posit an elided noun (mudaf) here, meaning: some of the believing men and women thought well of the selves of the others. Al-Karmani said, regarding the hadith "Your property is forbidden to you," that it is like the saying "the sons of so-and-so killed themselves," meaning some of them killed one another, either as a figurative usage or by implying an elision (idmar) because of an indicator that diverts it from its apparent meaning.

"Why" (lawla) here is exhortatory (tahdidiyyah), meaning "why not" (halla): ﴿and said, "This is a clear lie"﴾, meaning: this which we heard, concerning the slander of the Mother of the Believers, is a clear lie, evident to whoever reasons and reflects upon it.

Al-'Allamah al-Zamakhshari said: "If you ask: Why was it not said, 'Why, when you heard it, did you not think well of yourselves and say...'? And why did He shift from address (khitab) to third person (ghaybah), and from the pronoun to the noun?" I say: To intensify the rebuke through the device of shift (iltifat). And to state explicitly the word "the believers," indicating that sharing in faith requires that no believing man should accept on his brother's behalf, nor any believing woman on her sister's behalf, the words of a defamer or slanderer. This also serves as a reminder that when a believer hears a rumour about his brother, his duty is to base the matter on assumption (zann), not on doubt (shakk), and to say, with full voice, on the basis of his good opinion of the believer: ﴿This is a clear lie﴾, in exactly these words that declare his innocence, as one who is certain and acquainted with the true state of affairs would say. This indicates a fine courtesy (adab) which few people practise or preserve. Would that you found someone who, when he hears [a rumour], keeps silent and does not spread what he heard to others! End of quotation. And His saying, exalted be He:

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[13] ﴿Why did they not bring four witnesses for it? Since they did not bring the witnesses, then those—with Allah—they are the liars.﴾

(p-4462) ﴿Why did they not bring four witnesses for it? Since they did not bring the witnesses, then those—with Allah—﴾ means: in His judgment and His law, which is founded upon clear and certain proofs. ﴿They are the liars﴾ means: they are the complete liars, those who are witnessed against as such.

Al-Zamakhshari said: This is a rebuke and a reproach to those who heard the slander and did not strive to repel it and deny it, and an argument against them based on what is plain and manifest in the Sharia: that it is obligatory to declare the slanderer a liar without proof and to punish him when he slanders a chaste woman concerning the honor of the believing women. So how much more so concerning the Mother of the Believers, the truthful daughter of the truthful (al-Siddiqa bint al-Siddiq), the beloved wife of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the beloved of the Beloved of Allah?

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[14] ﴿And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy in this world and the Hereafter, there would have touched you for what you plunged into a great punishment.﴾

﴿And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy in this world and the Hereafter, there would have touched you for what you plunged into a great punishment.﴾ That is: you would have been hastened with the punishment, because of what you plunged into of the slander (ifk). But He is vast in grace and mercy. He gives the sinner respite for repentance, and forbears with him so that he may return.

The discussion of the words of His Exalted saying:

[15] ﴿When you received it on your tongues and uttered with your mouths what you had no knowledge of, and you thought it a trivial matter, while with Allah it is grave.﴾

﴿When you received it﴾, i.e., at the time when some of you received it from others. ﴿On your tongues and you uttered with your mouths what you had no knowledge of, and you thought it a trivial matter﴾, i.e., there is no consequence for it and no punishment for the one who spreads it. ﴿While with Allah it is grave﴾, i.e., and the reality is that it is grave in sin and in drawing down punishment. Al-Mahayimi said: "Because audacity toward the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and toward his friends resembles audacity toward Allah, the Exalted." Al-Zamakhshari said: "If you ask: what is the meaning of His saying ﴿with your mouths﴾ (p-4463), when speech only occurs by the mouth? I say: its meaning is that a known matter has its knowledge in the heart, and then the tongue expresses it. But this falsehood is nothing other than words that run over your tongues and circulate in your mouths, without being an expression of knowledge in the heart. Like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿They say with their mouths what is not in their hearts﴾ [Al 'Imran: 167]." End of quotation. So the qualifier is not purely emphatic (like "he looked with his eye"), but serves to restrict the statement away from anything other than it. It has also been said that it is a rebuke, as you say, "He said it with his whole mouth," for the speaker sometimes hints and sometimes speaks openly and boastfully. This has been said regarding His saying: ﴿Hatred has appeared﴾ [Al 'Imran: 118]. It has also been said that its benefit is that it should not be supposed to be inner speech of the self (kalam nafsi). So it is an emphasis to repel metaphor (majaz). The context requires the first meaning. Thus in (al-'Inayah).

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[16] ﴿And why, when you heard it, did you not say, "It is not for us to speak of this; glory be to You! This is a tremendous slander"?﴾

﴿And why, when you heard it, did you not say﴾ — that is, as a rebuke to those who spread it: ﴿It is not for us﴾ — that is, it is not proper for us in any way ﴿to speak of this. Glory be to You! This is a tremendous slander﴾ — that is, as an declaration of Your transcendence and a disavowal before You of what these people have brought. For it is a tremendous slander whose truth is impossible.

Al-Zamakhshari said: The phrase "Subhanaka" (glory be to You) is an expression of wonder at the magnitude of the matter. If you ask, "What is the sense of wonder in the word of glorification (tasbih)?" I answer: The origin of this is that one glorifies God upon seeing a marvel among His creations; then it became frequent until it was used for everything that is wondered at. Or it is for declaring God exalted above the violation of the sanctity of His Prophet, peace be upon him, being immoral. End of quotation.

On the first view, it is a metaphor branching from metonymy (kinaya), and this is common. Al-Nawawi mentioned it in (al-Adhkar). Likewise, "There is no god but God" (la ilaha illa Allah) is also used to express wonder. As for invoking blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ) in a context of wonder, it is not attested and has not been heard in the language of the Sharia. The jurists have explicitly prohibited it. It has only occurred from the common people and some narrators of hadith, such as the saying:

"Whoever sees his beauty, the one to be ransomed, at once, let him bless Muhammad."

On the second view, it is a literal usage. Thus [it is stated] in (al-Inayah).

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 24, verses 17–18:

The discussion of His saying, exalted is He:

[17–18] ﴿God admonishes you never to return to the like of it, if you are believers﴾ ﴿And God makes the signs clear to you, and God is Knowing, Wise﴾ [al-Nur: 18].

﴿God admonishes you never to return to the like of it, if you are believers﴾: for true attachment to faith (ittisaf) restrains one from every reprehensible act. ﴿And God makes the signs clear to you﴾ [al-Nur: 18], i.e., the signs indicating the sacred laws (shara'i') and the noble etiquettes (mahasin al-adab), with a clear indication, so that you may take heed and be disciplined by them. That is, He sends them down thus, made clear, with an evident indication upon their witnessing: ﴿and God is Knowing, Wise﴾ [al-Nur: 18].

Then the Exalted pointed to a third discipline for one who hears some of the evil speech, such that something of it lodges in his mind: that he should not speak of it nor spread it, with His glorified saying, threatening:

That is, He sends them down thus, made clear, with an evident indication upon their witnessing: ﴿and God is Knowing, Wise﴾ [al-Nur: 18].

Then the Exalted pointed to a third discipline for one who hears some of the evil speech, such that something of it lodges in his mind: that he should not speak of it nor spread it, with His glorified saying, threatening:

The Explanation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[19] ﴿Indeed, those who love that immorality should spread among those who have believed will have a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter. And Allah knows, while you do not know.﴾

﴿Indeed, those who love that immorality should spread﴾ i.e., that the extremely ugly trait spreads, which is slander and the accusation of fornication or the like, such as sodomy and what is greater in obscenity. ﴿Among those who have believed, they will have a painful punishment in this world﴾ i.e., from the prescribed punishment (ḥadd) and other things that befall through worldly calamities. ﴿And the Hereafter﴾ i.e., from the punishment of the Fire. ﴿And Allah knows﴾ i.e., the secrets and inner thoughts that are in the hearts. ﴿And you do not know﴾ meaning: He has known the love of whoever loved the spreading (of the immorality), and He will punish him for it.

Section on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[20] ﴿And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, and that Allah is Kind and Merciful...﴾

﴿And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, and that Allah is Kind and Merciful﴾ is a repetition of the favour, by not hastening the punishment, to indicate the magnitude of the offence. The answer (jawab) is omitted, as it is dispensed with by its mention once before, and it is (﴿لَمَسَّكُم﴾, "would have touched you").

The discourse on the interpretation of His saying:

[21-22] ﴿O you who have believed, do not follow the footsteps of Satan. And whoever follows the footsteps of Satan - indeed, he enjoins immorality and wrongdoing. And if not for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy, none of you would ever have been purified. But Allah purifies whom He wills, and Allah is Hearing and Knowing. And let not those of virtue and wealth among you swear not to give to the near of kin and the needy and the emigrants in the way of Allah; let them pardon and overlook. Would you not like that Allah should forgive you? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ [al-Nur: 22]

﴿O you who have believed, do not follow the footsteps of Satan﴾, i.e., by spreading indecency. ﴿And whoever follows the footsteps of Satan - indeed, he enjoins immorality and wrongdoing. And if not for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy, none of you would ever have been purified﴾, i.e., would never have been cleansed of its filth. ﴿But Allah purifies whom He wills﴾ of His servants, by inspiring them with repentance and turning back (to Him). ﴿And Allah is Hearing and Knowing.﴾

﴿And let not those of virtue and wealth among you swear not to give to the near of kin and the needy and the emigrants in the way of Allah; let them pardon and overlook. Would you not like that Allah should forgive you? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ [al-Nur: 22]

al-Zamakhshari said: (yatali) is from (ta'tali), meaning to swear an oath. It is an iftial form from al-alyah, which is the oath. It was also said that it derives from their saying "ma alawtu juhdan" (I did not spare any effort), when one does not hold back any of it. The recitation variant of al-Hasan (al-Basri) supports the first meaning: "wa la yata'alla" (with a doubled lam). The meaning is: they should not swear that they will not do good to those who deserve kindness, or that they will not fall short in doing good to them, even if there is enmity between them due to an offence they committed. Rather, they should return to them with pardon and forgiveness, and should treat them as they hope their Lord will treat them, despite the abundance of their own sins and transgressions. The occasion of its revelation and the person it refers to will come later.

Then Exalted is He explained the threat against those who slander chaste women, by His saying:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[23–24] ﴿Indeed, those who accuse chaste, unwary, believing women are cursed in this world and the Hereafter, and theirs is a great punishment.﴾ ﴿On the Day when their tongues, their hands and their feet will testify against them concerning what they used to do.﴾ [An-Nur: 24]

﴿Indeed, those who accuse chaste, unwary﴾, meaning: those who are modest and free from immorality, pure of heart regarding it, ﴿believing women are cursed in this world﴾ by blame, by the prescribed punishment (hadd), and by the rejection of their testimony, unless they repent; ﴿and the Hereafter﴾, meaning: where the angels and whomever God wills will curse them; ﴿and theirs is a great punishment.﴾ ﴿On the Day when their tongues, their hands and their feet will testify against them concerning what they used to do.﴾ [An-Nur: 24] Meaning: they will acknowledge it, either through God, exalted is He, making them speak, or through the appearance of the traces of what they did upon them, so that whoever witnesses them knows what they did. This happens in a manner that God knows. Thus it is a metaphor (isti'arah). The first sense returns to His saying: ﴿They will say: "God has made us speak, He who made everything speak."﴾ [Fussilat: 21]. Its apparent meaning is the literal sense (haqiqah), and taking it in the second sense is far-fetched.

It has been said: it will come in (Ya-Sin): ﴿This Day We shall seal their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will bear witness to what they used to earn.﴾ [Ya-Sin: 65]. Sealing the mouths contradicts the testimony of the tongues. The answer is that sealing the mouths means preventing them from speaking what they wish and what benefits them, according to their own supposition, by choice, such as denial and making excuses. Or this applies in one situation and that in another situation. Or each of them applies to a different group than the other. Or this applies to the slanderers and that to the disbelievers. (But this is not valid), since there is no contradiction. The secret of explicitly mentioning the tongues here, and not mentioning them there, is that since this verse concerns the one who slanders with his tongue, and he is required to produce four witnesses, here He mentions five as well, and explicitly names the tongue by which his deed was done, in order to disgrace him, as a recompense for him of the same kind as his action. Thus [it is stated] in (al-'Inayah).

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[25] ﴿On that Day Allah will pay them their just recompense in full, and they will know that Allah is the Manifest Truth.﴾

﴿On that Day﴾ means: the day when they will bear witness against themselves concerning what has been mentioned. ﴿Allah will pay them their due recompense﴾ means: their reward. ﴿In full﴾ means: what is owed and established. ﴿And they will know that Allah is the Manifest Truth﴾ means: He is the One who makes things manifest as they truly are in themselves.

Then Exalted is He pointed to what confirms the exoneration by the evidence of custom and habit: that one does not join a like to anything except its like, and people are not driven except to their own kind, by His saying, glorified is He:

**Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 24, verse 26 (part 1 of 7):**

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[26] ﴿Evil women are for evil men, and evil men are for evil women; good women are for good men, and good men are for good women. Those are free of what they say. For them is forgiveness and a generous provision.﴾

﴿Evil women﴾, that is, of the women, ﴿are for evil men﴾, that is, of the men. ﴿And evil men are for evil women, and good women are for good men, and good men are for good women﴾, that is, in such a way that each one hardly passes beyond its own kind. And (*al-tayyib*, "the good"): the opposite of the *khabith* (the evil), and it is the best of everything, the finest and the most excellent.

Abu al-Su'ud said: Since the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was the best of the best and the choicest of the first and the last, it becomes clear by necessity that the Truthful One (*al-Siddiqah*), may Allah be pleased with her, is among the best of the good. The baselessness of what was said about her, of the fabrications, has become evident, as indicated by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those are free of what they say. For them is forgiveness and a generous provision﴾, which is Paradise. With this verse the account of the people of the slander (*ahl al-ifk*) was concluded. (p-4468)

Know that what these verses contain of rulings, benefits, objectives and etiquettes cannot be covered by volumes. However, we point to some of that, drawing from the most important references, to complete what we have summarized in its interpretation.

The first point: the account of the slander occurred in the expedition of al-Muraysi' (a diminutive of *marsu'*, a well or water belonging to Khuza'ah), and it was in Sha'ban of the fifth year (of the Hijrah). Its cause was that the Prophet (ﷺ) received word that al-Harith ibn Abi Dirar, the chief of Banu al-Mustaliq, had marched with his people and whoever among the Arabs he could gather, intending to make war on the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set out with those of his Companions who were with him. And with them went a group of the hypocrites who had not gone out on any campaign before it. He attacked them and took captive their children and their property.

'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, had gone out with him, peace be upon him, on this expedition, by a lot that fell to her, and that was his custom with his wives. When they returned from the expedition, they halted at some of the stopping places. 'A'ishah went out for her need, and she lost a necklace that belonged to her sister, which she had borrowed from her. She went back looking for it in the place where she had lost it, at that time. Then the men who used to load her howdah came and thought she was in it, so they lifted the howdah. They did not notice its lightness, because she, may Allah be pleased with her, was a young girl whose flesh had not yet come upon her, the flesh that would have made her heavy. Also, when the men cooperated in lifting the howdah, they did not notice its lightness; and if the one who lifted it had been one or two people, their condition would not have been hidden from them.

'A'ishah returned to their stopping place, and she had found the necklace, but there was no one to call or answer. She sat down in the place, thinking that they would miss her and come back looking for her. But Allah prevails over His affair; He manages the affair from above His Throne as He wills. So sleep overcame her eyes, and she did not wake until she heard the words of Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal (with a shaddah on the ta', from Salma, of the Dhakwan clan, a Companion, a distinguished man who was early in Islam): "Indeed we belong to Allah and to Him we return," the wife of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Safwan had lagged behind at the rear of the army, because he was a heavy sleeper, as came in his report in the *Sahih* of Abu Hatim and in the *Sunan*. When he saw her, he recognized her, for he used to see her before the veil was revealed. So he said the words of return, made his mount kneel, and brought it close to her, and she mounted it. He did not speak a single word to her, and she heard from him nothing but his words of return.

Then he led her on, leading the mount, until he came with her, and the army had halted at the height of midday. When the people saw that, each one of them spoke according to his nature and what was fitting for him. The vile one, the enemy of Allah, Ibn Ubayy, found an opening, so he breathed out from the distress of hypocrisy and envy that was between his ribs. He began to dig up the slander, to spread it, to broadcast it, to publicize it, to gather it and to scatter it. And his companions drew near to him. When they reached Madinah, the people of the slander spread the talk, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained silent and did not speak. Then he consulted his Companions about separating from her. 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, advised him to divorce her and take another, by way of allusion and not explicit statement. Usamah and others advised him to keep her and not to pay attention to the words of the enemies. 'Ali, seeing that what was said was doubtful, advised abandoning doubt and suspicion in favour of certainty, so that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would be relieved of the worry and grief that had befallen him from the people's talk. So he advised cutting out the disease. As for Usamah, when he knew the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) love for her and for her father, and when he knew of her chastity, innocence, purity and piety what was beyond that and greater than it, and when he knew of the honour of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with his Lord, his rank with Him, and his defence of him, that he would not place the mistress of his house, his beloved among women, and the daughter of his Siddiq, in the position into which the masters of the slander had placed her. And that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is more honoured by his Lord and more dear to Him than that He would put beneath him a lewd woman. And he knew that the Truthful One is the beloved of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and is more honoured by her Lord than that He would test her with indecency while she is under His Messenger.

Whoever's knowledge of Allah and knowledge of His Messenger and his estimation of him with Allah grows strong in his heart, will say, as Abu Ayyub and other chiefs of the Companions said when they heard that: ﴿Glory be to You, this is a tremendous slander﴾ [al-Nur: 16]. And reflect on what there is in their glorifying Allah and declaring Him free of imperfection in that situation, of knowledge of Him and of declaring Him free of what is unfitting for Him: that He would make for His Messenger, His intimate friend, and the most honoured of creation before Him, a vile, lewd woman. Whoever thinks this of Him, glory be to Him, has thought evil of Him. And the people of knowledge of Allah and His Messenger knew that a vile woman is only fit for a vile man like herself, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Evil women are for evil men﴾. So they were certain beyond any doubt that this was a tremendous slander and a manifest falsehood.

If it is said: Why did the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) hesitate about her matter, and ask about it, and investigate, and consult, while he is the best knower of Allah and of his rank with Him in what befits Him? Why did he not say, "Glory be to You, this is a tremendous slander," as the excellent Companions said? (p-4470)

The answer: This is part of the overwhelming wisdoms for which Allah made this story a cause, and a trial and a test for His Messenger (ﷺ) and for the whole Community until the Day of Resurrection, so that through this story He would raise some people and lower others. ﴿And Allah increases those who are guided in guidance and faith, and He does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss.﴾ The completion of the trial and the test required that the revelation be withheld from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for a month concerning her affair, so that he received no revelation about it at all, in order to complete His wisdom which He had decreed and ordained, and to manifest it in its most perfect form, and so that the believers who are truthful would increase in faith and steadfastness upon justice, truthfulness, good opinion of Allah and His Messenger and the people of his household and the righteous among His servants. And so that the hypocrites would increase in slander and hypocrisy, and so that their inner secrets would be manifest to the Messenger and the believers, and so that the servitude intended from the Truthful One and her father would be completed, and so that Allah's blessing upon them would be complete, and so that their need, their desire for Him, their dependence upon Allah, their humility before Him, their good opinion of Him, and their hope in Him would be intensified; and so that her hope from the created beings would be cut off, and she would despair of obtaining victory and relief at the hand of any of creation. For this reason He appointed this station its due: when her father said to her, "Stand up to him," while Allah had sent down His acquittal of her upon him, she said, "By Allah! I will not stand up to him, and I will praise none but Allah, who sent down my acquittal."

Also, among the wisdom of withholding the revelation for a month was that the matter had matured and come to a head, and the hearts of the believers were greatly eager, with the utmost longing, for what Allah would reveal to His Messenger concerning it. So the revelation came at the moment when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the people of his household, the Siddiq and his family, his Companions and the believers were most in need of it. It descended upon them like rain upon the earth when it is most needed. So it fell upon them in the greatest and most gracious way, and they were delighted with it with the utmost delight, and they attained complete happiness through it. Had Allah informed His Messenger of the true state of affairs from the very first moment, and sent down the revelation immediately about that, these wisdoms and their multiples, indeed multiples of multiples, would have been lost.

Also, Allah, glory be to Him, wished to show the rank of His Messenger and the people of his household among them, and his honour with Him: that He would remove His Messenger from this affair and Himself take up the defence and the protection of him, and the refutation of his enemies, (p-4471) and their blame and their condemnation for a matter in which he had no part and which was not attributed to him; rather He Himself would be the one who undertook that, avenging His Messenger and the people of his household.

Also, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was the one intended by the harm. The one whose wife was accused, it was not fitting that he should testify to her innocence, despite his knowledge, or his assumption approaching knowledge, of her innocence; he had never thought ill of her at all, far be it from him and far be it from her. For this reason, when he sought to be excused from the people of the slander, he said: "Who will excuse me regarding a man whose harm has reached me concerning my household? By Allah! I know nothing of my household but good. And they have mentioned a man of whom I know nothing but good. And he never entered upon my household except with me." So he had among the indications that testify to the innocence of the Truthful One more than the believers had. But because of his perfect patience, steadfastness, gentleness, good opinion of his Lord, and trust in Him, he fulfilled the station of patience, steadfastness and good opinion of Allah its due, until the revelation came with what gladdened his eye, delighted his heart, magnified his rank, and made manifest to his community the regard of his Lord for him and His care for his affair.

When the revelation came with her innocence, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered that those who had openly spread the slander be given the prescribed punishment, eighty lashes each. But the vile one, 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy, was not given the prescribed punishment, although he was the head of the slander. It was said: Because the prescribed punishments (*hudud*) are a lightening for their recipients and an expiation, and the vile one is not fit for that. And Allah has promised him a great punishment in the Hereafter, so that will suffice him instead of the prescribed punishment. And it was said: Rather, he used to dig up the talk, gather it and relate it, and put it into forms that do not come from one who is related to him. And it was said: The prescribed punishment for false accusation (*qadhf*) is not established except by confession or evidence. He did not confess to the accusation, and no one testified against him, for he only used to mention it among his companions, and they did not testify against him, and he did not mention it among the believers. And it was said: The punishment for false accusation is a right of the human being; it is not exacted except upon the demand of the one wronged, and 'A'ishah did not demand it from Ibn Ubayy. And it was said: Rather, he was left unpunished for a benefit greater than carrying it out, just as the Prophet left his execution despite the manifest nature of his hypocrisy and his speaking words that deserved his execution repeatedly; the benefit being the winning over of his people and not repelling them from Islam, for he was obeyed among them and was their chief. So there was no assurance that carrying out the punishment would stir up strife. And perhaps he was left for all these reasons together.

So Mistah ibn Uthathah, Hassan ibn Thabit and Hamnah bint Jahsh were given the prescribed punishment. These were among the truthful believers, for their purification and expiation. And the enemy of Allah, Ibn Ubayy, was left; so he is not among the people of that. (p-4472) This is what Imam Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, stated in *Zad al-Ma'ad*, and it is the essence of the reports on this subject.

Then he (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Whoever reflects on the words of al-Siddiqa (the truthful one, i.e., 'A'isha), when her innocence had been revealed and her father said to her, "Stand up and go to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)," and she said, "By Allah! I will not stand up to him, and I will praise none but Allah," will recognize her knowledge of Allah, the strength of her faith, her attribution of the blessing to her Lord, her singling out of Allah alone for praise in that situation, her renewal of tawhid (affirmation of Allah's oneness), the firmness of her heart, and her confidence in the innocence of her good name. She had not done anything that would require her to stand before him as one who seeks reconciliation and asks for it. Because she was confident of the love of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for her, she said what she said, as an expression of intimacy (idlal) toward the beloved by the beloved, especially in such a situation, which is the finest of the situations in which one may express such intimacy, and she placed it in its proper place. By Allah, how beloved she was to him when she said, "I praise none but Allah, for it is He who sent down my innocence." By Allah, that steadfastness and dignity on her part, which was the thing most beloved to her, and for which she had no patience, even though the heart of her beloved had been estranged from her for a month. Then she met his acceptance and his turning toward her, and she did not rush to stand up before him, or to rejoice in his good pleasure and nearness, despite her intense love for him. This is the utmost of steadfastness and strength. End of quotation.

* *

The chains of the hadith of the slander (hadith al-ifk) are numerous, related from Umm al-Mu'minin 'A'isha, from Ibn al-Zubayr, Umm Ruman, Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Hurayra and Abu al-Yusr. Ten of the Successors (tabi'un) related it, as in (Fath al-Bari), and it appears in the Musnads, the Sahih collections, the Sunan and others, some in full and some in summary. Of the summarized versions is what Imam Ahmad transmitted from Umm Ruman, who said: "While I was with 'A'isha, a woman of the Ansar entered upon her and said, 'May Allah do such-and-such to her son.' 'A'isha said, 'Why?' She said, 'He was among those who spread the report.' She said, 'And what report?' She said, 'Such-and-such.' She said, 'Has that reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?' She said, 'Yes.' She said, 'And has it reached Abu Bakr?' She said, 'Yes.' So 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, fell down in a faint. When she recovered, she had a fever with shivering. She said, 'I got up and covered her.' She said: Then the Prophet (ﷺ) came and said, 'What is the matter with her?' I said, 'O Messenger of Allah, she has been taken by a fever with shivering.' He said, 'Perhaps it is because of a report that has been spoken of?' She said: 'A'isha sat up and said, 'By Allah, if I swear to you, you will not believe me, and if I offer an excuse to you, you will not accept my excuse. My case and yours is like that of Ya'qub and his sons when he said: ﴿So patience is most fitting, and Allah is the One whose help is sought against what you describe﴾ [Yusuf: 18].'" She said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out, and Allah sent down her innocence. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned with Abu Bakr accompanying him, entered and said, "O 'A'isha! Allah the Exalted has sent down your innocence." She said, "Praise be to Allah, not to you." Abu Bakr said to her, "Do you say this to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?" She said, "Yes."

She said: Among those who spread this report was a man whom Abu Bakr supported. He swore that he would no longer give him anything, so Allah the Exalted sent down: ﴿And let not those of virtue and wealth among you swear not to give﴾ [al-Nur: 22], to the end of the verse. Abu Bakr said, "Yes, indeed," and he continued to give him. Al-Bukhari alone transmitted it.

The second point: In (al-Iklil) on the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who came with the slander﴾ [al-Nur: 11], it is said that it was revealed concerning the innocence of 'A'isha from what she was accused of. The jurists therefore used it as evidence that one who slanders her is to be killed, because he denies the explicit text of the Qur'an. The scholars said: slandering 'A'isha is disbelief, because Allah glorified Himself when mentioning it, saying: ﴿Glory be to You! This is a great slander﴾ [al-Nur: 16], just as He glorified Himself when mentioning what the polytheists attributed to Him of a spouse and offspring. And in His words: ﴿Why, when you heard it, did the believing men and believing women not think good of one another?﴾ [al-Nur: 12], there is the prohibition of thinking ill, and that one may not judge on the basis of suspicion, and that one known for righteousness is not to be turned away from it by the report of an informant, and that the slanderer is rejected in the Sharia unless he produces witnesses. And in His words: ﴿Indeed, those who love that indecency should spread among the believers﴾ [al-Nur: 19], to the end of the verse, there is an exhortation to conceal the believer and not to expose him. Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, who said: Whoever reports what his eyes have seen and his ears have heard is among those who love that indecency should spread among those who believe. He also transmitted from 'Ata', who said: Whoever spreads indecency deserves punishment, even if he is truthful.

He also transmitted from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Zakariyya that he was asked about this verse and said: It is the man in whose presence something is said about another man, so he desires that and does not object to it.

In His words: ﴿And let not those of virtue and wealth among you swear not to give﴾ [al-Nur: 22], to the end of the verse, there is a prohibition against swearing not to do good, and that whoever swears an oath and then sees something other than it to be better, it is recommended for him to break the oath. It also contains the command to pardon and forgive.

Those who hold that His words: ﴿Indeed, those who accuse chaste, unaware, believing women﴾ [al-Nur: 23], to the end of the verse, were revealed specifically concerning the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ), use it as evidence that their slanderer is to be killed if no repentance is mentioned for him, as I have mentioned concerning the slanderer of others at the beginning of the surah. End of quotation.

Ibn Kathir said: Some have held that it is specific to 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, but the correct view is that the verse is general to all believing women, and the Mothers of the Believers enter into it in the first place, especially she who was the occasion of its revelation, 'A'isha.

Ibn Kathir said: The scholars, may Allah have mercy on them all, have unanimously agreed that whoever reviles her after what is mentioned in this verse is a disbeliever, because he opposes the Qur'an. Regarding the remaining Mothers of the Believers there are two opinions, the more sound of which is that they are the same as her. And Allah knows best.

The third point: Imam Ibn Taymiyya said concerning the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Wicked women are for wicked men, and wicked men are for wicked women﴾, to the end of the verse: Allah the Exalted informed that wicked women are for wicked men, so there is no wicked woman for a righteous man, for that would contradict the restriction. And He informed that righteous men are for righteous women, so there is no righteous man for a wicked woman, for that would contradict the restriction, since He stated that all wicked women are for wicked men. So there remains no wicked woman for a righteous man, nor a righteous man for a wicked woman. And He informed that all righteous women are for righteous men, so there remains no righteous woman for a wicked man. Thus the restriction came from both sides, in agreement with His words: ﴿The adulterer does not marry except an adulteress or a polytheist﴾ [al-Nur: 3], to the end of the verse. For this reason some of the early scholars (salaf) said: No wife of a prophet ever committed adultery, since the beginning of this surah was revealed concerning the people of the slander.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 24, verse 26 (part 3 of 7):

For this reason, when it became a matter of suspicion, the Prophet (ﷺ) consulted about divorcing her (p-4475), since it is not fitting for him to have a wife who is not good. It has been related that: "No cuckold (dayyuth) enters Paradise," and the dayyuth is the one who tolerates evil in his household. For this reason, jealousy (ghayra) over unchastity is among the things that Allah loves and has commanded. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do you wonder at the jealousy of Sa'd? I am more jealous than he is, and Allah is more jealous than I am." For this reason He forbade the indecencies, whether apparent or hidden. For this reason Allah permitted the accuser (qadhif) who is a husband to perform li'an (mutual oaths of cursing), because of what he was commanded regarding jealousy, and because she has corrupted his bed. If she conceived from unlawful intercourse, then li'an is obligatory for him, lest someone who is not his be attributed to him. The Sunnah (the prophetic tradition and practice) has established separation between them, whether the separation occurs through mutual cursing, or through a judge, or upon the completion of the husband's li'an, because one of them is cursed or wicked, and their union requires the joining of the wicked with the good.

In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Imran concerning the she-camel that a woman cursed, he commanded that what was on her be taken and that she be released, and he said: "No cursed she-camel shall accompany us." When he passed by the dwellings of Thamud, he said: "Do not enter upon these punished people unless you are weeping, lest what befell them befall you." So he forbade crossing their dwellings except in a state of fear that prevents punishment. Likewise is the Sunnah regarding associating with the wrongdoers, the adulterers, the people of innovation (bid'ah), the sinful, and all other sins. It is not proper for anyone to associate with them or mix with them except in a manner by which he is saved from the punishment of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. The least of that is that he be one who denounces their wrongdoing, who hates them and detests what they are engaged in, to the extent that he is able.

This is as in His saying: "Whoever among you sees an evil, let him change it with his hand..." etc. And the Exalted said: ﴿Allah has struck a parable for those who believe: the wife of Pharaoh﴾ [At-Tahrim: 11], and the verse goes on. Likewise is what He mentioned about Joseph and his work for the lord of Egypt among a disbelieving people. The matter is that a believer engages in associating with disbelievers only in two situations. The first: that he is compelled to it. The second: that there is in it a religious benefit that outweighs the harm of the association, or that leaving it would involve a greater harm to his religion, so he repels the greater of the two harms by accepting the lesser, and the preponderant benefit is achieved by accepting the lesser harm. In reality, the one who is compelled is the one who repels corruption by accepting the lesser of the two, and this is the matter to which he is compelled. The Exalted said: ﴿except one who is compelled while his heart remains firm in faith﴾ [An-Nahl: 106]. And the Exalted said: ﴿And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution﴾ [An-Nur: 33]. And the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves﴾ [An-Nisa: 97], up to His saying: ﴿Pardoning, Forgiving﴾ [An-Nisa: 99]. And He said: ﴿What is [the matter] with you that you do not fight in the cause of Allah and for the oppressed among men and women and children?﴾ [An-Nisa: 75].

The verse indicates the prohibition of marrying an adulterer, and marriage is a particular type of companionship. Marriage in the original linguistic sense is coition (al-mujama'a). When a marriage contract is concluded between them, their hearts are joined and there arises between them a mutual affection that did not exist before. For this reason, it establishes the prohibition of affinity (hurmat al-musaharah) in matters other than the stepdaughter (rabiba), merely by that, in inheritance, in the waiting period of widowhood, and in other matters. The middle level of that is their being together alone in one place, which is the cohabitation that confirms the dowry (mahr), as the caliphs issued legal opinions. The last level is the joining of intercourse. And this, even if it occurs without a marriage contract, is a weak union, and the joining of hearts is greater than the mere joining of two bodies in fornication. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And good women are for good men﴾ indicates this both in meaning and in wording. It also indicates the prohibition of associating with the immoral and marrying them, as other texts also indicate this, such as His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their spouses﴾ [As-Saffat: 22], meaning their counterparts and their likes.

Zawaj (pairing, spouse) is more general than the known nikah (marriage). The Exalted said: ﴿or He pairs them with males and females﴾ [Ash-Shura: 50]. And He said: ﴿of every beautiful pair﴾ [Al-Hajj: 5]. And He said: ﴿And when souls are paired﴾ [At-Takwir: 7]. And He said: ﴿And of everything We created two mates﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 49]. And He said: ﴿And We created you in pairs﴾ [An-Naba: 8]. And He said: ﴿Indeed, among your spouses and your children are enemies to you﴾ [At-Taghabun: 14]. Although the verse has explicit reference to the wife who is the companion and to the child born of her, the meaning is: in every similar and associate, in every type and follower. ﴿Say: Praise be to Allah, who has not taken a son and has not had a partner in dominion﴾ [Al-Isra: 111], ﴿Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant﴾ [Al-Furqan: 1], the two verses.

Thus companionship, affinity, and brotherhood are not permissible except with obedience to Allah according to His will. This is indicated by the hadith in the Sunan: "Do not keep company except with a believer, and let none eat your food except a pious person." And in them also: "A person follows the religion of his close friend, so let each of you look at whom he befriends." And in the Two Sahihs, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah: "If the slave girl of one of you commits adultery, let him inflict the prescribed punishment (hadd) upon her," up to his saying: "Then if she commits adultery again, let him sell her, even for a rope (dafir)." The dafir is a rope, and this is a command to sell her even for the least of what could be exchanged for her. Ahmad said: "If he does not sell her, he is one who has abandoned the command of the Prophet (ﷺ)." The slave girls who do this, most of them are for service. So how about a slave girl taken for enjoyment (umm al-tamattu')? And if it is obligatory to remove an adulterous slave girl from his ownership, how about an adulterous wife? The male slave is the equivalent of the female slave, by his saying (ﷺ): "Allah curses whoever shelters an innovator (muhdith)." This requires the curse upon everyone who shelters an innovator, whether his innovation is by adultery, theft, or otherwise, and whether the sheltering is by right of ownership, or by marriage, or otherwise, because the least of what is in it is abandoning the denunciation of the evil.

The believer needs to test whoever he wishes to keep company with or be connected to, through marriage and otherwise. The Exalted said: ﴿When believing women come to you as emigrants, test them﴾ [Al-Mumtahanah: 10]. Likewise, a woman with whom a man has committed adultery: he does not marry her except after repentance, according to the most correct opinion, as the Book, the Sunnah, and the reports indicate. However, if he wishes to test her, to see whether her repentance is sound, Ibn Umar said: he solicits her. If she responds to him, her repentance is not valid; if she does not respond, then she has repented. Ahmad explicitly stated this. It was said: this involves seeking the indecency, and she may break her repentance, and his own self may command him to accomplish that, and Satan may adorn it for him, especially if he loves her and she loves him and they have tasted each other. Whoever holds the first view says: a matter aimed at testing her is not a command to do what Allah has forbidden. He may avoid seeking the indecency and instead make an allusion (ta'rid), and allusion for a need is permissible, even obligatory in many situations. As for her breaking it: if it is permissible for her to break her repentance with him, it is permissible for her to break it with another. What is intended is that she be unwilling toward the one who solicits her. As for Satan's adorning the act for him, this falls under every good deed a person does in which he finds a trial. So when a believer wishes to keep company with someone who has been reported to be immoral, and it was said that he repented, or that this was said about him truthfully or falsely, he tests him by means of what reveals his righteousness or his immorality. Likewise, when he wishes to appoint someone to a position, he tests him, as Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz commanded his servant to test the son of Abu Musa, when he was impressed by his bearing. He said to him: "You know my standing with the Commander of the Faithful. How much will you give me if I recommend you to him for an appointment?" So he offered him a great sum of money, and he knew that he was not one fit for the position. Likewise in dealings. Likewise with boys and slaves who are known for, or said to be given to, immorality, and a man wishes to buy one: he tests him. Knowledge of people's conditions is sometimes through the testimony of people, sometimes through the evaluation of narrators (al-jarh wa al-ta'dil), and sometimes through examination and testing.

* *

Then Ibn Taymiyya, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Just as Allah magnified the indecency, He magnified its mention in falsehood, which is qadhf (false accusation). So He said after that: ﴿And those who accuse chaste women and then do not produce four witnesses, lash them with eighty lashes﴾ [An-Nur: 4], the verse. Then He mentioned a man's accusation of his wife and what He commanded in it of mutual cursing. Then He mentioned the story of the people of the slander (ifk) and explained what good is in it for the one accused, and what sin is in it for the accuser, and what is obligatory upon believers when they hear such a thing: that they should think well of their believing brothers and say: ﴿This is a clear lie﴾, because its evidence is an obvious falsehood. Then He informed that it is a statement without proof, and said: ﴿Why did they not bring four witnesses for it? When they did not bring the witnesses, they are the liars in the sight of Allah﴾ [An-Nur: 13]. Then He informed that were it not for His grace and mercy upon them, He would have punished them for what they said. His saying: ﴿When you received it with your tongues and said with your mouths what you had no knowledge of﴾ [An-Nur: 15] is an explanation of the cause of the punishment: it is receiving falsehood with the tongues and speaking with the mouths. These are two forbidden things: speaking falsehood and speaking without knowledge. Then He, glorified be He, said: ﴿Why, when you heard it, did you not say, "It is not for us to speak of this; glory be to You, this is a great slander"?﴾ [An-Nur: 16].

So the first is an exhortation to think well, and this is a prohibition for them against speaking slander. In the first, there is His saying: ﴿Avoid much of suspicion, for indeed some suspicion is sin﴾ [Al-Hujurat: 12], and His saying (ﷺ): "Beware of suspicion, for suspicion is the most false of speech." And His saying: ﴿The believing men and believing women thought well of their own people﴾ [An-Nur: 12] is evidence for the goodness of this kind of thinking which Allah commanded.

In the Sahih, there is his saying to Aishah: "I do not think that so-and-so and so-and-so understand anything of our religion" (?). This indicates the permissibility of some suspicion, as al-Bukhari argued from it. But with knowledge of what the Muslim person has of faith, which deters him from committing indecency, it is obligatory to think well of him rather than ill. In the verse there is a prohibition against receiving such a thing with the tongue, and a prohibition against a person saying what he has no knowledge of, because of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge﴾ [Al-Isra: 36].

Allah has placed for committing indecency and for slander a punishment that He did not place for any other sin. He prescribed for it stoning, and the people of Lot were stoned when they were the first to commit the indecency of sodomy. He made the punishment for the one who falsely accuses of it eighty lashes, while accusing of other things involves discretion (ijtihad). It is permissible, according to some scholars, for it to reach eighty, as Ali said: "I will not be brought a man who prefers me over Abu Bakr and Umar except that I will lash him the punishment for the slanderer." And as Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf said: "When he drinks, he raves; and when he raves, he slanders." The punishment for drinking is eighty, and the punishment for the slanderer is eighty.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who love that indecency should spread among those who believe will have a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter﴾ [An-Nur: 19]. This is a censure of whoever loves that. This may occur through the title alone, and it may occur along with that by tongue and by limbs. It is a censure of whoever speaks of it or reports it, out of love for its occurrence among the believers, whether out of envy or hatred, or out of love for the indecency itself. So everyone who loves its occurrence mentions it.

The scholars disliked amatory poetry (ghazal) that encourages it. Likewise, mentioning it as backbiting (ghiba) of a forbidden kind is prohibited, whether in verse or in prose. Likewise, likening someone to one who commits it is forbidden, just as commanding it is. For the act is sought sometimes by command and sometimes by report. These two matters concern the sinful adulterers and sodomites, just as mentioning the stories of the prophets and the righteous concerns believers. Those learn from the jealousy through them, and these learn from the deceptions. For the people of disbelief, wickedness, and disobedience mention from the stories of their like what provides them an example in it.

[p. 4480]

Among that is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And among people is one who buys idle talk﴾ [Luqman: 6], and so on. It has been said that He meant singing (ghina'). It has also been said that He meant the stories of the kings of the disbelievers. In sum, whatever encourages souls to obedience and restrains them from disobedience is part of obedience. Whatever encourages disobedience and restrains from obedience is part of disobedience. As for mentioning indecency (fahisha) and its people in a manner that the Sharia requires or recommends, such as forbidding it and forbidding them, condemning it and condemning them, and mentioning its people in general terms where that is permissible, whether in their presence or in their absence, then this is good; it is sometimes obligatory and sometimes recommended. Thus God related the stories of the believers and the wicked, so that they might take lessons from both.

God has mentioned, concerning His prophets and His righteous servants, something of the mention of indecency and its associations, in the manner of condemnation, and in it there is a lesson. He said, exalted is He: ﴿And Lot, when he said to his people, "Do you commit the abomination?"﴾ [al-A'raf: 80], and so on, in several places. There is in this a degree of reproach, but it is not of the kind of slander and defamation. Then they threatened him with expulsion from the town. This is the condition of the people of corruption: when among them is one who forbids them, they seek to expel him. God punished the sin of the people of Lot with what they had intended to inflict upon the people of piety, for He ordered the banishment of the adulterer and the effeminate man. Thus the Sunna was established, banishing this one and that one. He, glorified and exalted is He, removed the righteous from among them when the punishment descended. Likewise is what He mentioned in the story of Joseph, in His saying: ﴿And she, in whose house he was, sought [to seduce] him from himself﴾ [Yusuf: 23], up to His saying: ﴿So He turned away from him their plotting. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing﴾ [Yusuf: 34]; and what He mentioned after it of Joseph's saying: ﴿What is the matter with the women who cut their hands?﴾ [Yusuf: 50]. This is of the kind of consideration (i'tibar) that necessitates aversion from disobedience and adherence to piety. Likewise is what He made clear at its end, in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿There has certainly been in their stories a lesson for those of understanding﴾ [Yusuf: 111], and so on. Nevertheless, among people there are those who love to hear it because of what it contains of the mention of passionate love and what is connected with it, out of their love for that and their desire for indecency. Some of them even have it recited to women out of their love for evil, and they do not choose to hear what is in Surat al-Nur of punishment and prohibition of that. So much so that one of the early pious predecessors (salaf) said: "Everything I acquired from Surat Yusuf I spent on Surat al-Nur."

God, exalted is He, has said: ﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is healing and mercy for the believers, but it increases the wrongdoers in nothing but loss﴾ [al-Isra': 82]. And He said: ﴿And whenever a surah is revealed, among them are those who say, "Which of you has had his faith increased by this?"﴾ [al-Tawba: 124], and the verses that follow. Everyone loves to hear that which stirs up blameworthy love, and dislikes hearing that which stirs it, turning away from repelling this love; so this is blameworthy. Of this kind is the mention of the conditions of the disbelievers and the wicked and other things that contain encouragement to disobedience and obstruction from the way of God. Of it also is the hearing of the words of the people of innovation (ahl al-bid'a), and looking into their books for one whom that harms. This category gathers together doubts (shubuhat) and desires (shahawat).
