God condemned these people in such sayings as: ﴿Some of them inspire to others decorated speech as deception﴾ [al-An'am: 112]; His saying: ﴿As for poets, the deviators follow them﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 224]; His saying: ﴿Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend?﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 221] and what follows it; His saying: ﴿And among people is one who buys idle talk﴾ [Luqman: 6]; His saying: ﴿Scorning it, talking nonsense by night﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 67]; His saying: ﴿And if they see the way of right conduct, they will not take it as a way; but if they see the way of error, they will take it as a way﴾ [al-A'raf: 146]; and His saying: ﴿And if you obey most of those on earth﴾ [al-An'am: 116]. Similar to this in the Qur'an is much. The people of sin are many in the world; indeed, they are the majority, as God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if you obey most of those on earth, they will lead you astray from the way of God﴾ [al-An'am: 116], and so on. In souls there are blameworthy doubts and desires, in speech and in action, that none knows except God. Their people call others to them and subdue whoever disobeys them, and they adorn them for whoever obeys them. They are the enemies of the messengers and their rivals. The messengers call to obedience by means of hope and fear, and they struggle against those who oppose it. They forbid sins and warn against them by means of hope and fear, and they struggle against those who commit them. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿The hypocrites, men and women, are of one another; they enjoin what is evil (munkar) and forbid what is good (ma'ruf)﴾ [al-Tawba: 67], and so on. Then He said: ﴿The believing men and believing women are allies of one another; they enjoin what is good and forbid what is evil﴾ [al-Tawba: 71], and so on. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those who believe fight in the way of God, and those who disbelieve fight in the way of Taghut﴾ [al-Nisa': 76]. Similar to this in the Qur'an is much. God, glorified is He, has commanded us to enjoin what is good and forbid what is evil. Commanding a thing is preceded by knowledge of it, so whoever does not know what is good cannot enjoin what is good. Forbidding what is evil is preceded by knowledge of it, so whoever does not know it cannot forbid it.

* *

God has made it obligatory upon us to do what is good and to abandon what is evil. The love of a thing and doing it, and the hatred of that and abandoning it, do not occur except after knowledge of both, so that the intention to do what is good and abandon what is evil may be sound. For that is preceded by knowledge of it. Whoever does not know a thing cannot be conceived as loving it or hating it, nor as doing it or abandoning it. But doing a thing and commanding it requires that one know it in detail, such that one can do it and command it when it is commanded in detail. For this reason God made it obligatory upon man to know what he is commanded to do of the obligations, such as the manner of prayer, fasting, pilgrimage, struggle (jihad), and enjoining what is good and forbidding what is evil. When one is commanded with attributes, there must be knowledge of their existence. Just as we are not obedient when we know the absence of obedience, so we are not obedient when we do not know its presence. Indeed, ignorance of its presence is like knowledge of its absence, and each of them is disobedience. For ignorance of equality is like knowledge of excess in the exchange of usurious (ribawi) wealth.

As for knowing what one abandons and forbids, one may in some places suffice with knowing it in summary. For a person needs to know the evil and to reject it. He may need proofs that clarify this, and a response to what its adherents raise in opposition, and a repelling of their desires. That requires a firm will and the capacity for it, and this cannot be achieved except through patience, as God, exalted is He, said: ﴿By time﴾ [al-Asr: 1], ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾ [al-Asr: 2], ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds and advise each other to truth and advise each other to patience﴾ [al-Asr: 3]. The first step in this is that sayings and deeds be mentioned in the manner of condemning them and forbidding them, and clarifying the corruption within them. For rejection by the heart and tongue precedes rejection by hand. This is the method of the Qur'an in what it mentions of the disbelievers and the disobedient. Just as, in what the people of knowledge and faith mention, in the manner of praise, love, clarifying its benefit, and encouraging it, there is the like of His saying: ﴿And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son."﴾ [Maryam: 88] ﴿You have certainly produced a monstrous thing﴾ [Maryam: 89], and the verses that follow. This is very abundant. Whoever loves their sayings and their deeds is one of them, either a disbeliever or a wicked person. There is none among them who is the opposite of this. But one is not rewarded merely for the absence of that; rather, one is rewarded for intending to abandon it and wanting to abandon it. That is preceded by knowledge of the ugliness of that and hatred of it for God's sake. This knowledge, intention, and hatred are part of the faith for which one is rewarded, and it is the lowest level of faith, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever among you sees an evil..." up to his saying: "...and that is the weakest of faith." Changing the heart occurs through hating that and disliking it, and that does not occur except after knowledge of it and of its ugliness.

After that, rejection occurs by the tongue, and then by the hand. The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "and that is the weakest of faith" regarding one who sees an evil. But if one sees it and does not know that it is an evil, and does not dislike it, then this faith is not present in the heart at the time of its existence and its sighting, in such a way that its hatred and dislike are obligatory. Knowledge of its ugliness necessitates fighting the disbelievers and hypocrites when they are present. When the evil is not present, that is not obligatory, and whoever rejects it when it exists is rewarded, but whoever is not confronted with it is not rewarded until he rejects it. Likewise, among what enters into this of sayings, deeds, and evils, many people turn away from them, just as they turn away from fighting the disbelievers and hypocrites, and from enjoining what is good and forbidding what is evil. These people, even if they are among the emigrants (muhajirun) who abandoned evil deeds, are not among the strugglers (mujahidun) who strive to remove them, so that there may be no tumult (fitna) and the religion may be entirely for God. So reflect upon this, for often these two matters gather together in many people: hatred of disbelief and its people, and hatred of wickedness and its people, together with hatred of forbidding them and striving against them, just as one loves what is good and its people, yet does not love to command it, nor to strive for it with self and wealth. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿The believers are only those who believe in God and His Messenger and then do not doubt and strive with their wealth and their selves in the way of God. Those are the truthful﴾ [al-Hujurat: 15]. He said: ﴿Say, "If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your spouses, your kindred, the wealth you have acquired, the commerce you fear will decline, and the dwellings you are pleased with are dearer to you than God and His Messenger and striving in His way..."﴾ [al-Tawba: 24], and the verse. He said: ﴿You will not find a people who believe in God and the Last Day loving those who oppose God and His Messenger, even if they were their fathers or their sons or their brothers or their kindred﴾ [al-Mujadila: 22]. Many people, indeed most of them, dislike striving against evils more than they dislike the evils themselves, especially when evils are abundant and doubts and desires are strong among them. So they sometimes incline toward them and at other times turn away from them. Thus the soul of one of them becomes self-reproaching (lawwama) after having been commanding to evil (ammara).

[p. 4485]

[p. 4485]

Then, when he ascends to the higher state of abandoning misdeeds, and his soul becomes tranquil, leaving off what is forbidden and what is disliked, but he does not love jihad (striving, including fighting, in the way of God) or steadfastness against the enemy in that cause, or bearing what harms him of words and deeds, then this is another matter, included in His words: ﴿Have you not seen those to whom it was said, "Restrain your hands"?﴾ (4:77) up to His words: ﴿And God is ever Sufficient over all things⁠﻿⁠﻿ (4:85). Shafa'a (intercession) means aid, for the one who aids has become an intercessor for the one who is aided. Thus, whoever aids in righteousness and piety has a share of it, and whoever aids in sin and transgression bears a portion of it. This is the condition of people in what they do with their hearts, their tongues, and their hands, by aiding in righteousness and piety and aiding in sin and transgression. Among this is jihad with the self and wealth in that cause, from both sides, as God, exalted is He, said before that: ﴿O you who believe, take your precautions﴾ (4:71) up to His words: ﴿Indeed, the plot of Satan is ever weak﴾ (4:76).

Here the distinction appears in hearing and sight, between faith and its effects and disbelief and its effects, and the distinction between the believer and the disbelieving wicked. The believers hear of the coming of the people of faith, and they witness their appearance with knowledge, recognition, love, and veneration for them and for their reports and their traces, like the Companions' seeing the Prophet (ﷺ) and hearing what he conveyed to them from God. The disbeliever and the hypocrite hear and see with hatred and ignorance, as God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes when they hear the Reminder﴾ (68:51), the verse. And He said: ﴿But when a decisive surah is sent down and fighting is mentioned therein, you see those in whose hearts is a disease looking at you with the look of one fainting from death﴾ (47:20). And He said: ﴿They were not able to hear, nor did they see﴾ (11:20). And He said: ﴿They were blind and deaf; then God turned to them; then many of them became blind and deaf again﴾ (5:71). And God, exalted is He, said concerning the believers: ﴿And those who, when reminded of the verses of their Lord, do not fall upon them deaf and blind﴾ (25:73). And He said concerning the disbelievers: ﴿So what is wrong with them that they turn away from the reminder?﴾ (74:49). The verses on this are very numerous.

Likewise, looking at the adornment of this world is a trial. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And do not extend your eyes toward what We have given to pairs of them as the splendor of the worldly life, that We may test them therein﴾ (20:131), and at the end of Al-Hijr. And His words: ﴿So let not their wealth nor their children impress you﴾ (9:55). And He said: ﴿Say to the believers that they should lower their gaze﴾ (24:30), the verse. And He said: ﴿And do not let your eyes pass over them, desiring the adornment of the worldly life﴾ (18:28), the verse. And He said: ﴿Do they not look at the camels, how they were created?﴾ (88:17), the verses. And He said: ﴿Say, "Look at what is in the heavens and the earth"﴾ (10:101), the verse. And He said: ﴿Have they not looked at what is before them and behind them of the heaven and the earth?﴾ (34:9), the verse. Likewise Satan said: ﴿Indeed, I see what you do not see﴾ (8:48). And He said: ﴿Then when the two hosts saw each other﴾ (26:61), the verses. And He said: ﴿When God showed them to you in your dream as few﴾ (8:43), the verses.

So looking at the goods of this world with love and veneration for them and their people is forbidden. Looking at the upper and lower creations with contemplation (i'tibar) is commanded. As for seeing those things at the time of jihad, enjoining good and forbidding evil, to repel the evil of those people, this is commanded. Likewise, the seeing of contemplation is legislated in general. So one eye may be directed at something in a way that is commanded, either for contemplation or for hatred of that thing, and looking at it out of hatred of jihad is forbidden. Likewise, loyalty and enmity. A servant may be afflicted with a trial through a forbidden look while he thinks it is a look of contemplation. And he may be commanded to jihad and think that this is a look of trial, like those about whom God said: ﴿And among them is one who says, "Give me permission and do not put me to trial"﴾ (9:49). It was revealed concerning Jadd ibn Qays when the Prophet (ﷺ) commanded him to prepare for the expedition against the Byzantines, and he said: "I am infatuated with women, and I fear the trial of the women of the Byzantines." This and similar things occur by way of speech with the tongue.

As for what occurs by way of action with the limbs, every deed that involves love for indecency to spread among those who believe is included in this. Rather, its punishment will be greater, for God has threatened punishment for mere love. This may not be accompanied by speech or action, so how much more when it is accompanied? Rather, a person must hate what God, exalted is He, has hated of committing indecency, slandering with it, and spreading it among those who believe. Whoever is pleased with the deed of a people will be gathered with them, just as the wife of Lot was gathered with them, though she did not commit the indecency of sodomy, since that does not occur from a woman. But because she was pleased with their deed, the punishment encompassed her along with them. From this category it is said: whoever aids in indecency and its spread, like the pimp, because of the leadership, nobility, or illicit gain he obtains. Likewise the people of trades that generate income, such as singers, wine-drinkers, those who farm out government revenue departments, and others, for they love that indecency spread among those who believe. For when it spreads, they gain power over their aims of leadership, wealth, and committing indecency, and they gain power to repel whoever disapproves of it, unlike when it is rare.

There is no disagreement among the Muslims that what calls to disobedience of God and forbids obedience to Him is forbidden and unlawful. As God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing, and the remembrance of God is greater﴾ (29:45), meaning: what is in it of the remembrance of God, obedience to Him, and carrying out His command is greater than that. And He said concerning wine and gambling: ﴿And it hinders you from the remembrance of God and from prayer﴾ (5:91), meaning: that brings you into His disobedience, which is enmity and hatred. This is among the greatest of the wrongs that prayer forbids. Wine calls to indecency and wrongdoing, as is the reality. For the wine-drinker's self calls him to intercourse, whether lawful or unlawful. God, glorified is He, did not mention intercourse, because wine does not call to the specific unlawful intercourse. Intoxication removes the intellect by which one distinguishes between the lawful and the unlawful, and sound intellect forbids committing what is unlawful. For this reason the wine-drinker commits indecencies far more than others, to the point that he may fall upon his daughter, son, and close relatives. He may be content with the lawful if it is available to him. And drinking wine calls to taking people's wealth by theft, highway robbery, and other means, because he needs wine and what accompanies it of food and other things, and other indecencies and singing. Drinking wine also reveals men's secrets, so that its drinker speaks what is in his inner self. Many people, when they want to learn the secrets in men's hearts, give them wine, and sometimes they drink with them what does not intoxicate them. Moreover, wine turns a person away from his knowledge and his management. So all the matters that turn him away from these and bring about corruption are included in His words, exalted is He: ﴿And it hinders you from the remembrance of God and from prayer﴾ (5:91). Likewise, bringing about enmity and hatred is the ultimate aim of Satan. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Shall I not inform you of something better than the rank of prayer, fasting, and charity, and enjoining good and forbidding evil?" They said: "Yes, O Messenger of God." He said: "Reconciling between people, for the corruption of relations is the shaver; I do not say it shaves hair, but it shaves religion."

We have mentioned elsewhere that indecencies, wrongdoing, and other sins bring about enmity and hatred, and that every enmity or hatred has its root in disobedience, and Satan commands disobedience in order to bring about what is greater than it, and he is not content except with the utmost he is able to achieve. Moreover, enmity and hatred are pure evil, which no rational person loves, unlike sins, for in them there is pleasure. Souls desire them, and Satan calls to them, so as to bring the soul into an evil it does not desire. God, glorified is He, has explained what Satan intends by wine and gambling, but He did not mention what a human being intends. Then He said in Surat al-Nur: ﴿Do not follow the steps of Satan; whoever follows the steps of Satan, indeed he enjoins immorality and wrongdoing﴾ (24:21). Likewise, in Al-Baqarah He forbade following his steps, which means following his command by taking him as a model and following him. And He informed that he commands indecency, wrongdoing, evil, and speaking against God without knowledge. And He said in it: ﴿Satan threatens you with poverty and commands you to immorality﴾ (2:268). So He mentioned that Satan commands that. And after this: ﴿And God promises you forgiveness from Him and bounty﴾ (2:268). And He said: ﴿Indeed, God commands justice and good conduct and giving to relatives, and forbids immorality, wrongdoing, and oppression﴾ (16:90). And He said about His Prophet: ﴿He commands them to what is right and forbids them from what is wrong﴾ (7:157), the verse. And He said about his community: ﴿They enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong﴾ (3:114). He mentioned similar things in many places. Sometimes He restricts the name "wrong" to the prohibition, sometimes He pairs it with "immorality," and sometimes He pairs with them "oppression." Likewise with "right": sometimes He restricts it to the command, and sometimes He pairs it with other things, as in His words: ﴿There is no good in much of their secret conversation, except for one who enjoins charity, or what is right, or reconciliation between people﴾ (4:114), the verse. The reason is that names may be general or specific according to whether they occur singly or in combination, like the terms "the poor" and "the needy." Once this is understood, the name "wrong" encompasses everything God dislikes and forbids, and the name "right" encompasses everything God loves and is pleased with. When "wrong" is paired with "immorality," then immorality is founded on love, and wrong is what hearts reject. It may be thought that the love present in immorality removes it from being included in the wrong, but although immorality is something hearts reject, souls desire it. Likewise "oppression" is paired with them, because it is further from the love of souls. For this reason the kind of punishment of its perpetrator is greater than the kind of punishment of the one who commits immorality, and its source is the intensity of anger. Each soul takes pleasure in attaining what it seeks. So immorality and oppression are paired with wrong. As for polytheism and speaking against God without knowledge, these are pure wrong, and there is no inclination in souls toward them. Rather, they occur only through obstinacy and injustice. So they are pure wrong by nature: ﴿Whoever follows the steps of Satan, indeed he enjoins immorality and wrongdoing﴾ (24:21). Whether the pronoun refers to Satan or to the one who follows him, the meaning holds. For whoever does that, if Satan commanded him, then he is his follower and worshipper. And if the one who does it is the one who commands, then commanding an act is more eloquent than doing it. So whoever commands another to it is pleased with it for himself.

* *

Among immorality and wrong is a servant's listening to the flutes of Satan. The singer is his caller, who summons to his obedience, for singing is an incantation for fornication. Likewise, among following the steps of Satan is speaking against God without knowledge, as is the case of the people of innovation (bid'a) and corruption, and many who consider it lawful to associate with women and beardless youths, to bring them to listen to singing, and who claim to love their forms for God's sake, and other things by which many people have been tested, so that they became misguided and misleading.

Then God, glorified is He, forbade the one who has been wronged by slander from withholding what is fitting to do of kindness to relatives, the needy, and those who repent. He commanded him to pardon. For just as he loves to be forgiven, let him forgive. There is no doubt that maintaining the ties of kinship is obligatory, giving to the needy is obligatory, and aiding the emigrants is obligatory. So it is not permissible to abandon what is obligatory of kindness toward a person merely because he has wronged you, just as one may not withhold his inheritance and his due share of the charities and the public revenue merely because of one sin among the sins, though one may withhold from that for some sins.

[p. 4490]

The verse contains evidence that maintaining ties of kinship (ṣilah) and providing maintenance (nafaqah), among other obligations, are owed to blood relatives (dhawu al-arham) who do not inherit either as sharers with a fixed portion (fard) or as residual heirs (ta'sib).

It is firmly established in the Sahih (the authentic collections) from ʿĀʾishah, in the account of the slander (al-ifk), that Abu Bakr al-Siddiq swore that he would no longer spend on Mistah ibn Uthathah, who was one of those who spread the slander about ʿĀʾishah. Mistah's mother was the daughter of Abu Bakr's maternal aunt. Allah has made him one of the close relatives whose support Allah forbade withholding. A prohibition requires prohibition (in the sense of unlawfulness). So if swearing to abandon an act is not permissible, then the act is obligatory, because swearing to abandon what is permissible is itself permissible. The words of Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, end here.

Fourth: al-Zamakhshari said: "If you were to examine the whole Qur'an and search for what has been prepared for the sinners, you would not find that Allah has been more severe in any matter than in the slander of ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her. Nor were there revealed verses more striking, filled with severe warning, eloquent rebuke, harsh reproach, and great emphasis on the enormity of what was fabricated and the horror of what he (the slanderer) committed, through various ways and with varied and captivating methods. Each of them was in its own category, and He did not reveal anything except these three, meaning His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who accuse﴾ [al-Nur: 23] up to His saying: ﴿it is the manifest truth﴾ [al-Nur: 25], which would suffice. In them He made the slanderers cursed in both worlds together, threatened them with a great punishment in the Hereafter, and declared that their tongues, hands and feet will testify against them concerning what they had fabricated and what they had slandered. He will repay them their due recompense, the true and obligatory one that they deserve, so that at that time they will know that Allah is the manifest truth. He was concise in this and yet thorough, detailed yet comprehensive, emphatic and repetitive, in a way that did not occur in the threats against the polytheists, the idolaters, except in what is less severe than it. And this was for a reason." 

It is related from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, that he was in Basra on the day of ʿArafah, and he was asking about the interpretation of the Qur'an, until he asked about these verses, and said: "Whoever commits a sin and then repents, his repentance is accepted, except for the one who engaged in the matter of ʿĀʾishah." This was from him an exaggeration and a magnification of the matter of the slander.

Allah cleared four people with four things: He cleared Yusuf through the testimony of a witness: ﴿And a witness from her family testified﴾ [Yusuf: 26]. He cleared Musa from the claims of the Jews about him through the stone that carried off his garment. He cleared Maryam by making her son speak when he called out from her lap: ﴿Indeed, I am the servant of Allah﴾ [Maryam: 30]. And He cleared ʿĀʾishah with these great verses in His inimitable Book, recited upon the face of time, with such a clearing and such emphasis. So look at how far apart her clearing is from theirs! And this was only to display the high rank of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and to draw attention to the exalted station of the master of the children of Adam, the best of the first and the last, and the proof of Allah over the worlds.

Whoever wishes to verify the greatness of his (ﷺ) status, the firmness of his step, and his winning of the prize of precedence over every predecessor, let him take that from the verses of the slander. Let him reflect on how Allah became angry on his behalf regarding his sanctity, and how He emphasized in negating the accusation from his household.

[p. 4491] (If you say): If ʿĀʾishah is the one intended, why was the word "the chaste" (al-muhsanat) used? (I say): In this there are two possibilities:

One of them: that by "the chaste" are meant the wives of the Messenger (ﷺ), and they are specified by the fact that whoever slanders them, this threat applies to him. And if they mean ʿĀʾishah, she is the most senior of them in rank and nearness to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so she was the first intended.

The second: that she is the mother of the believers, so the plural was used, intending her and her daughters from among the women of the Ummah who are described as chaste, heedless (of evil) and believing. The words end here.

Al-Nasir said: "The more evident view is that the intended meaning is the general category of the chaste, and the purpose of mentioning them in general terms is the threat against whoever slandered ʿĀʾishah in the most emphatic way. For if this is the threat against one who slanders individual believing women, what then is the expectation regarding the one who slanders their chief and the wife of the master of mankind (ﷺ)? Moreover, generalizing the threat is more emphatic and more horrible than specifying it." And the meaning of the words of Zulaykha: ﴿What is the recompense of one who intended evil to your household, except that he be imprisoned or suffer a painful punishment?﴾ [Yusuf: 25] is that she generalized the intention, to frighten and terrify him. But the one protected is the one whom Allah protects. The words end here.

Fifth: Imam Ibn Taymiyyah said in Minhaj al-Sunnah: Many of the People of the Sunnah have held that ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, is the best of his (ﷺ) wives, and they cited what is in the two Sahihs from Abu Musa and from Anas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The superiority of ʿĀʾishah over women is like the superiority of tharid over other food." Tharid is the best of foods, because it is bread and meat, as the poet said:

"When bread is accompanied with meat, that is the trust of Allah, the tharid."

This is because wheat is the best of staple foods, and meat is the best of condiments, as in the hadith narrated by Ibn Qutaybah and others from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "The master of condiments of the people of this world and the Hereafter is meat." So if meat is the master of condiments, and wheat the master of staples, and their combination is tharid, then tharid is the best of food.

It has been authentically reported through more than one route from the truthful and the one believed in (ﷺ) that he said: "The superiority of ʿĀʾishah over women is like the superiority of tharid over food." And in the Sahih, from ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs, who said: "I said: O Messenger of Allah! Which of the women is most beloved to you?" He said: "ʿĀʾishah." I said: "And of the men?" He said: "Her father." I said: "Then who?" He said: "ʿUmar," and he named other men. 

These (who favour Khadijah) say: his (ﷺ) saying to Khadijah: "Allah has not given me in exchange anyone better than her" means, if its meaning is correct, "He did not give me in exchange anyone better for me than her." For Khadijah benefited him at the beginning of Islam with a benefit that no one else could replace. So she was better for him in this respect, because she benefited him at the time of need. But ʿĀʾishah accompanied him at the end of prophethood and the perfection of the religion. So she gained from knowledge and faith what was not gained by one who only lived to the beginning of prophethood. Thus she was more excellent because of this additional merit, for the Ummah benefited from her more than from anyone else, and she attained a level of knowledge and age that no one else reached. Khadijah's good was confined to the person of the Prophet (ﷺ) himself; she did not convey anything from him, and the Ummah did not benefit from her as they benefited from ʿĀʾishah. Also, the religion had not yet been completed when she could teach it, and she did not attain the perfections that were attained by one who knew and believed in it after its completion. It is known that whoever has his concern gathered upon one thing is more effective in it than one whose concern is scattered among varied works. So Khadijah, may Allah be pleased with her, is better for him in this respect. But the kinds of righteousness are not confined to that. Do you not see that those among the Companions who were greater in faith and more active in jihad with their lives and wealth, such as Hamzah, ʿAli, Saʿd ibn Muʿadh, Usayd ibn Hudayr and others, are more excellent than those who served the Prophet (ﷺ) and benefited him personally more than they did, such as Abu Rafiʿ, Anas ibn Malik and others?

In sum, the discussion of the excellence of ʿĀʾishah and Khadijah is not the place to exhaust it. But the purpose here is that the People of the Sunnah are unanimous on honouring ʿĀʾishah and loving her, and that his (ﷺ) wives are the mothers of the believers, [p. 4492] of whom he died leaving; ʿĀʾishah was the most beloved of them to him and the greatest in sanctity among the Muslims. It is established in the Sahih that "the people used to seek out their gifts on the day of ʿĀʾishah, because of what they knew of his love for her." Until "his wives became jealous of that, and they sent Fatimah, may Allah be pleased with her, to him to say: 'Your wives ask you for justice regarding the daughter of Abu Quhafah.' He said to Fatimah: 'My daughter, do you not love what I love?' She said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Then love this one.'" This hadith is in the two Sahihs. And also in the two Sahihs, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O ʿĀʾishah! This is Jibril, who sends you greetings." She said: "And upon him be peace and the mercy of Allah. You see what we do not see." And Sawdah bint Zamʿah gave her day to ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with them both, with his permission (ﷺ). And in his illness in which he died he would say: "Where am I today?" Longing for the day of ʿĀʾishah. Then he asked his wives' permission to be nursed in the house of ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, and he fell ill there [p. 4493] and died in her house, between her chest and throat, and in her lap. She, may Allah be pleased with her, was blessed for his Ummah, to the extent that Usayd ibn Hudayr said, when Allah revealed the verse of tayammum because of her: "This is not the first of your blessings, O family of Abu Bakr. No matter ever befell you that you disliked, except that Allah placed in it a blessing for the Muslims." The verse clearing her had been revealed before that, when the people of the slander accused her. Allah cleared her from above the seven heavens and made her among the pure women. And success is from Allah. The words end here.

* * *

Ibn Hazm went to an extreme, holding that the best of people after the prophets are his (ﷺ) wives. It is known that ʿĀʾishah is the most excellent of them, and he expounded on that at length in his book al-Milal, so refer to it.

Sixth: al-Qashani, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Allah only magnified the matter of the slander and was severe in the threat concerning it in a way He was not severe regarding other sins, and He emphasized the punishment for it in a way He did not emphasize regarding fornication and the killing of a sacred soul. This is because the enormity of a vice and the greatness of a sin depend on the power which is its source. The vices differ in how they veil their possessor from the divine presence and the holy lights, and how they plunge him into the destructive material realms and the dark abysses, according to the differences in their origins. So whenever the power which is their source and origin is nobler, the vice that proceeds from it is more vile. And conversely, since vice is the opposite of virtue, and since virtue is nobler, what opposes it of vice is baser. Slander is a vice of the irascible power. So according to the nobility of the first over the other two, the vileness of its vice increases.

This is because a person is only a human being through the first (the rational power), and his ascent to the higher world, his turning toward the divine side, his acquisition of knowledge and perfections, and his gaining of goods and happiness, all come through it. When it is corrupted by the domination of satanic qualities over it, and veiled from the light by the ascendancy of darkness, the greatest wretchedness results, and the punishment of the Fire is due. This is the total rust and veil.

Do you not see that the satanic whispering that misleads the son of Adam is further from the divine presence than the beastly and animal natures, and further by an incalculable measure? So the human being, through the firm establishment of his vice of the seminal sort, becomes a devil; and through the firm establishment of the other two vices, he becomes an animal like a beast or a predator. And every animal is more hopeful of goodness and nearer to success than the devil. For this reason Allah said: ﴿Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend?﴾ [al-Shuʿara: 221] ﴿They descend upon every lying sinner﴾ [al-Shuʿara: 222]. And here He forbade following the steps of the devil. For committing such abominations does not happen except by following him and obeying him, and the one who does so is among his soldiers and followers, so he becomes baser and more humiliated than him, deprived of the grace of Allah which is the light of His guidance, veiled from His mercy which is the outpouring of perfection and happiness, cursed in this world and the Hereafter, detested by Allah and the angels. His limbs testify against him by altering their forms and disfiguring their appearance, his essence and soul are corrupt, and he is entangled in filth. For such foulness proceeds only from the foul. As Allah said: ﴿Foul women are for foul men﴾. As for the good people, who are free of vices, only good things and virtues proceed from them. The words end here.

The seventh point concerns the reason adultery is linked with polytheism (shirk) in the words of God, exalted is He: ﴿The adulterer does not marry except an adulteress or a polytheist, and the adulteress is not married except by an adulterer or a polytheist, and that has been made unlawful for the believers﴾ [al-Nur: 3]. The verse is examined in detail. The Imam Ibn al-Qayyim, may God have mercy on him, said in *Ighathat al-Lahfan*: The impurity of adultery and sodomy is more severe than other impurities, because it corrupts the heart and greatly weakens its monotheism (tawhid). For this reason, the people most favored with this impurity are the ones most given to polytheism. Whenever polytheism dominates a servant, this impurity and these vices become more prevalent in him. Whenever his sincerity is greater, he is further removed from them, as God, exalted is He, said about Joseph the Truthful, peace be upon him: ﴿Thus, that We might turn away from him evil and immorality. Indeed, he was of Our chosen, sincere servants﴾ [Yusuf: 24]. The love of forbidden forms is a kind of worship of them; indeed, it is among the highest kinds of worship. Especially when it takes control of the heart and becomes firmly rooted in it, it becomes *tatayyum* (passionate, enslaving love), and *tatayyum* is worship. The lover becomes a worshipper of his beloved. Often his love, his remembrance of the beloved, his longing for him, his striving to please him, and his preference for what the beloved loves, overcome his love of God, his remembrance of Him, and his striving to please Him. Indeed, often all of that vanishes entirely from the lover's heart, and he becomes attached to the beloved form, as is observed, so the beloved becomes his god besides God, the Mighty and Majestic. He puts the beloved's pleasure and love before the pleasure and love of God; he draws near to the beloved in ways he does not draw near to God; he spends for the beloved's pleasure what he would not spend for God's pleasure; and he avoids the beloved's anger more than he avoids God's anger, the exalted. Thus he becomes more dear to his beloved than his Lord, in love, submission, humility, hearing, and obedience. For this reason, passionate love and polytheism are mutually entailing. God, glory be to Him, related passionate love only of the polytheists among the people of Lot, and of the wife of the Governor (al-'Aziz), who was then a polytheist. So whenever a servant's polytheism grows stronger, he is afflicted with passion for forms, and whenever his monotheism grows stronger, that is turned away from him. Adultery and sodomy are the perfection of pleasure, and they come from passionate love, and their practitioners are not free of it. And because the lover moves from place to place, his love does not remain confined to a single object; rather it is divided among many arrows, and each beloved receives a share of his devotion and worship. There is nothing among sins more corrupting to the heart and to religion than these two vile acts. They have a special property of distancing the heart from God, for they are among the greatest impurities. When the heart is dyed with them, it is distanced from Him who is good and does not ascend to Him except what is good. The more impure it becomes, the further it goes from God. For this reason, the Messiah (Christ) said, as narrated by Imam Ahmad in *Kitab al-Zuhd*: "The idlers will not be among the wise, and adulterers will not enter the kingdom of heaven." Since adultery is in this state, it is close to polytheism in the Book of God, exalted is He. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿The adulterer does not marry except an adulteress or a polytheist, and the adulteress is not married except by an adulterer or a polytheist, and that has been made unlawful for the believers﴾ [al-Nur: 3]. The correct position is that this verse is definitive (muhkam), acted upon, and not abrogated by anything. It includes both a report and a prohibition. No one who claimed its abrogation (naskh) has brought a single argument for it. (p-4498) As for what was difficult in it for many people, it is clear, praise be to God, Exalted. They found it difficult to determine whether God's words ﴿The adulterer does not marry except an adulteress or a polytheist﴾ [al-Nur: 3] are a report, a prohibition, or a permission. If it is a report, we have seen many adulterers marry chaste women. If it is a prohibition, it would mean He forbade the adulterer to marry except an adulteress or a polytheist, which would be a prohibition for him against marrying chaste believing women, and a permission for him to marry polytheist women and adulteresses, which God, glory be to Him, definitely did not intend. When this was difficult for them, they sought a meaning for the verse that could be sound. Some said: the intended meaning of "marriage" is sexual intercourse and fornication. So it is as if He said: "The adulterer only commits adultery with an adulteress or a polytheist." This is corrupt, for it has no benefit, and the speech of God, exalted is He, must be preserved from being interpreted in such a way. For it is known that an adulterer only commits adultery with an adulteress, so what is the benefit of informing us of this? When the majority saw the corruption of this interpretation, they set it aside. Then a group said: "This is general in wording but specific in meaning. The intended referent is one man and one woman, namely 'Anaq and her companion, for he embraced Islam and asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for permission to marry her, and this verse was revealed." This also is corrupt. For although this particular case was the occasion of revelation (sabab al-nuzul), the Qur'an is not restricted to the specific cases of its occasions. Were it so, its use as evidence for other cases would be invalid. Another group said: "Rather, the verse is abrogated by His words: ﴿And marry the single among you﴾ [al-Nur: 32]." This is the most corrupt of all, for there is no contradiction between these two verses, and neither negates the other. Rather, He, glory be to Him, commanded the marrying of the single, and forbade marrying an adulteress, just as He forbade marrying a woman in her waiting period, a woman forbidden by lineage or marriage, and close relatives. So where is the abrogating and the abrogated in this? (If it is said): What is the meaning of the verse? It is said: Its meaning, and God knows best, is that the one who marries is commanded to marry a chaste, virtuous woman, and marriage to a woman was permitted only on this condition, as He mentioned in the surahs of al-Nisa' and al-Ma'idah. A ruling conditioned on a stipulation ceases to apply when that stipulation is absent. The permission has been conditioned on the stipulation of chastity (ihsan), so when chastity is absent, the permission conditioned on it is void. (p-4499) So the one who marries either commits himself to God's ruling and law which He legislated through His Messenger, or he does not commit himself to it. If he does not commit himself to it, he is a polytheist who is pleased to marry only one who is a polytheist like him. If he commits himself to it but opposes it, and marries what is forbidden to him, the marriage is not valid, and he is an adulterer. Thus the meaning of His words ﴿does not marry except an adulteress or a polytheist﴾ [al-Nur: 3] becomes clear, and its full explanation is made manifest. The same applies to the ruling for the woman. Just as this ruling is the requirement and plain meaning of the Qur'an, it is also the requirement of the natural disposition (fitrah) and the demand of reason. God, glory be to Him, forbade His servant to be a qarnan (a man who tolerates his wife's adultery) or a dayyuth (a cuckold who allows his wife's immorality), or a husband of a prostitute. For God, exalted is He, created people with a disposition to find this ugly and repugnant. For this reason, when they wish to revile a man to the utmost, they say: "husband of a whore," and God forbade the Muslim from being like that. Thus the wisdom of the prohibition appears and the meaning of the verse becomes clear. And God is the Granter of success. Among what clarifies the prohibition, and that it is what befits this perfect Sharia, is that this crime by a woman leads to corruption of the husband's bed and the corruption of lineage, which God, exalted is He, established among people for the completion of their welfare, and which they counted among His blessings upon them. Adultery leads to the mixing of waters and confusion of lineages. Thus among the excellences of the Sharia is the prohibition of marrying an adulteress until she repents and her womb is cleansed. Also, an adulteress is impure, as previously explained, and God, glory be to Him, made marriage a means for affection (mawaddah) and mercy, and affection is pure love. How then can an impure woman be loved by a good man as his wife? The husband is called zawj (spouse) from *izdiwaj* (pairing), so the two spouses (zawjan) are two similar things, and repugnance is established between the good and the impure, both by law and by decree. Thus pairing, mercy, and mutual affection cannot be achieved with it. Whoever adopted this position did so with complete excellence, and prevented a man from being the husband of a prostitute. Where is this from the saying of one who permitted him to marry her and have intercourse with her tonight, though an adulterer had been with her yesterday? He said: "The semen of an adulterer has no sanctity." Grant that this is so; yet the semen of a husband has sanctity, so how is it permissible for it to mingle with the semen of an adulterer in one womb? The point is that God, glory be to Him, named adulteresses and adulterers as impure men and impure women. The nature of this act is one in which purity has been prescribed, even though it is lawful. The one who performs it is called junub (in a state of major ritual impurity), because he is distant from reciting the Qur'an, from prayer, and from the mosques. He is prevented from all of that until he purifies himself with water. Likewise, when it is forbidden, the heart becomes distant from God, exalted is He, and from the Last Abode. Indeed, it stands between him and faith, until he purifies himself completely (p-4500) through repentance, and purifies his body with water. The saying of the people of Lot: ﴿Expel them from your town; indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure﴾ [al-A'raf: 82] is of the same kind as His words, exalted is He, concerning the People of the Trench: ﴿They resented them only because they believed in God, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy﴾ [al-Buruj: 8], and His words, glory be to Him: ﴿Say: O People of the Scripture, do you resent us only because we believed in God and in what has been revealed to us and what was revealed before?﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 59]. Likewise, the polytheist resents the monotheist for devoting himself purely to monotheism and not mixing it with polytheism; and likewise the innovator resents the Sunni for devoting himself purely to following the Messenger and not mixing it with the opinions of men or with anything that opposes it. The monotheist who follows the Messenger, enduring what the people of polytheism and innovation resent in him, is better for him, more beneficial, and easier for him than enduring what God and His Messenger resent in him by conforming to the people of polytheism and innovation.

*If there is no escape from patience, then be patient for the truth; that patience has a praiseworthy outcome.*

**An anecdote:**
The son of the judge Sharaf al-Din Ibn al-Muqri, author of *al-Rawd*, wrote to his father when he had cut off his maintenance:

*Do not cut off the habit of kindness, nor make the reproach of a man into his livelihood.*
*For the matter of the slander by Mistah lowers the rank of the star from its horizon.*
*What occurred from him has occurred, and al-Siddiq was rebuked regarding his right.*

His father, Sharaf al-Din, answered him with these words:

*The distressed may be denied carrion when he disobeys by traveling its roads.*
*For he is able to repent in a way that brings him to his livelihood.*
*Had Mistah not repented of his sin, al-Siddiq would not have been rebuked regarding his right.*

Since God, exalted is He, has mentioned the deterrents against adultery and against accusing chaste women of it, He then explained some of the deterrents that might lead to one of these two acts. These concern the mixing of men with women, their entering upon them, times of seclusion, and teaching beautiful manners. Thus He, glory be to Him, said:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 24, verse 27–28:

The discussion of His saying, exalted is He:

[27–28] ﴿O you who believe, do not enter houses other than your own houses until you have asked permission and greeted their people. That is best for you, that you may be reminded.﴾ ﴿And if you find no one therein, do not enter them until permission is given to you. And if it is said to you, "Go back," then go back; it is purer for you. And Allah is Knowing of what you do.﴾ [An-Nur: 28].

﴿O you who believe, do not enter houses other than your own houses until you have asked permission﴾: i.e., seek to know and uncover the situation, whether entry is desired or not. It is from (al-isti'nas) [seeking familiarity/knowledge], which is (al-isti'lam) [seeking information]. From (anasa al-shay') when one sees it clearly and plainly exposed. Or the meaning is: until permission is given to you, so that you become familiar, from (al-isti'nas), which is the opposite of (al-istīhash) [feeling of estrangement]. This is because the one seeking permission feels estranged by the hiddenness of the situation from him; so the thing is expressed by what is necessarily associated with it, as a metonymy (majaz) or a metaphor (isti'ara). It has also been allowed that it is from (al-ins) [humankind], and the meaning is: until you know whether there is a person therein? ﴿and greet their people﴾: i.e., so that he reassures them regarding what would make them feel uneasy. ﴿That﴾: i.e., the seeking of permission and the greeting: ﴿is best for you﴾: i.e., better than entering suddenly: ﴿that you may be reminded﴾: i.e., that you may take heed and act in accordance with its requirement.

﴿And if you find no one therein﴾ [An-Nur: 28]: i.e., of those who grant permission: ﴿do not enter them until permission is given to you﴾ [An-Nur: 28]: i.e., be patient until you find someone who gives you permission. It may also be understood: if you find no one therein from its people, and you have a need therein, then do not enter them except with the permission of its people.

Al-Zamakhshari said: That is because seeking permission was not prescribed merely so that the one entering does not look upon a private part (awrah), and his eye does not fall upon what it is not lawful to look at; rather, it was prescribed so that one is not made aware of the circumstances which people customarily conceal from others and guard against anyone's knowledge of them; and because it is a disposal of another's property, so it must be with his consent, otherwise it resembles usurpation and domination. End of quote.

(p-4502) ﴿And if it is said to you, "Go back," then go back﴾ [An-Nur: 28]: i.e., if you are told by the people of the house to return, whether the one ordering it is one who has authority to grant permission or not, such as women and children, then go back and do not persist by repeatedly asking for permission, for this brings about resentment in people's hearts. For this reason He, exalted is He, said: ﴿it﴾ [An-Nur: 28]: i.e., the returning: ﴿is purer for you﴾ [An-Nur: 28]: i.e., more pure from the baseness of stain that persistence and standing at doors does not escape. And it increases your being loved.

Al-Zamakhshari said: Since He forbade that because it leads to resentment, it becomes obligatory to refrain from everything that leads to it, such as knocking on the door violently, shouting at the owner of the house, and other things that fall under the habits of those who have not been refined, among most people.

A subtle point:

Ibn Kathir said: Qatadah said: Some of the emigrants said: "I have sought this verse all my life and have not attained it: that I seek permission to enter upon one of my brothers, and he says to me, 'Go back,' and I go back while being pleased." End of quote. ﴿And Allah is Knowing of what you do﴾ [An-Nur: 28]: i.e., He will recompense you according to your good intention in visiting, or [according to] deceit and treachery against the people of the one visited or his property.

A caution:

Al-Suyuti said in (al-Iklil): In this verse is the obligation of seeking permission upon entering another's house, the obligation of returning if one is not given permission, and the prohibition of entering if there is no one in it. From this is derived the prohibition of entering another's property, staying in it, and occupying it without the permission of its owner, and under this fall countless legal questions and subsidiary rulings. Most scholars cited the verse for combining seeking permission with greeting; the fewer cited it for placing seeking permission before greeting, by its being mentioned first in the verse. Most answered that the conjunction "wa" does not indicate sequence. Those who held that one may seek permission more than three times, until he is given permission or is explicitly refused, also cited it, and it was understood from the verse that a man does not need to seek permission when entering his own house upon his wife. End of quote.

Ibn Kathir said: It should be known that one who seeks permission from the people of a dwelling should not stand directly in front of the door, but let the door be to his right or left. In the Two Sahihs, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If a man looked at you without permission, and you struck him with a pebble and put out his eye, there would be no blame upon you." The group [of compilers] also reported on the authority of Jabir, who said: "I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning a debt that was owed by my father. I knocked on the door, and he said, 'Who is it?' I said, 'I.' He said, 'I, I,' as if he disliked it." He disliked it because this expression does not identify its speaker until he states his name or the kunya by which he is well known; otherwise, everyone refers to himself as "I," and thus the intended purpose of seeking permission, which is the familiarity commanded in the verse, is not achieved. It is reported on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "Seek permission before your mothers." On the authority of Tawus, who said: "There is no woman I dislike more to see her private part than a woman who is within the prohibited degrees (dhat mahram)," and he would strongly condemn this. Ibn Juraij said: I said to Ata': "Should a man seek permission before entering upon his wife?" He said: "No." Ibn Kathir said: This is to be understood as meaning it is not obligatory; otherwise, it is better for him to inform her of his entry and not surprise her with it, since she may be in a state in which she does not wish him to see her. It is reported on the authority of Zaynab, the wife of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: "When Abdullah came from some errand and reached the door, he would clear his throat and spit, out of dislike that he might come upon us in something he disliked." For this reason it is reported in the Sahih on the authority of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he forbade a man to come to his family suddenly at night.
