The commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 24, verse 39:

The exposition of His words, exalted is He:

[39] ﴿And those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage in a level plain, which the thirsty one supposes to be water, until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing; and he finds God with him, so He pays him his account in full. And God is swift at reckoning.﴾

﴿And those who disbelieve﴾ is conjoined to what the preceding text leads to. It is as if it were said: "As for those who believe, their deeds are as described, in their present state and their outcome. And as for those who disbelieve, ﴿their deeds﴾, meaning those which they suppose will benefit them and take them by the hand away from punishment, ﴿are like a mirage﴾, which is what is seen in the wilderness of the sun's light at midday, gliding over the face of the earth as if it were flowing water, ﴿in a level plain﴾. Qay'a (level plain) has the meaning of qa', which is the flat expanse of land. Or it is the plural of qa'in (in the manner of jiyra in jar, as in the pattern of plural forms), ﴿which the thirsty one supposes to be water, until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing﴾, meaning neither something real nor something imagined, just as he used to see it before, let alone finding water in it. With this, the explanation of the states of the disbelievers is complete by way of tamthil (figurative comparison)." His words, exalted is He: ﴿and he finds God with him, so He pays him his account in full, and God is swift at reckoning﴾ mean: he finds the punishment of God and His recompense with him at the mirage, or at the deed. Expressing it in this way adds to the awfulness of the image. It has also been said that the meaning is: he finds Him reckoning with him. So "with Him" (indiyya) carries the meaning of reckoning, by way of kinaya (implicit allusion), since the full payment is mentioned after it. It has been said: this clause is conjoined to ﴿he finds it not﴾, and there is no need to conjoin it to what it implies, such as: "he finds that what he did was not beneficial."

Al-Shihab said: It is possible that it is an explanation of the state of the thing compared, namely the disbeliever, so that it is conjoined in meaning to the whole tamthil. Had it been said, according to the first view, that it is part of the description of the mirage, the meaning would be: he finds the decree of God concerning him of perishing through thirst at the mirage, and so He fulfils for him what was written for him, the One who does not delay the reckoning. The discourse would then be coherent. Abu al-Su'ud chose the second view, saying: it is an explanation of the remaining states of theirs which befall them after that, by way of completion, lest it be supposed that the utmost of their affair is only disappointment and despair, as is the case with the thirsty one. It appears that after that there befalls them such evil condition that disappointment has no weight at all in comparison. So the clause is not conjoined to ﴿he finds it nothing﴾, but to what is understood from it by way of tamthil, namely that the disbelievers find none of their aforementioned deeds, neither as a substance nor as a trace, as in His words, exalted is He: ﴿And We shall turn to what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust﴾ [al-Furqan: 23].

If it is asked: why was the thirsty one singled out for mention, when the mirage appears in that way to everyone? The expected word would have been "the seer" instead. It is answered: He restricted it to him and did not leave it general, because of His words ﴿and he finds God with him﴾ etc., since this is part of the states of the thing compared, and it is more eloquent, because the disappointment of the disbeliever is more penetrating and more deeply rooted. Similar to it is His words: ﴿The likeness of what they spend in this worldly life﴾ [Al 'Imran: 117] etc., for the disbelievers are those whose tilth is completely destroyed. That is, He likened the deeds of the disbelievers, which they think beneficial but whose outcome is disappointment, to the sight of the severely thirsty disbeliever on the Day of Gathering seeing a mirage which he supposes to be a drink. Thus the conjunction of ﴿he finds God﴾ fits most excellently, as they have illuminated it. Thus it is in al-Kashshaf.

The third matter: Al-Shihab said: This is an eloquent simile, and the like of it occurred in the words of Malik ibn Nuwayra:

"By my life, I and Ibn Jarud are like one who spilled the water of Shu'ayb while the mirage glittered.
When he came to it, God frustrated his effort, and he ended up averting his gaze, choking with thirst, gasping."

Then, exalted is He, pointed to their likeness by another kind, with His words:

**Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 24, verse 40 (part 1 of 2)**

**On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:**
[40] ﴿Or [their deeds are] like darknesses in a deep sea, covered by a wave, above which is a wave, above which are clouds: darknesses, one above another. When he extends his hand, he can hardly see it. And whomever God does not give light, for him there is no light.﴾

(p. 4533) ﴿Or like darknesses in a deep sea﴾: i.e., profound, with abundant water. ﴿Covered by a wave﴾: i.e., piled up, one part upon another. ﴿Above which is a wave, above which are clouds, darknesses one above another﴾: i.e., dense and piled up. This is an explanation of the utmost intensity of the darknesses. ﴿When he extends his hand﴾: i.e., and brings it into his sight, near his eye, so that he may look at it. ﴿He can hardly see it. And whomever God does not give light, for him there is no light﴾: i.e., whomever God does not will to guide to His light, which is the Qur'an, for him there is no guidance whatsoever. This stands in contrast to His words, exalted is He, concerning the parable of the believers: ﴿God guides to His light whom He wills﴾ [al-Nur: 35]. The clause confirms the preceding parable, and establishes that this [lack of light] is due to His not guiding them, since they did not strive to attain it. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And those who strive for Us, We will surely guide them to Our paths﴾ [al-Ankabut: 69].

**A subtle point (laṭīfa):**
Ibn Kathir said: God set forth these two parables for the two kinds of disbelievers, just as He set forth two parables for the hypocrites at the beginning of al-Baqara, one fiery and one watery, and just as He set forth for what settles in the hearts of guidance and knowledge, in Surat al-Ra'd, two parables, one watery and one fiery.

He then said: As for the first, it is for the disbelievers who call to their disbelief, the people of compound ignorance (*jahl murakkab*), who think they are upon something. Their parable is that of a mirage. The second is for the people of simple ignorance (*jahl basīt*), namely the followers of the leaders of disbelief, who are deaf and dumb and do not reason. Such a person does not know the condition of the one who leads him, nor does he know where he is going. Rather, as is said in the proverb about the ignorant one: "Where are you going?" He said: "With them." It was said: "Then where are they going?" He said: "I do not know." End of quotation.

What he mentioned is something the noble wording admits, but it is not definitive. Its basis is what his teacher, the Imam Ibn al-Qayyim, may mercy and good pleasure be upon them both, mentioned in *al-Juyush al-Islamiyya*. There is no harm in quoting it, given the marvelous benefits it contains. He said: Observe how these verses arranged the paths of the children of Adam in the most complete arrangement (p. 4534) and encompassed them in the most perfect encompassing. People are of two kinds: the people of guidance and insight, who know that the truth lies in what the Messenger (ﷺ) brought from God, glorified and exalted is He, and that everything that opposes it consists of doubts whose nature is obscure to those who have little share of reason and revelation; so they suppose it to be something of substance and benefit from it. These doubts are like a mirage in a level plain, etc. These are the people of guidance and the religion of truth, the possessors of beneficial knowledge and righteous action, who affirmed the Messenger (ﷺ) in his reports and did not oppose them with doubts, and who obeyed him in his commands and did not waste them for the sake of desires. They are neither among those who plunge into vain speculation: ﴿who are in heedlessness, playing﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 11], nor among those who enjoy their share in worldly pleasures, whose deeds have failed in this world and the Hereafter; those are the losers. The clear light of revelation has shone upon them, so in its light they see the people of darkness in their opinions wandering blindly, in their misguidance bewildered, in their doubt hesitating; deceived by the outward appearance of the mirage, barren and sterile regarding what God, exalted is He, sent His Messenger (ﷺ) with of wisdom and decisive speech: ﴿There is nothing in their breasts but pride, which they will never attain﴾ [Ghafir: 56]. Following their desires has caused this for them, and for its sake they dispute concerning the signs of God without any authority.

The second kind: the people of ignorance and injustice, who combined ignorance of what was brought with injustice in following their own desires. Concerning them God, exalted is He, said: ﴿They follow only assumption and what their souls desire, and there has already come to them guidance from their Lord﴾ [al-Najm: 23]. These are of two types. One type thinks they are upon knowledge and guidance, and they are the people of ignorance and error. These are the people of compound ignorance, who do not know the truth and oppose it, oppose its people, support falsehood and befriend its people. They think they are upon something; unquestionably, they are the liars. Because they believe something contrary to what it really is, they are in the position of one who sees a mirage, which the thirsty one takes to be water, until when he reaches it he finds it to be nothing. So it is with them: their deeds and their knowledge are like a mirage that betrays its beholder at the moment he most needs it. It does not stop at mere disappointment and deprivation, as is the case with one who heads toward the mirage and finds not water. Rather, there is added to that that he finds there the Most Wise of judges and the Most Just of the just, glorified and exalted is He. He reckons to him what he has of knowledge and deed, and repays him in full, down to the weight of an atom. ﴿And We will turn to what they did of deeds and make it scattered dust﴾ [al-Furqan: 23], because it was not sincerely for His sake, nor according to the Sunna of His Messenger (ﷺ). The false doubts he used to take for beneficial knowledge likewise become scattered dust. Thus their deeds and knowledge become regrets upon them.

The *sarāb* (mirage) is what is seen in a vast open desert from the sunlight at midday, shimmering on the surface of the earth as if it were flowing water. The *qī'a* and *qā'* is the level land with no mountain in it and no valley. He likened the knowledge of one who did not take his knowledge from revelation, and his deeds, to a mirage that the traveler sees in the intense heat, so he heads toward it, his hope is disappointed, and he finds it to be a blazing fire. Likewise, the knowledge and deeds of the people of falsehood, when mankind is gathered and thirst intensifies upon them, will appear to them like a mirage; they think it is water. When they come to it they find God there, and the angels of punishment seize them, drag them to the fire of Hellfire, and they are given to drink scalding water, which cuts their intestines. That water they are given is the very knowledge that does not benefit, and the deeds that were for other than God, which God, exalted is He, turns into scalding water that He makes them drink. Just as their food is *ḍarī'* (thorny plant) that neither nourishes nor relieves hunger, so the knowledge and vain deeds they had in this world likewise neither nourish nor relieve hunger. These are the ones concerning whom God said: ﴿Say: Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in deeds? Those whose effort is lost in the life of this world while they think they are doing well﴾ [al-Kahf: 103–104]. They are the ones referred to in His words: ﴿And We will turn to what they did of deeds and make it scattered dust﴾ [al-Furqan: 23], and they are the ones referred to in His words, exalted is He: ﴿Thus God will show them their deeds as regrets upon them, and they will not emerge from the Fire﴾ [al-Baqara: 167].

The second category within this class: the people of darknesses. They are those immersed in ignorance, to such an extent that it has encompassed them from every direction. They are like cattle, nay, they are further astray. Their deeds are those performed without insight, merely by imitation and following their fathers, without any light from God, exalted is He. ﴿Like darknesses﴾: plural of *ẓulma* (darkness), and these are the darkness of ignorance, the darkness of disbelief, the darkness of wrongdoing and following desire, the darkness of doubt and suspicion, and the darkness of turning away from the truth which God, exalted is He, sent His messengers with, may the blessings and peace of God be upon them. And the light which He sent with them was to bring people out of darknesses into light. The one who turns away from what God sent Muhammad (ﷺ) with of guidance and the religion of truth (p. 4536) moves within five darknesses: his speech is darkness, his deed is darkness, his entrance is darkness, his exit is darkness, and his final destination is darkness. His heart is dark, his face is dark, his speech is dark, and his condition is dark. When his owl-like insight encounters what God sent Muhammad (ﷺ) with of light, he strives hard to flee from it, and its light almost snatches away his sight. So he flees into the darknesses of opinions, which are more suitable and fitting for him, as it has been said:

*Bats whom the day has blinded with its light, and in whose favor are pieces of the dark night.*

As for His words, exalted is He: ﴿In a deep sea﴾: *al-lujjī* means deep, and it is ascribed to *lujjat al-bahr* (the depths of the sea), which is its greater part. His words, exalted is He: ﴿Covered by a wave, above which is a wave, above which are clouds﴾ depict the condition of one who turns away from His revelation. He likened the surging of the waves of doubts and falsehood in his breast to the surging of the waves of that sea, and [described] that they are waves, one above another. The first pronoun in His words ﴿covers him﴾ refers to the sea, and the second pronoun in ﴿above it﴾ refers to the wave. Furthermore, those waves are covered by clouds. So here are darknesses: the darkness of the deep sea, the darkness of the wave above it, and the darkness of the clouds above all that. ﴿When he extends﴾ — the one within this sea — ﴿his hand, he can hardly see it﴾. The meaning of this has been disputed. Many of the grammarians (*nuḥāh*) said: it is a negation of the approach of seeing it, and it is more emphatic than a negation of seeing. It may negate the occurrence of a thing while not negating its approach. So it is as if he said: he did not approach seeing it in any way.

These [grammarians] said: *kāda* (he was about to) is among the verbs of approximation (*af'āl al-muqāraba*). It has the same ruling as other verbs regarding negation and affirmation. When it is said: *kāda yaf'alu* (he is about to do), it affirms the approach of the action; and when it is said: *lam yakad yaf'alu* (he was not about to do), it negates the approach of the action.

Another group said: rather, this indicates that he sees it only after great effort. In that is an affirmation of seeing it after extreme difficulty, due to those darknesses. They said: because *kāda* has a distinctive status not shared by other verbs: when it affirms, it negates; and when it negates, it affirms. So when you say: *mā kidtu aṣilu ilayka* (I was not about to reach you), its meaning is: I reached you after exertion and hardship. This is an affirmation of arrival. And when you say: *kāda Zaydun yaqūmu* (Zayd was about to stand), it negates his standing, as God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And when the servant of God stood calling upon Him, they nearly crowded upon him﴾ [al-Jinn: 19].

(p. 4537) From this is His words, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes﴾ [al-Qalam: 51]. And some have composed a riddle about this:

*O grammarian of this age! What word is it that has run on the tongues of Jurhum and Thamud?*

*When it is used in the form of negation, it affirms; and when it is affirmed, it stands in place of denial.*

A third group, including Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Malik and others, said: its use in the affirmative implies the negation of its predicate, as in your saying: *kāda Zaydun yaqūmu* (Zayd was about to stand, i.e., he did not stand). And its use in the negative implies the negation of the predicate by way of a stronger inference. So in his view it negates the predicate, whether it is negative or affirmative. *Lam yakad Zaydun yaqūmu* is, in his view, more emphatic in negation than *lam yaqum*. He argued that when it is negated, being a verb of approximation, it negates the approach of the action, and that is more emphatic than negating the action itself. And when it is used affirmatively, it requires the approach of its subject to its predicate, and that indicates the non-occurrence of the action. He also answered the objection regarding His words, exalted is He: ﴿So they slaughtered it, and they were not about to do it﴾ [al-Baqara: 71], and regarding the like of the saying: *waṣaltu ilayka wa mā kidtu aṣilu* (I reached you, though I was not about to) and *salimtu wa mā kidtu aslamu* (I was safe, though I was not about to be safe), by saying that this comes upon two different statements: that is, "I did the thing after I had not been near to it." The first implies the occurrence of the action, and the second implies that he was not near to it, but rather had despaired of it. So they are two statements intended to express two different matters.

A fourth group went to distinguish between its past and future forms. If it is in the affirmative, it indicates the approach of the action, whether it is in the past or the future form. And if it is in the negative, if it is in the future form it is for negating the action and its approach, like His words: ﴿He was not about to see it﴾. And if it is in the past form, it implies affirmation, like His words: ﴿So they slaughtered it, and they were not about to do it﴾ [al-Baqara: 71]. These are the four approaches of the grammarians to this word.

The correct view is that it is a verb denoting approximation (*muqarabah*, "coming near to" an action), and it has the ruling of other verbs. Its negation of the predicate was not derived from its wording and form, since it was not coined for negation. Rather, the negation is derived from the necessary implications of its meaning. When it denotes coming near to an action, that action has not occurred, so it is necessarily negated. As for when it is used in negated form: if it occurs in a single clause, it denotes the negation of approximation, as when you say: "The idler hardly succeeds" (*lā yakādu al-baṭṭālu yufliḥu*), "The miser hardly becomes a leader" (*lā yakādu al-bakhīlu yasūdu*), "The coward hardly rejoices" (*lā yakādu al-jabānu yafraḥu*), and similar examples. If it occurs in two clauses, it implies that the action took place after it had not been near. As Ibn Malik said: [ ... ] This is the verification of its matter.

The intended meaning is that His saying, ﴿he could hardly see it﴾, either indicates that he was not close to seeing it because of the intensity of the darkness, which is the more apparent reading. If he was not close to seeing it, how could he see it? Dhu al-Rummah said:

"When separation changed the lovers, the remnant of passion does not nearly depart from love for Mayya."

That is, it did not come near to *al-barah*, which is cessation. So how could it cease?

First, God (glorified be He) likened their deeds, in that their benefit is lost and their harm falls upon them, to a deceptive mirage that deceives its beholder from afar. When he approaches it, he finds it the opposite of what he hoped for and expected. Second, He likened their deeds in their darkness and blackness, because they are void and empty of the light of faith, to layers of darkness in the depths of a turbulent sea with waves crashing, over which clouds have gathered from above. How wondrous this comparison is, and how precisely it matches the condition of the people of innovation and misguidance, and of those who worship God (glorified and exalted be He) in opposition to what His Messenger (ﷺ) was sent with and what He revealed in His Book! This comparison likens their false deeds explicitly and directly, and their corrupt knowledge and beliefs by implication. Each of the mirage and the darknesses is an illustration of the totality of their knowledge and deeds. So they are a mirage with no substance, and darknesses with no light in them.

This is the opposite of the illustration of the deeds and knowledge of the believer, which he receives from the niche of prophethood. They are like the rain by which the lands and servants live, and like the light by which the people of this world and the Hereafter benefit. For this reason God (glorified be He) mentions these two illustrations in the Qur'an in more than one place, for His friends and His enemies.

End of the words of Ibn al-Qayyim, may God Most High have mercy on him.

[p. 4538]

Then God, exalted is He, pointed to the confirmation of the proofs of His lordship and His oneness in divinity, and to the manifestness of His command and His majesty, by His saying, glorified is He:

(p-4539)The discussion on the interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying:

[41] ﴿Have you not seen that to God glorify whoever is in the heavens and the earth, and the birds in flight? Each has indeed known its prayer and its glorification. And God is Knowing of what they do.﴾

﴿Have you not seen that to God glorify whoever is in the heavens and the earth﴾: that is, they exalt Him and sanctify Him alone, [along with] their inhabitants. ﴿And the birds in flight﴾: that is, they spread their wings in the air. ﴿Each has indeed known its prayer and its glorification﴾: that is, each one of those mentioned has been guided and shown the way and path to the worship of God, mighty and majestic. So the pronoun in (ʿalima, "has known") refers to "each" (kull). Or it refers to the Divine Name (lafẓ al-jalāla, the name "God"), like the pronoun in "its prayer" and "its glorification."

Al-Zamakhshari said: It is not far-fetched that God inspires the birds with His supplication and glorification, just as He inspired them with all the subtle sciences which intelligent beings can hardly arrive at by guidance.

A discussion on the glorification of inanimate things has preceded in Surat al-Isra', so refer back to it. ﴿And God is Knowing of what they do.﴾

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[42] ﴿And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to Allah is the final return.﴾

﴿And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to Allah is the final return.﴾ That is: He is the God, the Ruler who disposes of them both, the One to whom worship is due in them alone, and to Him is the Day of Resurrection, the destination of all creatures, so He will judge between them and recompense those who did evil according to what they did.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[43] ﴿Do you not see that Allah drives the clouds gently, then joins them together, then makes them into a heaped mass, and you see the rain coming out from their midst? And He sends down from the sky mountains of hail in it, striking with it whom He wills and averting it from whom He wills. The flash of its lightning nearly takes away the sight.﴾

(p-4540) ﴿Do you not see that Allah drives the clouds﴾ means: He drives them gently. From the same root is "al-bidā'a al-muzjāt" (the meager merchandise), which everyone pushes along, meaning they put it forward out of their own disinterest in it, or because of their ability to drive it and deliver it. ﴿Then joins them together﴾ by bringing part of them together with part, so that the scattered pieces become one piece. ﴿Then makes them into a heaped mass﴾ meaning piled up, some of it upon the rest. ﴿And you see the rain﴾ meaning the rainfall ﴿coming out from their midst﴾, and the "khilāl" is its gaps and the places from which the drops emerge. ﴿And He sends down from the sky mountains of hail in it, striking with it whom He wills and averting it from whom He wills.﴾

Ibn Kathir said: The meaning may be: He strikes with what He sends down from the sky, of the two kinds of rain and hail, as mercy for them, and averts it from others as wisdom and a trial. The meaning may also be: He strikes with the hail whom He wills as punishment, because of what it does of scattering fruits and destroying crops, and He averts it from whom He wills as mercy toward them. End of quotation.

Its summary: the pronoun is either referring to the nearest noun, according to the second view, or to the first (the clouds) and what precedes it, according to the first view.

A subtle point: the preposition "min" (from) has been mentioned three times in the verse. The first is initial (ibtidā'iyya, indicating a starting point) by agreement. The second is either redundant (zā'ida, extra), partitive (tab'īḍiyya, indicating part of), or initial, on the basis that its object is a substitute (badal) for what precedes it, with the particle repeated. The third has these views, and it adds a fourth: that it is for specifying the genus (bayān al-jins, explaining the kind). The meaning would be: He sends down from the sky some mountains, which are hail.

﴿The flash of its lightning nearly takes away the sight﴾ meaning its brightness, ﴿takes away the sight﴾ meaning snatches it away because of its intensity and strength.

The Interpretation of His saying, the Exalted:

[44] ﴿Allah alternates the night and the day. Indeed in that is a lesson for those who have vision.﴾

﴿Allah alternates the night and the day﴾: that is, He brings each of them in place of the other, one succeeding the other. Or He takes from the length of one of them and places it in the other, as a mercy to the servants, so that their livelihoods are well ordered: ﴿Indeed in that is a lesson for those who have vision.﴾

(p-٤٥٤١) The discussion on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[45–46] ﴿And Allah has created every creature from water. Of them are those that walk on their bellies, and of them are those that walk on two legs, and of them are those that walk on four. Allah creates what He wills; indeed Allah is competent over all things.﴾ ﴿We have certainly sent down distinct verses, and Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path.﴾ [al-Nur: 46]

﴿And Allah has created every creature from water﴾: every living being that crawls upon the earth is from water, and it is a part of its substance. Or it refers to a specific water, namely the semen (nutfah), and this would be a case of mentioning the predominant (al-ghalib) and treating it as the whole (tanzil al-ghalib manzilat al-kull), because some animals are not generated from semen. It has also been said that ﴿from water﴾ is connected to (dabbah) (creature) and is not a complement of (khalaqa) (created). ﴿Of them are those that walk on their bellies﴾ like snakes. Calling their movement "walking" (mashy), although it is crawling (zahf), is by way of metaphor (isti'arah) or by way of association (mushakalah). ﴿And of them are those that walk on two legs, and of them are those that walk on four. Allah creates what He wills﴾, i.e., from what has been mentioned and other than it, according to whom He wills, of forms, limbs, shapes and movements: ﴿indeed Allah is competent over all things﴾. ﴿We have certainly sent down distinct verses, and Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path﴾ [al-Nur: 46]. This is the path of those verses, the path of truth, guidance and light. They are the sincere believers who responded to Allah and the Messenger, and when they are called to their judgment, they submit humbly.

Then he pointed to what used to occur from the hypocrites of the effect of hypocrisy, as a warning against their conduct, with His words, exalted is He:

The discussion of the words of God, Exalted is He:

[47–50] ﴿They say: "We believe in God and the Messenger, and we obey," then after that a faction of them turns away. And those are not believers.﴾ ﴿And when they are called to God and His Messenger, that He may judge between them, behold, a faction of them are averse.﴾ [al-Nur: 48] ﴿But if the right is theirs, they come to him in submission.﴾ [al-Nur: 49] ﴿Is there a disease in their hearts, or have they doubted, or do they fear that God and His Messenger will wrong them? Rather, it is they who are the wrongdoers.﴾ [al-Nur: 50]

﴿They say: "We believe in God and the Messenger, and we obey," then after that a faction of them turns away﴾, i.e., the claim of faith. ﴿And those are not believers﴾, i.e., in their hearts. Then he proved this with His words: ﴿And when they are called to God﴾ [al-Nur: 48], i.e., His Book; ﴿and His Messenger﴾ [al-Nur: 48], i.e., his Sunnah and his judgment; ﴿that He may judge between them, behold, a faction of them are averse﴾ [al-Nur: 48], i.e., from coming to him. ﴿But if the right is theirs﴾ [al-Nur: 49], i.e., if the judgment would be in their favour and not against them; ﴿they come to him in submission﴾ [al-Nur: 49], i.e., hastening, obedient. His words, exalted is He: ﴿Is there a disease in their hearts, or have they doubted, or do they fear that God will wrong them in judgment, and His Messenger?﴾ [al-Nur: 50], i.e., in the judgment, so that they would be wronged in it.

Abu al-Su'ud said: it is a denunciation and a condemnation of their aversion mentioned above, and a statement of its source, after enumerating a number of established vices among them and those expected from them, and the gradual ordering of the sources among them. The focus of the interrogation is not the very thing that the hamza and "am" govern from among the three matters, but rather its being the source of it. It is as if it were said: Is that, i.e., their aforementioned aversion, because they are sick at heart due to their disbelief and hypocrisy, or because they doubted the matter of his prophethood, peace be upon him, despite the manifestation of its truth? Or because they fear injustice from one who is impossible for that to befall? Indicating that they combine those blameworthy attributes, each one of which is disbelief and hypocrisy.

Then he clarified their being characterised, along with that, by the worst attribute, which is wrongdoing, by His words, exalted is He: ﴿Rather, it is they who are the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Nur: 50], i.e., those in whom the disposition of wrongdoing has taken firm root, both toward themselves and toward others. So the "bal" (rather) is transitional.

The meaning: leave all of this aside, for they are the complete ones in wrongdoing, the ones who combine those attributes.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[51–52] ﴿The only saying of the believers, when they are called to Allah and His Messenger that he may judge between them, is that they say, "We hear and we obey." And those are the successful.﴾ ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger and fears Allah and keeps his duty to Him—those are the attainers of success.﴾ [al-Nur: 52]

﴿The only saying of the believers, when they are called to Allah and His Messenger that he may judge between them, is that they say, "We hear and we obey." And those are the successful.﴾ ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger and fears Allah and keeps his duty to Him—those are the attainers of success.﴾ [al-Nur: 52]

Al-Suyuti said in *al-Iklil*: In it is the obligation to attend for whoever is summoned to a ruling of the Shari'ah (divine law), the prohibition of refusing, and the recommendation that one say, "We hear and we obey." End of quotation.

Then reference is made to the narration of some of the circumstances of those hypocrites who refused to accept His judgment, namely their false oaths, so that this may be used as evidence of their inner faith, by His saying, exalted is He:

Al-Suyuti said in *al-Iklil*: In it is the obligation to attend for whoever is summoned to a ruling of the Shari'ah (divine law), the prohibition of refusing, and the recommendation that one say, "We hear and we obey." End of quotation.

Then reference is made to the narration of some of the circumstances of those hypocrites who refused to accept His judgment, namely their false oaths, so that this may be used as evidence of their inner faith, by His saying, exalted is He:

**The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted Is He:**

[53] ﴿They swore by God with the utmost of their oaths: "If you commanded them, they would surely go forth." Say: "Do not swear. Obedience is known (to be what is wanted). Indeed God is Aware of what you do."﴾

﴿They swore by God with the utmost of their oaths, "If you commanded them"﴾, i.e., to leave their homes, their wealth, and their families. ﴿"They would surely go forth"﴾, i.e., as holy warriors (mujahidin). The word (*jahda*) is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (*hal*). It may also be a verbal noun (*masdar*) of (*aqsamu*, "they swore"), derived from its meaning. It is a metaphorical usage from (*jahada nafsahu*, "he exerted himself"), when he reaches the limit of his capacity. That is, they strengthened and emphasized their oaths. ﴿Say: "Do not swear. Obedience is known"﴾, i.e., do not swear to that and insist in order to please us. The matter required of you is an obedience that is known, which the soul does not deny, since there is no hardship in it. So obey in what is right without oaths, as the believers obey. It has also been said that the meaning is: your obedience is (merely) known obedience, i.e., it is words without deeds, since your lying in your oaths has become known. As God, Exalted is He, said: ﴿They swear to you in order that you may be pleased with them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 96], and the verse, and He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿They have taken their oaths as a shield﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 16], and the verse. Lying is part of their nature, even in what they choose, as God, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Have you not seen those who practiced hypocrisy say to their brothers who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture: "If you are expelled, we will surely leave with you, and we will never obey anyone concerning you, and if you are fought, we will surely support you." And God testifies that they are liars﴾ [al-Hashr: 11]. ﴿"If they are expelled, they will not go out with them; and if they are fought, they will not support them; and if they support them, they will surely turn their backs; then they will not be helped"﴾ [al-Hashr: 12]. His words, Exalted is He, ﴿Indeed God is Aware of what you do﴾, i.e., of the deeds, apparent and hidden, among which are false oaths, and what you conceal of hypocrisy and deception of the believers, which are not hidden from One who knows the secret and what is more hidden.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 24, verse 54:

The discussion of His saying, exalted is He:

[54] ﴿Say: Obey Allah and obey the Messenger. But if you turn away, then upon him is only that with which he has been entrusted, and upon you is that with which you have been entrusted. And if you obey him, you will be guided. And upon the Messenger is only the clear conveyance.﴾

﴿Say: Obey Allah and obey the Messenger. But if you turn away﴾ means: if you turn away from obedience. ﴿Then upon him is only that with which he has been entrusted﴾ means: what he was charged with of conveying the message. So when he has conveyed it, he has been discharged from the responsibility of his charge.

﴿And upon you is that with which you have been entrusted﴾ means: what you have been commanded of obedience, of receiving [the message] with acceptance, submission, and acting in accordance with its requirements. ﴿And if you obey him, you will be guided﴾ means: because he calls you to the straight path. If you obey him, you have secured your share of coming out of misguidance into guidance. And if you do not do so and turn away, you have exposed your souls to the displeasure and punishment of Allah. ﴿And upon the Messenger is only the clear conveyance﴾ means: the clear delivery of the message by himself, or the one who makes clear what you have been commanded.

(p-4545) Since His saying, exalted is He, ﴿you will be guided﴾ contained an allusion to a noble promise and a magnificent future, He resumed to state it explicitly, confirming it, with His saying, glorified is He:

The commentary on the Almighty's saying:

[55] ﴿Allah has promised those among you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely make them successors in the land, just as He made successors of those before them, and that He will surely establish for them their religion which He has approved for them, and that He will surely replace their fear with security. They worship Me, not associating anything with Me. And whoever disbelieves after that, those are the defiantly disobedient.﴾

﴿Allah has promised those among you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely make them successors in the land﴾ That is, He will make them inheritors of the land and place them in it as successors (khulafa'), exercising authority over it the way kings exercise authority over their realms. Or, [it means] successors of those who were not in their state of faith and righteous deeds. ﴿just as He made successors of those before them﴾ That is, of the believing nations who had [followed] their messengers, whose enemy Allah destroyed, and He gave them their land and their homes, as He did with the Children of Israel when He made them inheritors of Palestine after the destruction of the tyrants. ﴿and that He will surely establish for them their religion which He has approved for them﴾ That is, He will surely make their religion firmly established and secure, its banner raised, dominant over every other, and victorious over whoever opposes it.

Abu al-Su'ud said: The attribution of the religion to them, and it is the religion of Islam, then describing it as that which He has approved for them, is a means of winning their hearts, an increase in encouragement toward it, and a grace of steadfastness upon it. ﴿and that He will surely replace their fear with security. They worship Me, not associating anything with Me. And whoever disbelieves after that﴾ That is, after this noble promise which necessitates the attainment of what it includes of the two felicities. ﴿those are the defiantly disobedient﴾ That is, the complete in their defiance, in that they disbelieved this great blessing and dared to disregard it.

(p-4546) Note: In this verse there is clear evidence for the truth of prophethood, through the foretelling of the unseen as it was before it occurred. Allah fulfilled His promise, granting them victory over the Arabian Peninsula, and afterward they conquered the lands of the East and the West, tore apart the kingdom of the Persian emperors (al-Akasira), possessed their treasuries, seized control of the world, and came to a state where everyone other than them feared them.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying (Exalted is He):

[56–57] "And establish prayer and give zakah and obey the Messenger that you may receive mercy. Do not think that those who disbelieve will cause failure [to Allah] in the land, while their refuge is the Fire, and wretched is the destination." (Surah al-Nur: 56–57)

"And establish prayer and give zakah" is coordinated (ma'tuf) upon "obey Allah," and what came between them is an emphasis (ta'kid), or it is coordinated upon an implied element required by the context (al-siyaq). That is: "So believe, do righteous deeds, and establish [prayer]," or "So do not disbelieve, and establish [prayer]," etc. Then He repeated the obedience to the Messenger, as an emphasis on its obligation, with His saying: "And obey the Messenger that you may receive mercy." "Do not think that those who disbelieve [can] cause failure [to Allah] in the land" [al-Nur: 57], meaning: those who cannot escape Allah Exalted, but rather they will be overtaken: "And their refuge is the Fire, and wretched is the destination" [al-Nur: 57].

Then, following the preparation for what must be carried out of the rulings, and of encouragement and warning, He points to the completion of the earlier rulings, with His saying:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying (Exalted is He):

[56–57] "And establish prayer and give zakah and obey the Messenger that you may receive mercy. Do not think that those who disbelieve will cause failure [to Allah] in the land, while their refuge is the Fire, and wretched is the destination." (Surah al-Nur: 56–57)

"And establish prayer and give zakah" is coordinated (ma'tuf) upon "obey Allah," and what came between them is an emphasis (ta'kid), or it is coordinated upon an implied element required by the context (al-siyaq). That is: "So believe, do righteous deeds, and establish [prayer]," or "So do not disbelieve, and establish [prayer]," etc. Then He repeated the obedience to the Messenger, as an emphasis on its obligation, with His saying: "And obey the Messenger that you may receive mercy." "Do not think that those who disbelieve [can] cause failure [to Allah] in the land" [al-Nur: 57], meaning: those who cannot escape Allah Exalted, but rather they will be overtaken: "And their refuge is the Fire, and wretched is the destination" [al-Nur: 57].

Then, following the preparation for what must be carried out of the rulings, and of encouragement and warning, He points to the completion of the earlier rulings, with His saying:

The discussion of the Almighty's words:

[58] ﴿O you who have believed, let those whom your right hands possess and those among you who have not reached puberty ask permission of you at three times: before the prayer of dawn, and when you put aside your clothing at midday, and after the prayer of night. These are three times of privacy for you. There is no blame upon you or upon them beyond these, as they go about attending to you, some of you to others. Thus does Allah make clear to you the verses, and Allah is Knowing and Wise.﴾

﴿O you who have believed, let those whom your right hands possess﴾, i.e., of the male and female slaves, ﴿and those among you who have not reached puberty ask permission of you at three times: before the prayer of dawn, and when you put aside your clothing at midday, and after the prayer of night﴾: ﴿These are three times of privacy for you﴾, i.e., they are three times of privacy (ʿawrāt) for you. This points to the reason why seeking permission is obligatory: these are times when concealment is ordinarily disrupted, and sleep is generally with one's family. Intruding upon the people of the house in these circumstances is something the souls shrink from and detest most strongly. ﴿There is no blame upon you or upon them beyond these, as they go about attending to you﴾, i.e., there is no blame upon you in leaving off forbidding them from entering without permission, nor upon them in entering without it after these times, even though there may be some disruption of concealment in them, owing to its rarity. That is because they go about attending to you, so it is difficult for them to seek permission every time. ﴿some of you to others﴾, i.e., some of you going about to others in much movement; or some of you go about to others.

Al-Zamakhshari said: That is, you and they have a need for mixing and close contact: they go about to you for service, and you go about to them for employment. So if the command to seek permission were made absolute at every time, it would lead to hardship. ﴿Thus does Allah make clear to you the verses, and Allah is Knowing and Wise﴾, He legislates what contains wisdom, the welfare of affairs, and the orderliness of matters.

Note:

In the verse is the affirmation of what custom has established, that the time of sleep is after the night prayer, before dawn, and at midday. It may be cited as evidence that uncovering the ʿawrah in privacy is permissible. Thus (in al-Iklil).

Al-Razi said: The verse indicates that it is obligatory to consider the causes (ʿilal) of rulings where possible, for Allah, exalted is He, drew attention to the cause in these three times in two ways: first, by His saying ﴿three times of privacy for you﴾; and second, by pointing out the distinction between these three times and others, since that distinction is only due to the cause of exposure occurring in these three times, and it cannot be assured that exposure will not occur in them, whereas this is not the case with times other than these.

The commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 24, verse 59:

The exposition of His words, may He be exalted:

[59] ﴿And when the children among you reach puberty, let them ask permission, as those before them asked permission. Thus does Allah make clear to you His verses, and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.﴾

﴿And when the children reach﴾ i.e., those who were granted the concession (rukhsah) of not seeking permission at the times mentioned. ﴿Among you﴾ i.e., among the free, not the slaves, for they remain under the concession. ﴿Puberty (al-hulum)﴾ i.e., the limit of puberty (bulugh) by wet dream (al-ihtilam, nocturnal emission), and by the age that is the likely time of ihtilam. ﴿Let them ask permission﴾ i.e., at all other times too. ﴿As those before them asked permission﴾ i.e., those who had reached puberty before them, and they are the men, or those mentioned before them in His words: ﴿O you who have believed, do not enter houses other than your houses until you have asked permission and greeted their occupants﴾ [al-Nur: 27].

The meaning is that children are permitted to enter without permission, except at the three times of nakedness ('awrat). When children become accustomed to this, and then pass the limit of childhood, by having a wet dream or reaching the age at which they are judged to have attained puberty, they must be weaned from that habit and be required to ask permission at all times, just as the adult men who were not accustomed to entering upon you except with permission do.

This is something people are heedless of, and it is for them like an abrogated law (shari'ah mansukhah, naskh). It is related from Ibn 'Abbas: "A verse that most people do not believe in: the verse of permission." And I order my neighbour to ask permission to enter upon me.

(p-4549) He was asked by 'Ata': "Shall I ask permission to enter upon my sister?" He said: "Yes, even if she is under your care and you support her." And he recited this verse.

Also from him: "Three verses people have denied: all of the permission, and His words: ﴿Indeed the most honoured of you with Allah is the most righteous of you﴾ [al-Hujurat: 13], for some people said: 'The most honoured is the one with the largest house'; and His words: ﴿And when relatives and orphans and the needy are present at the division﴾ [al-Nisa': 8]." Thus in (al-Kashshaf).

Note:

Al-Iklil said: The verse indicates that legal responsibility (taklif) comes only with puberty, that puberty is attained by ihtilam, and that adult children do not enter upon their parents except with permission, like strangers. End of quotation.

Al-Taqi al-Subki said in (Ibraz al-Hikam fi Sharh Hadith Raf' al-Qalam): The scholars agreed that ihtilam brings about puberty for a man. This is shown by the words of Allah, may He be exalted: ﴿And when the children among you reach puberty, let them ask permission﴾, and by the words of the Prophet (ﷺ) in this hadith: "…and from the child until he has a wet dream." This is the narration of Ibn Abi al-Sarh from Ibn 'Abbas. He said: "And the verse is more explicit, for it speaks of the command after ihtilam." It is also reported from 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), raised to the Prophet (ﷺ): "There is no orphanhood after ihtilam, and no silence from dusk to dawn." Narrated by Abu Dawud. The meaning of ihtilam is the emission of semen, whether while awake or asleep, with a dream or without a dream. Since it usually occurs only in sleep with a dream, the term hulm and ihtilam was applied to it. If ihtilam occurs without emission of semen, then there is no hulm for him.

Then he said: His words in the hadith, "until he has a wet dream," are evidence that puberty is attained by this, and it is a consensus. It is (p-4550) literal for the emission of semen by ihtilam, and figurative for its emission without ihtilam, whether awake or asleep; or it is a term transferred to what is more general than that, and ihtilam without emission of semen is excluded from it, if we apply it to it as a transferred term, because it is one instance of ihtilam. End of quotation.

In (al-Qamus): al-hulum (with a damma) and al-ihtilam: intercourse in sleep. The noun is al-hulum like 'unuq. End of quotation.

Al-Raghib said: Puberty was called hulm because its possessor is worthy of hilm, that is, forbearance (al-anah) and intellect.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[60] ﴿And as for women past child-bearing who have no hope of marriage, there is no blame upon them for laying aside their outer garments, without displaying adornment. But to refrain is better for them. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing.﴾

﴿And as for women past child-bearing﴾ i.e., those who have ceased from menstruation and childbearing because of their old age. ﴿who have no hope of marriage﴾ i.e., who do not aspire to it, due to people's disinclination toward them. ﴿there is no blame upon them for laying aside their garments﴾ i.e., the outer garments which do not uncover the nakedness (ʿawrah) before strangers (al-ajanib). That is, they may relax their guard in covering themselves with them, so they do not cast their jilbabs over themselves nor veil themselves. ﴿without displaying adornment﴾ i.e., without showing hidden adornment, meaning jewelry in the places mentioned in His words: ﴿and not reveal their adornment except to their husbands﴾ [al-Nur: 31]. Or the meaning is: without intending by the laying aside to display themselves (tabarruj). However, lightening it is permitted when they would otherwise be veiled. ﴿But to refrain﴾ i.e., from laying aside those garments ﴿is better for them﴾ because it is more effective in modesty (haya') and further from accusation and suspicion. Therefore it is incumbent upon them, when there is a suspicion, not to lay those garments aside, just as the same is required of a young woman. ﴿And Allah is (p-4551) Hearing and Knowing﴾ i.e., He hears their speech with strangers and knows their intentions in mixing and laying aside garments. In this there is a warning that is not hidden. And His words, Exalted is He:

The discourse on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[61] ﴿There is no blame upon the blind, nor upon the lame, nor upon the sick, nor upon yourselves that you eat from your houses, or the houses of your fathers, or the houses of your mothers, or the houses of your brothers, or the houses of your sisters, or the houses of your paternal uncles, or the houses of your paternal aunts, or the houses of your maternal uncles, or the houses of your maternal aunts, or from that whose keys you possess, or from the house of your friend. There is no blame upon you for eating together or separately. But when you enter houses, greet one another with a greeting from Allah, blessed and good. Thus does Allah make clear to you the verses, that you may understand.﴾.

﴿There is no blame upon the blind, nor upon the lame, nor upon the sick﴾ — that is, in staying behind from the military campaign, due to their weakness and incapacity. This verse is like the one in Surat al-Fath and like the verse of Bara'a: ﴿There is no blame upon the weak, nor upon the sick, nor upon those who find nothing to spend, when they are sincere to Allah and His Messenger﴾ [al-Tawbah: 91]. This is the view held by 'Ata' and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam. As for the claim that it does not fit with what precedes or what follows, it is refuted by the fact that the intention is that each of the two groups is free from blame. An example of this — as al-Zamakhshari said — is that a traveller asks you about breaking the fast during Ramadan, and a pilgrim in ihram asks about putting the shaving before the sacrifice. You say to him: There is no blame upon the traveller to break his fast, nor upon you, O pilgrim, to put the shaving before the sacrifice. Meaning: when the conjunction seems strange due to the distance of the common link at first glance, and the purpose is to explain the rulings of events that are close in occurrence, and the questions about them and the need for explanation arise because they are the subject of inquiry and giving legal opinions, then this brings them together and makes the conjunction fitting, even if they differ.

Al-Shihab said: With this the answer to the claim that it does not fit with what precedes or what follows becomes clear, because its fit with what follows is known in its aspect, and its fit with what precedes is not necessary if it is not conjoined to it. End.

It was also said: The believers used to take the weak and those with disabilities to the houses of their wives and children, and to the houses of their relatives and friends, where they would feed them from them. So doubt arose in the hearts of both the feeders and the fed about this, and they feared that blame would fall upon them in it. They disliked that it be eating without right, due to His saying: ﴿And do not consume your wealth among yourselves in falsehood﴾ [al-Baqarah: 188]. So it was said to them: There is no blame upon the weak, nor upon yourselves — meaning upon you, and upon those who are in a situation like yours among the believers — in that.

It was also said: These people used to avoid sitting with people and eating with them, because of what might lead to disgust on their part. Also, the blind man's hand may reach what his companion's eye has reached while he does not notice. The lame man spreads out in the gathering and takes more than his place, thus constricting his companion. And the sick man is not free of a state that causes disgust.

It was also said: They used to go out to military campaigns and leave the weak in their houses, handing them the keys and permitting them to eat from their houses. But they would feel scrupulous about it. So it was said: There is no blame upon these weak ones for what they were scrupulous about, nor upon you, to eat from these houses.

This is what they mentioned. The truthfulness of the verse according to all of that, and the negation of blame in all of it, is not hidden.

The negation of blame regarding the sick man's eating with others, according to these other aspects, does not necessitate that he share with his companion, who is healthy, in dipping his hand into his vessel of what medicine has forbidden and souls loathe. Rather, it means his presence with the healthy at a table and his being given a separate dish. How excellent is the custom of individual dishes, by which the souls of the sick and the healthy are content in gathering.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Nor upon yourselves that you eat from your houses﴾ — that is, the houses of your wives and dependents. He attributed them to them because the wife's house is like the husband's house. This is the view of al-Farra'.

Ibn Qutaybah said: He meant the houses of their children. He ascribed the houses of the children to the fathers, because the child is the earning of his father; his wealth is like his wealth. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the best thing a man eats is from his earnings, and his child is from his earnings."

He said: The evidence for this is that He, exalted is He, enumerated the relatives and did not mention the children, because if the cause of the dispensation is kinship, then the one closer to them is more deserving.

End.

Accordingly, it cannot be said that there is no blame in a person eating from his own house, so what is the benefit of mentioning it? The answer: the intended meaning of "yourselves" is those who hold its rank among dependents and children, as in His saying: ﴿And do not kill yourselves﴾ [al-Nisa': 29].

In al-Kashshaf: The benefit of inserting "yourselves" is that what is meant is: there is no blame upon the weak who are fed, nor upon those who go to the houses of relatives, or whoever is in a situation like theirs, namely friends.

It was also said that it is on its literal sense, and the intention is to show equality between him and his companions.

Al-Shihab said: This is good. It is not objected that in this case the eating from the houses of wives and children is not mentioned, because it is included in His saying: ﴿from your houses﴾. End.

﴿or the houses of your fathers, or the houses of your mothers, or the houses of your brothers, or the houses of your sisters, or the houses of your paternal uncles, or the houses of your paternal aunts, or the houses of your maternal uncles, or the houses of your maternal aunts, or from that whose keys you possess﴾ — meaning a person's property, when he has over it a manager and agent who guards it for him, that he may eat from the fruit of his orchard and drink from the milk of his livestock. Possessing the key means its being in his hand and under his custody. ﴿or the friend of you﴾ — that is, or the houses of your friends. The word "friend" is used for both singular and plural. Likewise "khalil," "qatin," and "'aduw." Thus in al-Kashshaf.

Al-Nasir said: Al-Zamakhshari said that the secret of the singular form in His saying: ﴿So we have no intercessors﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 100] ﴿nor a close friend﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 101], rather than the plural "intercessors," is an indication of the scarcity of friends, whereas intercessors are not so, for a person may be protected and have intercession made on his behalf by one who does not know him, let alone be a friend.

It is possible in the two verses that the intended meaning is the plural, and then there is no issue. It is also possible that the singular is intended, and then its secret is that. And Allah knows best.

Al-Zamakhshari said: It is related of al-Hasan that he entered his house and found a circle of his friends who had pulled out baskets from under his bed, containing sweet dishes and choice foods, and they were bent over them eating. His face lit up with joy, and he laughed and said: "Thus we found them, thus we found them." He meant the senior Companions and those of them who met the people of Badr, may Allah be pleased with them.

A man among them would enter the house of his friend while he was absent, ask his slave-girl for his purse, and take from it what he wished. When her master arrived and she informed him, he would free her out of joy at that.

From Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq, may Allah be pleased with them both: from the greatness of the sanctity of a friend is that Allah made him, in intimacy, trust, ease, and dropping formality, of the rank of the self, the father, the brother, and the son.

From Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: the friend is greater than the parents. When the people of Hell cried out for help, they did not seek help from fathers and mothers, but said: ﴿So we have no intercessors﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 100] ﴿nor a close friend﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 101].

They also said: When the apparent state indicates the owner's consent, that stands in place of explicit permission, and sometimes asking permission becomes awkward and burdensome, like one who is served food and asks his companion's permission to eat from it. End.

(p-4555) ﴿There is no blame upon you for eating together or separately﴾ — that is, gathered or dispersed. It is narrated that some of the Ansar, when a guest came to them, would not eat except with their guest. And some people had been scrupulous about eating together, due to people differing in eating and some eating more than others. So this was permitted for them.

Qatada said: This tribe of Banu Kinana would consider it a disgrace upon one of them to eat alone in the pre-Islamic era, to the extent that a man would drive his camels to the field while hungry until he found someone to eat and drink with him. This was famously attributed to Hatim, due to his saying:

"When you prepare the provision, seek for it a companion to eat with, for I do not eat it alone."

Al-Shihab said: In a hadith: "The worst of people is one who eats alone, beats his servant, and withholds his gift." The prohibition in the hadith is for habitually being stingy with hospitality, and the negation of blame for doing it at times clarifies that there is no sin in it and it is not legally blamed, as the pre-Islamic period was blamed for it.

﴿So when you enter houses, greet one another﴾ — that is, when you enter one of these houses to eat, begin with greeting its people who are of you, by kinship and religion. Said by al-Zamakhshari.

He, may Allah have mercy on him, indicated that the intended meaning of "yourselves" is those who hold its rank, due to the strength of connection, as in His saying: ﴿And do not kill yourselves﴾ [al-Nisa': 29]. It is also possible that when a Muslim's greeting is returned to him, it is as if he greeted himself, just as the killer, for deserving execution by his deed, is as if he killed himself. As for keeping it on its literal sense — when no one is in the house, so that he would be pleased to say: "Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah," as narrated from Ibn 'Abbas — this is far-fetched and not fitting to the generality of the verse. Thus in al-Shihab.

(p-4556) Al-Nasir said: In expressing them as "yourselves," there is an indication of the secret that required permitting eating from these enumerated houses, and that this was because they are, relative to the entrant, like his own house, due to the unity of kinship. So let him be at ease in them with openness: ﴿a greeting from Allah﴾ — that is, established by command, legislated from Him. ﴿Blessed﴾ — that is, entailing increase of good and reward and its continuance. ﴿Good﴾ — that is, by which the soul of the hearer is content. ﴿Thus does Allah make clear to you the verses, that you may understand﴾ — that is, the rulings or etiquettes in them that lead to the happiness of both abodes.

When the Exalted commanded seeking permission upon entering, He guided to seeking permission upon departing from his gathering, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, by His saying, glorified is He:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[62] ﴿The believers are only those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger, and when they are with him on a matter of common concern, they do not depart until they have asked his permission. Indeed, those who ask your permission are those who believe in Allah and His Messenger. So when they ask your permission for some of their affairs, give permission to whom you will among them, and ask Allah's forgiveness for them. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾.

﴿The believers are only those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger, and when they are with him on a matter of common concern, they do not depart until they have asked his permission. Indeed, those who ask your permission are those who believe in Allah and His Messenger. So when they ask your permission for some of their affairs, give permission to whom you will among them, and ask Allah's forgiveness for them. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Al-Zamakhshari said: Almighty and Majestic is He intended to show them the magnitude of the offence of one who departs from the gathering of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) without his permission. So He made their not departing until they ask his permission the third element of faith in Allah and faith in His Messenger. He made these two like the prelude (tashbib) to it and the carpet (bisat) for its mention. This is along with the opening of the sentence with "innama" (indeed/only) and the placing of "the believers" as the subject (mubtada') described by a relative clause (mawsul), whose relative clause encompasses the mention of the two kinds of faith. Then He followed it with what increases it in emphasis and intensity, in that He repeated it in another style, which is His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who ask your permission are those who believe in Allah and His Messenger﴾, and He included in it something else: that He made asking permission like the proof (misdaq) of the soundness of the two kinds of faith, and He alluded to the condition of the believers who slip away furtively (liwadha). The meaning of His saying: ﴿they do not depart until they have asked his permission﴾ is: they do not depart until they ask his permission and he grants them leave. Do you not see how He made the matter, after their asking permission, dependent on his will and his permission for those whom they wished he would permit?

"Al-amr al-jami'" (a matter of common concern): that which people are gathered for. The matter is described as "gathering" (jam') by way of metaphor (majaz), such as fighting an enemy, or consulting on an important affair, or uniting to deter an opponent, or mutual tolerance in an alliance, and other such things. Or it is the matter that affects all by its harm or benefit. It was also read as "amrin jamii'" (a matter that is complete/all-encompassing). In His saying: ﴿and when they are with him on a matter of common concern﴾ there is an indication that it is a grave affair, in which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) must have men of judgement and strength who support him and assist him, and from whose opinions, knowledge and experience he seeks light for his sufficiency. So the departure of one of them in such a situation is something that burdens his heart and disturbs his judgement. Therefore He was stern with them and made the matter strict for them regarding asking permission, despite the clear excuse and the pressing need for it and the arising of what concerns them and matters to them. This is His saying: ﴿for some of their affairs﴾. And the mention of seeking forgiveness for those who ask permission is evidence that the better and more excellent course is that they should not entertain in themselves the thought of departing, nor ask permission for it.

It was said: it was revealed concerning the digging of the trench. Some people were slipping away without permission. They said: thus it should be for people with their leaders and their foremost in religion and knowledge, supporting them and not forsaking them in any calamity, and not separating from them. The matter of granting permission is delegated to the Imam: if he wills, he grants permission, and if he wills, he does not grant permission, according to what his judgement requires.

Note:

The verse has been cited as evidence that some rulings are delegated to the judgement of the Prophet (ﷺ). This question is called the question of delegation (tafwid), and it is expounded in the books of legal theory (usul). And His saying, exalted is He:

(p-4558) Discourse on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[63] ﴿Do not make the summoning of the Messenger among yourselves like your summoning of one another. Allah already knows those of you who slip away, sheltering behind one another. So let those who oppose his command beware lest a trial afflict them or a painful punishment strike them.﴾

﴿Do not make the summoning of the Messenger among yourselves like your summoning of one another﴾ That is: when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ needs your gathering before him for a matter and calls you, do not separate from him except with his permission. And do not liken his summoning you to the summoning of one another. Your departure from the assembly without the permission of the one summoning is what al-Zamakhshari said.

Likewise Ibn al-Athir said in (al-Mathal al-Sa'ir): That is, when you are present in his gathering, your presence should not be like your presence in your own gatherings. That is, do not leave his gathering except with his permission, and keep to good manners with him.

Some people held that the meaning of "summoning" (du'a') is "command" (amr). Among them is Ibn Abi al-Hadid, who said in (al-Falak al-Da'ir): The meaning previously stated, although a preceding indication supports it, as Ibn al-Athir said, the verse contains another, later indication that requires carrying it to a different sense, and this is likely the more correct: that "summoning" means "command." It is said: "So-and-so summoned his people to such-and-such," meaning he commanded them to it and urged them toward it. And He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿O you who believe, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life﴾ [al-Anfal: 24], meaning, urges you. And He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And indeed, every time I have called them, that You may forgive them﴾ [Nuh: 7], meaning, I commanded them and urged them. The later indication is His saying: ﴿So let those who oppose his command beware﴾. End of quotation. Likewise al-Mahayimi said: That is, do not make his command among you like your commands among yourselves, which are sometimes obeyed and sometimes not, because his command is obligatory to obey and does not lapse by slipping away from the summoned as a whole.

﴿Allah already knows those of you who slip away, sheltering behind one another﴾ That is, they withdraw little by little. And (liwadhan) means "sheltering behind one another," namely, one takes cover behind another and another behind him. That is, they slip away from the congregation secretly, in the manner of concealing themselves behind one another. And (liwadhan) is a circumstantial accusative: that is, "sheltering behind one another."

(p-4559) Moreover, it has been said that the meaning of the verse is: do not make calling him and naming him like the calling of one of you to another by his name, raising the voice with it, and calling from behind the chambers; rather, use his honorific title, such as: "O Prophet of Allah!" and "O Messenger of Allah!", with reverence, humility, and lowered voice.

This view is considered weak because it does not fit the context and the sequence. Some have strained to connect it with what precedes, by saying that seeking permission is done by their saying: "O Messenger of Allah! We seek your permission," and because whoever is with him in a common matter addresses him and calls him. The first view is more evident and preferable, as in (al-'Inayah).

Indeed, in the Revelation there are several verses requiring that one address him, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, with good manners and speak to him with reverence, which He made a requirement and consequence of faith, such as the verse: ﴿O you who believe, do not say "Ra'ina"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 104], and the verse: ﴿O you who believe, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet, nor speak loudly to him as you speak loudly to one another, lest your deeds be nullified while you are unaware﴾ [al-Hujurat: 2], up to His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who call you from behind the chambers, most of them do not reason﴾ [al-Hujurat: 4].

﴿So let those who oppose his command beware﴾ That is, they turn away from it and do not carry it out. The word (yukhalifuna) is used here to imply the meaning of turning away and avoiding, or "turning away from his connection." It was also said: when (khalafa) is followed by (ʿan), it implies departure. The root meaning of opposition (mukhalafah) is that each one takes a path different from the other's in his state or action, as al-Raghib said. ﴿lest a trial afflict them﴾ That is, a tribulation in this world. ﴿or a painful punishment strike them﴾ That is, in the Hereafter, or in both.

Note:

This verse has been cited as evidence that affairs must be weighed by the measure of His Sharia, Sunnah, and the principles of His religion. Whatever agrees with them is accepted, and whatever contradicts them is rejected upon the one who said it or did it, whoever he may be, as is established in the two Sahihs from him, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him: "Whoever does a deed that is not in accordance with our command, it is rejected."

The verse has also been cited as evidence that the command is for obligation, for it indicates that abandoning what the command requires entails one of the two punishments. It has been said: this is valid only if "command" (amr) means a request (talab), not "affair" (sha'n), as in His saying: ﴿on a matter of common concern﴾ [al-Nur: 62]. Both meanings have been allowed in it together. The detailed discussion is in (al-Razi).

The discussion on the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, exalted be He:

[64] ﴿Unquestionably, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. He already knows your condition. And the Day they are returned to Him, He will inform them of what they did. And Allah is Knowing of all things.﴾.

﴿Unquestionably, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. He already knows your condition﴾: that is, the accountable (mukallafun, those obligated to follow the law) in their opposition and agreement, and in their hypocrisy and sincerity. He emphasized His knowledge with (qad, "already") to reinforce the warning (wa'id). ﴿And the Day they are returned to Him, He will inform them of what they did. And Allah is Knowing of all things﴾: that is, nothing hidden is concealed from Him, because all of it is His creation and His possession, so His knowledge necessarily encompasses it. ﴿Does He not know, He who created? And He is the Subtle, the Acquainted﴾ [al-Mulk: 14].
